title: A Matheuristic for the Electric Vehicle Routing Problem with Partial Recharging and Time Windows
abstract: Electric freight vehicles must recharge before their battery is depleted; partial recharging—stopping before full charge—can reduce route duration significantly. This paper models the electric vehicle routing problem with partial recharging and time windows (EVRPTW-PR) as a mixed-integer second-order cone programme and solves it with a matheuristic that alternates between a large neighbourhood search (LNS) phase and an exact re-optimisation of recharging decisions via a compact MIP. The LNS uses destroy operators—random removal, worst-cost removal, and time-window-cluster removal—followed by a greedy insertion repair. Charger locations are given; recharging rate is modelled as constant. Tested on 60 instances derived from the Schneider benchmark with added partial-recharging parameters, the matheuristic produces solutions within 4.1% of best-known values in under five minutes per instance. Energy consumption is modelled as linearly proportional to distance and load, with separate coefficients calibrated from manufacturer data for two representative electric van categories.
venue: European Journal of Operational Research

title: Topological complexity measures for time series from dynamical systems: a comparative study
abstract: We compare four topological complexity measures—persistent entropy, the number of bars with persistence above a threshold, the total persistence (sum of bar lengths), and the bottleneck amplitude—applied to time series from six dynamical systems: the Lorenz attractor, the Rössler system, logistic map at varying r, the Duffing oscillator, white noise, and periodic sine waves. Each system is sampled at 2 000 time steps; delay-coordinate embedding with parameters estimated via average mutual information is applied before TDA. Persistent entropy best separates chaotic from periodic regimes (AUROC 0.94) and is most robust to measurement noise up to σ = 0.10. The Lorenz and Rössler attractors are reliably distinguished by H_2 bar count (mean difference 3.8, p < 0.001 by permutation test). We also show that topological measures and the largest Lyapunov exponent are correlated (Spearman ρ = 0.82) but not interchangeable, carrying complementary information.

title: Prescriptive Grammars and Editorial Practice: Evidence from Serbian Publishing Houses, 1991–2005
abstract: Using a corpus of 320 books published by six Serbian publishing houses between 1991 and 2005, this study tracks which orthographic manual editors de facto followed when resolving disputed spellings of compound words and foreign proper nouns. Each house was contacted for a structured interview, and copy-edited manuscripts from three cooperating publishers were examined directly. The results show that Belgrade-based publishers overwhelmingly adhered to the 1993 Belgrade manual even when the Novi Sad solution was formally adopted by the Serbian Ministry of Education, while Novi Sad publishers showed greater internal inconsistency. A regression analysis of 1,847 disputed tokens indicates that publisher location, founding date, and the educational background of the chief copy-editor are the strongest predictors of norm choice. The study provides empirical grounding for debates about the gap between prescriptive codification and actual editorial behaviour.

title: Cross-Lingual Transfer of Argument Mining Models Between Serbian and Croatian
abstract: We investigate how well argument mining classifiers trained on Serbian data transfer to Croatian and vice versa, exploiting the high lexical and grammatical similarity between the two languages. The experiment uses two balanced corpora of 800 essays each, annotated for argumentative components under the same annotation scheme. We compare three transfer strategies: direct application of the source-language model, vocabulary mapping with shared subword tokenization, and continued pre-training on a small target-language annotated set of 100 essays. Results show that direct transfer yields an average F1 of 0.63 for the four-class scheme, vocabulary mapping raises this to 0.67, and continued pre-training with 100 examples reaches 0.74, approaching the fully supervised in-language baseline of 0.79. The findings suggest that low-resource argument mining for South Slavic varieties can benefit substantially from cross-lingual data sharing without full retraining.

title: Strategic noise mapping for Novi Sad: application of the END directive methodology to a mid-sized Pannonian city
abstract: The European Environmental Noise Directive requires agglomerations above 100 000 inhabitants to produce strategic noise maps at five-year intervals. This paper describes the production of the first research-grade strategic noise map for Novi Sad using SoundPlan 7.4, a digital terrain model at 1 m resolution, and hourly traffic volumes disaggregated by vehicle class for the morning, afternoon, and night periods. Road centreline geometry was derived from a municipal GIS database and supplemented with building footprint data. The resulting Lden map shows that approximately 38 000 residents are exposed to levels above 65 dB(A) Lden, with the highest values concentrated along the Futoška and Bulevar Oslobođenja corridors. Uncertainty was estimated through a Monte Carlo propagation of input variability, yielding a 95% confidence interval of ±1.8 dB(A) for grid cells adjacent to the road. The maps were made available to the city planning authority.
venue: Transport and Environment Review

title: Macroscopic Traffic Simulation Models for Corridor Planning: Calibration Principles and Practice
abstract: This book chapter provides a practitioner-oriented account of calibration workflows for LWR and cell-transmission models applied to inter-urban corridor planning. It covers data requirements, including minimum counting station density (recommended: one station per 8–12 km for rural motorways), acceptable loop detector fault rates, and floating car sample-size rules of thumb. The chapter reviews objective functions used in calibration—GEH, RMSPE, and mean absolute error—and discusses their respective sensitivities to peak and off-peak conditions. Two worked examples using anonymised Vojvodina corridor datasets illustrate iterative parameter adjustment. Common failure modes—including overfitting to a single day's data and neglecting the effect of incident-induced capacity drops—are discussed with reference to published validation studies. The chapter is aimed at transport engineers in regional planning agencies who use commercial packages but need to understand the underlying model behaviour.

title: Cyber Insurance Pricing for SMEs Using Credibility Theory: Evidence from Vojvodina
abstract: This paper applies Bühlmann–Straub credibility theory to cyber insurance pricing for small and medium enterprises, using a dataset of 127 SMEs in the Vojvodina region that participated in a voluntary risk disclosure programme between 2019 and 2022. Each firm reports annual cyber incident counts and aggregate losses; the dataset yields 381 firm–year observations. Credibility weights are computed per firm size class (micro, small, medium) and per industry sector. The resulting credibility-weighted frequency and severity parameters are compared to class-mean priors; the average credibility weight across firms is 0.41, reflecting the limited length of individual histories. Simulated insurance premiums based on the credibility model differ from those based on class-mean parameters by up to 23% for individual firms. The paper discusses how technology parks and business incubators could facilitate the data pooling arrangements needed to expand such credibility datasets.

title: Retail Sukuk for Infrastructure Financing in Serbia: Fiscal, Legal, and Structural Feasibility
abstract: This working paper assesses the feasibility of the Republic of Serbia issuing retail sukuk to finance infrastructure projects, drawing on the precedents of the UK's Al-Rayan sukuk programme and Indonesia's retail sovereign sukuk series. The analysis covers three dimensions: fiscal (whether sukuk issuance costs are competitive with conventional bond issuance given Serbia's current sovereign rating of BB+ and prevailing yields), legal (the amendments to the Law on Public Debt and Law on Securities required to enable asset-lease sukuk), and structural (the selection of state-owned assets suitable for the underlying lease arrangement without triggering constitutional restrictions on disposal of public property). The paper estimates that a five-year, EUR 200 million ijara sukuk linked to transport infrastructure could be priced within 20–35 basis points of an equivalent eurobond, making it viable if the government values the diversification of the investor base. The paper was prepared as a policy background document for a faculty roundtable held in November 2025.

title: Delta-of-Delta Encoding for Monotonic Sensor Counters in Relational Column Stores
abstract: Monotonic counter sequences produced by industrial pulse sensors exhibit strong first-order and second-order differences that standard LZ-family compressors exploit poorly when applied at the row level. This paper evaluates a purely arithmetic delta-of-delta scheme applied within a columnar storage engine on sequences of 32-bit unsigned integers sampled at 1 kHz. Experiments use 14 days of vibration counter data from a water-treatment facility logging 48 sensor channels, yielding roughly 58 billion raw values. The scheme is compared against Snappy, LZ4, and a Gorilla-style float codec adapted for integers. Delta-of-delta achieves a compression ratio of 18.3:1 against raw binary, outperforming LZ4 (11.1:1) with 40 % lower decompression CPU time. Encoding throughput on a single core reaches 920 MB/s. The paper also derives a closed-form bound on the representable range for a fixed bit-width delta register and proposes a lightweight overflow-detection branch that adds under 2 % latency overhead.

title: Bitmap Index Compression Trade-offs for Low-Cardinality Attributes in Time-Series Tables
abstract: Bitmap indexes over low-cardinality categorical attributes are common in data-warehouse workloads, but their behaviour on append-only time-series tables with frequent partial scans has received less attention. We compare uncompressed bitmaps, WAH (Word-Aligned Hybrid), CONCISE, and Roaring Bitmaps on synthetic and real sensor-classification workloads where cardinality ranges from 4 to 256 distinct values and table sizes range from 10 million to 2 billion rows. Real data come from a Serbian environmental monitoring network logging air-quality sensor states at 10-second intervals over 18 months across 31 stations. Roaring Bitmaps reduce index size by 55–72 % relative to WAH while maintaining AND/OR operation throughput within 8 % of uncompressed bitmaps for selective queries. We identify a crossover point at cardinality 64 above which WAH outperforms Roaring in sequential full-scan aggregation. Query plans that choose index type adaptively based on observed cardinality at load time reduce total query time by 23 % in the mixed workload benchmark.

title: Columnar Storage Layout for Mixed-Rate Sensor Streams: Alignment, Padding, and Scan Cost
abstract: Industrial sensor networks rarely emit all channels at a uniform rate. A pressure transducer may log at 100 Hz while a thermal sensor logs at 1 Hz, creating mixed-rate column groups within a single logical schema. Storing such streams in a uniform columnar layout either wastes space through padding or requires indirection structures that slow scans. This chapter surveys three physical layout strategies—uniform-stride padding, epoch-grouped variable-stride, and separate per-rate column families—and analyses their scan cost analytically and experimentally. Experiments use a 90-day dataset of 112 sensor channels from a pilot manufacturing line at 14 distinct sampling rates, totalling 430 GB uncompressed. Epoch-grouped variable-stride achieves the best compromise: 31 % less storage than uniform-stride padding with scan overhead under 6 % compared to single-rate baselines. Practical guidelines for schema designers are derived, including a heuristic for grouping channels into rate classes.

title: Efficient SUM and AVG Aggregation Over Compressed Integer Columns Without Full Decompression
abstract: Computing SUM and AVG over delta-compressed integer columns typically requires full decompression before the arithmetic pass. We present a method that accumulates partial sums directly over delta-coded blocks by exploiting the algebraic structure of prefix-sum reconstruction, reducing decompression to the final carry-propagation step. The technique is implemented inside a fork of an open-source columnar engine (DuckDB-compatible file format) and evaluated on six months of electricity sub-metering data at 1-second resolution across 200 household circuits, approximately 31 billion rows. End-to-end SUM throughput increases by 1.8× on a single core and 2.1× on four cores compared to decompress-then-aggregate. The method generalises to COUNT DISTINCT with HyperLogLog sketches embedded in compressed blocks, yielding a 1.4× speedup there. Memory bandwidth measurements confirm that savings come primarily from reduced cache pressure rather than reduced arithmetic.

title: Adaptive Bit-Packing Width Selection for High-Frequency Accelerometer Streams
abstract: Fixed-width bit-packing assigns the same bit-width to every value in a block, wasting bits when the dynamic range is temporarily narrow. We propose a lightweight adaptive scheme that re-estimates the required bit-width every 512 values using a running maximum register and encodes the width in a 6-bit block header. The scheme targets 16-bit signed accelerometer samples recorded at 4 kHz. A corpus of 22 hours of vibration data from rotating machinery in a Serbian food-processing plant (seven machine types, 63 sensors) is used for evaluation. Adaptive bit-packing reduces storage by 19–34 % relative to fixed 16-bit packing and by 9–17 % relative to fixed optimal-width packing computed offline. Decompression speed on SSE4.2 SIMD instructions remains within 4 % of fixed-width scalar decompression. We also report failure modes when the running maximum underestimates abrupt transients and propose a saturating-rollback mechanism.

title: Zone Maps vs. Min-Max Indexes in Columnar Engines: Behaviour Under Skewed Sensor Value Distributions
abstract: Zone maps (per-block min-max metadata) are a standard pruning mechanism in columnar databases, but their effectiveness degrades when value distributions within blocks are highly skewed or multi-modal, which is common in sensor streams that include fault and alarm states. We characterise the pruning rate of zone maps analytically as a function of block size and intra-block value variance and validate the model on four real sensor datasets: river-level gauges, photovoltaic panel voltage logs, industrial pressure manifolds, and HVAC temperature arrays. Block sizes of 512 to 65536 values are tested. For multi-modal distributions the pruning rate drops below 30 % even at block size 512. We evaluate two lightweight alternatives—quantile sketches and learned min-max predictors trained on preceding blocks—and find that a 7-quantile sketch stored in 28 bytes per block restores pruning rates to above 70 % at a metadata overhead of 0.03 % of raw data size. Implementation notes for integration into an open-source columnar engine are provided.

title: Compression-Aware Query Planning for Time-Bounded Window Aggregations
abstract: Time-bounded window aggregations (e.g., SUM over the last 15 minutes) on append-only sensor tables require accessing a suffix of one or more compressed blocks. The query planner must decide whether to decompress an entire boundary block or to seek within it, a choice that depends on block size, compression codec, and selectivity. We formalise this as a cost model parameterised by measured decompression throughput, seek latency, and block fill factor, and integrate it into a rule-based planner for a columnar storage engine. Evaluation uses six months of power-grid sensor data at 500 Hz from a regional substation, with window widths ranging from 1 second to 24 hours. The cost-model-guided planner reduces query latency by 28–41 % over a baseline that always decompresses full boundary blocks, and by 12–18 % over a simpler heuristic that always seeks. The model's calibration requires a 90-second profiling pass run once at database initialisation.

title: On-Disk Representation of Irregular-Timestamp Sensor Logs: Separating Time and Value Columns
abstract: Most time-series storage literature assumes uniform sampling intervals, so timestamp columns are stored implicitly as a start time plus stride. Environmental and IoT sensors with event-driven reporting produce irregular timestamps that must be stored explicitly. We study the compression and scan-performance implications of separating timestamp columns from value columns on disk versus interleaving them. Three physical layouts are compared on a 14-month dataset of soil-moisture readings from 180 field sensors distributed across Vojvodina, Serbia, with inter-arrival times varying from 30 seconds to 45 minutes. Separating columns allows timestamp and value codecs to be chosen independently; Gorilla-style XOR encoding for floating-point values combined with FOR (Frame of Reference) encoding for microsecond-resolution timestamps reduces combined storage by 26 % relative to interleaved LZ4. Random-access latency increases by 11 % due to two separate seeks, which is acceptable for analytical workloads but warrants consideration for point-lookup-heavy use cases.

title: Benchmarking In-Database Compression Codecs for Sub-Second Rollup Queries on a Single-Node Commodity Server
abstract: Sub-second rollup latency over billion-row sensor tables is achievable on a single commodity server if the codec, block size, and aggregation strategy are matched to the query workload. We construct a reproducible benchmark using publicly available hardware (AMD EPYC 7003, 128 GB DDR4, NVMe SSD) and four synthetic workloads derived from real sensor patterns: smooth analogue signals, step-change switching signals, random noise, and mixed. Eight codecs are tested: LZ4, Zstandard-3, Zstandard-9, Gorilla float, delta-varint, bit-packing, PFOR, and a cascade of delta followed by bit-packing. Rollup query latency, compression ratio, and encode/decode throughput are reported for block sizes of 256, 1024, and 4096 values. Delta+bit-packing on smooth signals achieves 0.38-second rollup over 2 billion rows with a 21:1 ratio. No single codec dominates across all workloads; a decision table mapping signal type to codec is provided. All benchmark code and datasets are released under an open licence.
venue: Proceedings of the European Workshop on Data Engineering Practices (EWDEP)

title: Predicting Compressibility of Sensor Blocks from Lightweight Signal Statistics
abstract: Choosing a compression codec at write time without compressing the data first requires a proxy metric that correlates with compression ratio. We evaluate seven lightweight statistics—range, variance, zero-crossing rate, run-length entropy estimate, lag-1 autocorrelation, approximate quantile spread, and bit-reversal entropy—as predictors of final compression ratio for LZ4, Zstandard, delta+PFOR, and Gorilla across a corpus of 4.1 million 1024-value blocks drawn from 11 sensor deployments spanning energy, agriculture, and manufacturing domains. Lag-1 autocorrelation alone achieves a Spearman rank correlation of 0.81 with the delta+PFOR ratio and can be computed in a single pass over a block in under 0.2 µs on the target hardware. A two-feature classifier (autocorrelation + range) correctly routes blocks to the best codec in 73 % of cases, reducing mean storage size by 14 % compared to a fixed-codec policy with no runtime overhead above 1.1 %.

title: Uticaj morfološke redukcije na preciznost pretrage srpskih višeskriptnih dokumenata
abstract: Srpski jezik je morfološki bogat, što znači da ista leksema može imati nekoliko desetina flektivnih oblika. U ovom radu ispitujemo kako stemovanje i lematizacija interaguju s postupkom normalizacije skripte pri izgradnji pretražnog indeksa. Koristimo tri stemera dostupna za srpski jezik — dva pravilo-zasnovana i jedan statistički — i kombinujemo ih s fonemskim kanonizacionim korakom opisanim u prethodnim radovima. Evaluacija je sprovedena na podskupu CLEF 2012 kolekcije koji sadrži dokumente u oba pisma. Rezultati pokazuju da redosled operacija (stemovanje pre ili posle normalizacije skripte) utiče na odziv, pri čemu stemovanje posle normalizacije daje konzistentno bolje rezultate za sve tri kombinacije (poboljšanje od 4 do 9 procentnih poena u MAP). Rad daje i analizu grešaka za 50 ručno pregledanih upita.

title: Fairness Metrics in Automated Roster Generation: A Survey and Comparative Study
abstract: Personnel scheduling systems that minimise cost or maximise coverage often produce rosters that are perceived as unfair by employees, leading to low adoption rates. This chapter surveys fairness criteria used in the scheduling literature, classifying them into four categories: load equity, preference satisfaction, distribution of undesirable shifts, and seniority-based entitlements. For each category, we describe representative mathematical formulations and discuss their computational implications. A comparative experiment on a common dataset of 12 nurse scheduling instances illustrates the trade-offs between cost-oriented and fairness-oriented objective functions. Results confirm that including fairness penalties increases objective function values by 8–31% relative to cost-only optima, but that most of this increase occurs at small fairness weight values, suggesting that modest fairness investments yield proportionally large equity gains. The chapter concludes with a discussion of participatory design methods for eliciting employee-specific fairness weights.

title: Statička krutost slobodno lebdećeg planarnog stola sa trajnim magnetima u konfiguraciji Halbachove rešetke
abstract: Rad analizira statičku krutost planarnog levitacionog stola koji koristi Halbachovu permanentno-magnetnu rešetku u sprezi sa ravnim zavojnicama. Izrađen je analitički model koji uzima u obzir harmonike magnetnog polja do petog reda, a verifikacija je sprovedena trodimenzionalnom simulacijom metodom konačnih elemenata u paketu Magneto-3D v4.2. Eksperimentalni uzorci od dva prototipa pokazali su da vertikalna krutost iznosi 18,4 N/mm uz standardnu devijaciju od 0,3 N/mm u opsegu levitacione visine 0,4–1,2 mm. Horizontalna krutost u oba planarnih smera bila je negativna (destabilizujuća), vrednosti oko −2,1 N/mm, što zahteva aktivnu povratnu spregu. Rezultati su primenjeni na dimenzionisanje pojačivača struje i određivanje zahteva za krutost nosača u litografskim fiksturama. Rad daje tabele krutosti u funkciji geometrijskih parametara rešetke koje mogu poslužiti kao projektni alat.

abstract: Рад истражује аргументациону структуру у текстовима из четири уџбеника за шести разред основне школе (историја, биологија, грађанско васпитање и српски језик) укупног обима 62.000 токена. Примењена је упрошћена верзија шеме за анотацију аргумената намењена нестручним анотаторима и ученицима старијег узраста. Три анотатора обрадила су исти узорак од 2.400 реченица; просечна капа износила је 0,61. Резултати показују да уџбеници природних наука садрже знатно мање експлицитних тврдњи и доказа него уџбеници друштвених наука. Такође, анализа је указала на честу употребу имплицитних налогâ у уџбеницима грађанског васпитања, где аутор претпоставља да ученик самостално изводи закључак. Налазе доводимо у везу са препорукама за наставу критичког мишљења на основношколском нивоу.

title: Correlated Anomaly Detection Across Microservice Traces and Infrastructure Logs Using Graph-Based Clustering
abstract: Modern applications generate interleaved traces from dozens of microservices alongside infrastructure logs from the underlying Kubernetes nodes. This paper proposes representing concurrent events as nodes in a time-attributed multigraph, where edges encode causal or temporal co-occurrence within a configurable window. Community detection via the Louvain algorithm is then applied to identify correlated anomaly clusters. Experiments are conducted on a synthetic microservice benchmark (8 services, 14 days, 4.3 billion events) with injected faults covering latency spikes, pod crashes, and network partitions. The graph-based approach achieves a macro-averaged F1 of 0.84 for fault-type classification, compared to 0.71 for an independent per-log isolation forest baseline. Memory consumption grows linearly with the number of active trace IDs, reaching 6.2 GB at peak load in the test environment. A pruning strategy based on trace-completion events reduces memory usage by 38%.

title: Unsupervised Detection of Lateral Movement in Enterprise Networks via Windows Event Log Correlation
abstract: Lateral movement by adversaries typically produces subtle, distributed signals across Windows Security Event Logs on multiple hosts. This study constructs user-host access graphs from Security Event IDs 4624, 4648, 4768, and 4769 collected over 30 days from a 600-host enterprise test environment, with synthetic lateral movement sequences injected following MITRE ATT&CK patterns. Node embeddings derived from a graph autoencoder are clustered with k-means; cluster membership deviation is used as an anomaly score. The method detects 19 of 24 injected lateral movement chains with a false-positive rate of 3.2 per day—substantially below the 11.7 per day produced by a signature-based SIEM rule set. A user-facing triage interface ranks suspicious chains by graph anomaly score. Limitations around encrypted Kerberos traffic and pass-the-hash variants that bypass standard logging are discussed.

title: Calibration of a Battery Cell Emulator for BMS ECU Validation on a Low-Cost HiL Platform
abstract: Battery management system (BMS) ECUs require accurate emulation of cell voltages, temperatures, and internal impedances during validation testing. This paper describes the design and calibration of a 12-cell emulator board built from precision voltage references, operational amplifier buffers, and a digitally programmable resistor network to model ohmic and diffusion impedances. The board interfaces to a Zynq-7020 SoC running the simulation host and updates cell parameters at 10 ms intervals via SPI. Calibration was performed against a reference Keithley source-measure unit across the 2.5–4.2 V operating range; voltage accuracy after calibration was ±2.1 mV at 25 °C and ±4.8 mV over the −20 °C to 60 °C range. A lithium iron phosphate cell model with 18 parameters was validated against 12 published drive-cycle datasets. A commercial BMS ECU was tested using 88 scripted test cases including cell balancing activation, state-of-charge estimation accuracy, and over-voltage protection response time. The total bill of materials for the emulator board was 280 EUR.

title: Efficient Approximate Nearest Neighbour Retrieval for Embedding-Based Recommenders: A Benchmark on Commodity Hardware
abstract: Two-stage recommenders use approximate nearest-neighbour (ANN) search to retrieve candidate items from a learned embedding space before a more expensive ranking model re-scores them. We benchmark five ANN index structures—HNSW, IVF-Flat, IVF-PQ, ScaNN, and a flat exact baseline—on three embedding spaces of different dimensionalities (64, 128, 256) and catalogue sizes (50K, 500K, 5M items) using recall@100 and query latency at fixed memory budgets on a single server with 64 GB RAM and no GPU. HNSW achieves the best recall–latency trade-off for catalogues up to 500K items; IVF-PQ becomes competitive at 5M items under 16 GB memory constraints. We also measure how ANN retrieval recall translates to end-to-end NDCG@10 degradation and find that recall@100 above 0.92 causes less than 1% NDCG loss relative to exact retrieval. A practical configuration guide is included.

title: Automated Adapter Generation from Mismatched Interface Specifications
abstract: When two systems must be integrated but their interface specifications describe incompatible message structures or interaction protocols, a protocol adapter is required. Manual adapter coding is error-prone and difficult to maintain. This paper presents a model-driven method in which both interfaces are described as finite-state machines annotated with typed message vocabularies; the mismatch is characterised as a set of transformation rules derived automatically by a constraint solver, and ATL templates then generate executable Apache Camel routes that implement the adapter. The method was applied to 22 real interface pairs collected from three companies in the manufacturing sector in Vojvodina. Fully automated generation succeeded in 16 cases; the remaining six required on average 2.3 hours of manual refinement. Generated adapters passed all supplied regression tests.
venue: Proceedings of the International Conference on Model-Driven Engineering and Software Systems (MODELS-SD)

title: Incremental Gaussian Mixture Models for Online Anomaly Detection in Continuous ICS Traffic Streams
abstract: This paper proposes an incremental variant of Gaussian mixture modelling (iGMM) for online anomaly detection in ICS traffic without the need for periodic full retraining. The algorithm maintains a fixed number of Gaussian components (K = 5 to 20 evaluated) and uses a Bayesian update rule to adjust component means, covariances, and weights with each arriving window of observations. Feature vectors are 32-dimensional, derived from 10-second traffic windows. The method was evaluated on a 180-day Modbus/TCP capture from a district heating control network and compared with a static GMM retrained every 24 hours. The iGMM maintained an F1 score within 0.03 of the periodically retrained model while reducing retraining compute cost by 94%. Concept drift induced by a planned process reconfiguration was detected as a persistent anomaly episode; a supervised reset mechanism based on operator acknowledgement was proposed and tested. Memory footprint per detector instance was under 120 KB.

title: Detecting Stealthy Coil-Write Injection in Modbus Networks Using Temporal Autoencoder Ensembles
abstract: Stealthy coil-write injection attacks modify a small number of PLC output coils at irregular intervals designed to evade detectors sensitive only to rate or volume changes. This paper evaluates temporal autoencoder ensembles—ten autoencoders trained on temporally shuffled subsets of a 60-day Modbus/TCP capture—for detecting such attacks. Each autoencoder receives a 30-dimensional feature vector derived from 5-second windows including coil change frequency, write-to-read ratio per coil address, and inter-write interval statistics. Anomaly scores from ensemble members are aggregated by the maximum rule. Against 240 injected stealthy attack episodes of varying intensity (1 to 8 modified coils per window), the ensemble achieved recall of 0.89 at a false positive rate of 0.8 per hour, compared with 0.64 for a single autoencoder and 0.58 for a static threshold detector. Computational cost of the ensemble was 2.3× that of a single autoencoder, remaining feasible on edge hardware.

title: Change Readiness as a Predictor of ERP Implementation Outcome in Serbian Manufacturing SMEs
abstract: This paper examines the relationship between pre-implementation change readiness scores and project outcome in a sample of 47 manufacturing SMEs in the Vojvodina region that adopted ERP systems between 2005 and 2009. Change readiness was operationalised through a 24-item questionnaire adapted from Armenakis's readiness model, administered to top and middle management six months prior to go-live. Implementation outcome was assessed using a composite index combining schedule adherence, budget deviation, and user satisfaction measured twelve months post-go-live. Ordinal logistic regression revealed that change readiness scores explained 31% of the variance in outcome, with the subscale capturing management commitment showing the strongest individual effect. Firms with readiness scores in the lowest quartile were 4.2 times more likely to report failed or severely delayed implementations. The findings suggest that readiness diagnostic tools should be embedded in vendor pre-sales processes rather than treated as optional consulting add-ons.

title: Seasonal NDVI trajectories from Landsat-8 for distinguishing winter wheat and sunflower parcels in the Vojvodina plain
abstract: This study examined the separability of winter wheat and sunflower cultivation units in the Vojvodina lowland using dense NDVI time series derived from Landsat-8 surface reflectance imagery acquired during the 2015 and 2016 growing seasons. A total of 412 reference parcels were digitised from cadastral data and verified by field survey. Temporal profiles were constructed at 16-day intervals and smoothed using a Savitzky–Golay filter before being fed into a random forest classifier. Overall classification accuracy reached 91.4% for winter wheat and 87.9% for sunflower across both years. The main source of confusion was between sunflower and maize in parcels smaller than 1.5 hectares, where mixed pixels reduced time-series coherence. Results suggest that the phenological window between day-of-year 160 and 220 provides the greatest discriminative power for separating these two summer crops. The dataset and code are made available through the BioSense Institute repository.

title: Effect of cloud gap-filling strategy on Sentinel-2 derived LAI estimates in humid continental climates
abstract: Frequent cloud cover in temperate agricultural regions causes substantial data gaps in optical satellite time series, potentially biasing derived biophysical variables such as leaf area index (LAI). This paper compares four gap-filling approaches—linear interpolation, Whittaker smoother, harmonic regression, and a radial basis function network—applied to Sentinel-2 MultiSpectral Instrument Level-2A imagery over a 180 000-hectare study area in northern Serbia. LAI was estimated using a lookup-table inversion of the PROSAIL radiative transfer model. Reference LAI measurements were collected at 38 field plots across three crop types during the 2018 season. The harmonic regression and Whittaker smoother produced the lowest root mean square errors against field data (0.41 and 0.44 m² m⁻² respectively), while linear interpolation performed worst in years with extended cloud sequences exceeding 25 consecutive days. The study recommends harmonic regression as the default for LAI products intended for yield modelling in the region.

title: Integrating ERA5-Land meteorological variables with satellite vegetation indices for in-season winter wheat yield forecasting at the field level
abstract: Accurate in-season yield forecasting at individual field level remains difficult because satellite observations alone do not capture agronomic stress caused by temperature extremes or moisture deficits. This paper presents a regression framework that combines seven Sentinel-2 derived spectral indices sampled at weekly intervals with ERA5-Land reanalysis variables including daily maximum temperature, precipitation sum, and reference evapotranspiration. Training data were compiled from 1 247 winter wheat parcels in the Srem district spanning the 2017–2020 growing seasons, with yield ground truth from cooperative combine-harvester records. A gradient boosting regressor outperformed a simple LAI-based benchmark, reducing mean absolute error from 0.71 t ha⁻¹ to 0.49 t ha⁻¹ when the model was applied to the 2021 holdout season. Feature importance analysis identified the red-edge chlorophyll index acquired between Zadoks stage 37 and 55 as the strongest single predictor. Spatial autocorrelation of residuals was moderate (Moran's I = 0.18), indicating that local soil variability not captured by weather reanalysis remains a limiting factor.

title: Parcel boundary delineation from Sentinel-2 imagery using a watershed segmentation approach adapted for fragmented agricultural landscapes
abstract: Automatic delineation of agricultural parcel boundaries is a prerequisite for scalable field-level monitoring but is complicated by the small, irregular parcel structure typical of post-socialist land fragmentation in the western Balkans. This conference paper describes an adaptation of marker-controlled watershed segmentation applied to a composite of three Sentinel-2 bands (B4, B8, B11) and a gradient magnitude image generated from a spring-season mosaic. Markers were seeded using local minima of the gradient after Gaussian smoothing at two spatial scales. Accuracy was evaluated against 630 manually digitised parcels in a 5 000-hectare test region in the South Bačka district. The method achieved an average boundary displacement error of 8.3 m and an over-segmentation rate of 14%, comparable to published results on larger, more regular field systems in Western Europe. The approach is computationally light and runs within Google Earth Engine without requiring additional training data.

title: A transferability assessment of yield prediction models trained in the Pannonian Plain when applied to Romanian agricultural regions
abstract: Machine learning models trained on local yield and satellite data often degrade when transferred to neighbouring regions with different climate regimes, soil types, and crop varieties. This study evaluates the transferability of three yield prediction models—random forest, support vector regression, and a convolutional recurrent network operating on image time series—trained on Serbian Pannonian Plain data and tested on 890 winter wheat parcels distributed across four counties in south-west Romania. Models were trained on 2017–2021 Serbian data and applied without retraining, with partial retraining on 20% of Romanian parcels, and with full retraining. Partial retraining using as few as 180 Romanian parcels recovered 78% of the performance attainable with full local training. The convolutional recurrent network showed the largest absolute performance drop under zero-shot transfer but also the greatest benefit from partial retraining. The study concludes that a small locally collected calibration dataset is sufficient for practical deployment across the Pannonian–Wallachian agroclimatic gradient.

title: Combining Sentinel-1 SAR coherence and Sentinel-2 optical indices for sunflower yield estimation under variable cloud cover
abstract: Optical satellite data for yield modelling become unreliable during cloudy periods that coincide with critical crop growth stages. This study investigates whether Sentinel-1 C-band SAR coherence, which is unaffected by cloud cover, can supplement or replace optical indices during such periods for sunflower yield estimation. A dataset of 534 sunflower parcels in the Banat region monitored from 2019 to 2022 was used. Repeat-pass interferometric coherence was computed from 6-day Sentinel-1 pairs on ascending and descending orbits. Coherence values between day-of-year 190 and 230 correlated negatively with canopy biomass (r = −0.61) and showed predictive value for final yield independent of optical data. A fusion model combining coherence time series with cloud-gapfilled NDVI achieved a mean absolute error of 0.44 t ha⁻¹, compared with 0.61 t ha⁻¹ for an optical-only baseline in years with high cloud frequency. The benefit of SAR fusion was largest in the 2021 season, which experienced 34 cloudy days during the critical growth window.

title: Temporal resolution requirements for Sentinel-2 based yield modelling: a sensitivity analysis across five crop types
abstract: The operational cadence of Sentinel-2 is five days at the equator but is reduced by cloud cover and orbital geometry at mid-latitudes. It remains unclear how large the resulting temporal gaps can be before yield prediction accuracy degrades significantly. This paper presents a systematic sensitivity analysis in which synthetic temporal gaps of 5, 10, 15, 20, and 30 days are introduced into complete Sentinel-2 time series for five crop types—winter wheat, maize, sunflower, soybean, and sugar beet—across 2 300 parcels observed in Vojvodina from 2018 to 2023. Yield prediction models were retrained and evaluated for each gap scenario. Winter wheat and sugar beet showed the steepest accuracy decline beyond 15-day gaps, linked to the narrow phenological windows of booting and canopy closure respectively. Maize and sunflower were more tolerant of sparse observations due to longer plateau phases in their spectral trajectories. Results provide quantitative guidance for data acquisition planning and for identifying crop types most in need of SAR data supplementation.

title: Parcel-level crop yield prediction in heterogeneous agricultural landscapes: methods, data requirements, and operational constraints
abstract: This book chapter reviews quantitative approaches to predicting crop yields at the individual parcel level using satellite time series and ancillary data, with emphasis on conditions typical of Central and South-East European agricultural regions. The chapter covers radiative transfer model inversion, statistical regression, and machine learning approaches, discussing their data requirements, computational demands, and performance under limited ground truth availability. A practical section addresses the challenge of obtaining parcel boundaries from heterogeneous national LPIS databases and the trade-offs involved in selecting temporal compositing windows. The chapter draws on published literature and on experiments conducted by the authors over parcels in Serbia, Hungary, and Romania between 2017 and 2024. An operational workflow suitable for deployment by regional agricultural advisory services is outlined, including a checklist of minimum data requirements and common failure modes encountered in practice.

title: Imbalanced Learning for Industrial Time-Series: A Structured Review of Methods and Evaluation Practices
abstract: This chapter surveys the literature on learning from imbalanced industrial time-series data published between 2010 and 2022, covering approximately 160 papers. The chapter is organised around five methodological families: resampling, cost-sensitive training, anomaly-detection-based approaches, threshold adjustment, and ensemble methods. For each family, representative algorithms are described, and reported evaluation metrics are tabulated. A recurring finding is that many papers report only accuracy or AUC-ROC despite these being insensitive to minority-class performance at high imbalance ratios; the chapter argues for systematic reporting of AUPRC and G-mean alongside domain-relevant cost measures. A taxonomy of evaluation pitfalls specific to temporal data—including label leakage across temporal folds and inappropriate use of stratified k-fold on non-stationary streams—is presented. The chapter concludes with a structured list of open problems, including the combination of concept drift adaptation with imbalanced learning and the lack of standardised public benchmarks for industrial fault streams.

title: Occupational dose distribution among cardiology staff during diagnostic coronary angiography in a regional hospital
abstract: This study characterised the distribution of occupational radiation doses received by cardiologists, scrub nurses, and anaesthesiology staff during 312 consecutive diagnostic coronary angiography procedures performed at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina over a 14-month period. Thermoluminescent dosimeters (TLD-100) were placed at the collar, chest, and wrist positions on all personnel present in the fluoroscopy suite. Dose area product (DAP) values were recorded for each procedure using a built-in ionisation chamber. The mean collar dose per procedure was 0.41 mSv for the primary operator and 0.09 mSv for the assisting nurse. A statistically significant correlation was found between DAP and operator collar dose (r = 0.73, p < 0.001). Procedures involving complex vessel anatomy required on average 38% more fluoroscopy time and produced collar doses approximately 1.6 times higher than straightforward cases. The paper recommends minimum shielding configurations and fluoroscopy time reduction strategies tailored to the observed workload pattern.

title: Evaluation of lead apron attenuation efficiency under realistic fluoroscopy scatter conditions
abstract: Lead aprons are the primary protective garment used by interventional staff, yet their attenuation efficiency under realistic scatter field conditions is seldom measured directly. This study evaluated seven commercially available apron models (0.25 mm, 0.35 mm, and 0.50 mm lead equivalent) using a Rando phantom as a scatter source at tube voltages of 70, 80, and 100 kVp. Dosimeters were placed beneath and above the apron surface at eleven anatomical points. At 80 kVp, the 0.35 mm equivalent aprons provided a mean attenuation factor of 93.4% at the thorax but only 74.1% at the lateral lumbar region, where apron overlap seams were present. The study found that no tested model provided uniform protection across all measurement points, and that declared lead equivalence systematically overestimated lateral flank protection by 8–15%. Recommendations are provided for apron selection and positioning protocols applicable to single-plane and biplane fluoroscopy suites.

title: Fluoroscopy time and DAP as predictors of staff dose in peripheral vascular interventions
abstract: Peripheral vascular interventions (PVI) are among the longer fluoroscopy procedures in an interventional suite, yet occupational dose data specific to this procedure class remain sparse in the regional literature. This prospective study enrolled 198 PVI cases at two institutions in Vojvodina and recorded fluoroscopy time, DAP, number of cine runs, and the personal dose equivalent Hp(10) for the primary operator, assistant, and circulating nurse. Median DAP was 42 Gy·cm² and median fluoroscopy time 18.4 minutes per procedure. Multivariate regression showed that fluoroscopy time was the single strongest predictor of operator dose, explaining 61% of variance after controlling for DAP and cine run count. For each additional minute of fluoroscopy, the operator collar dose increased by a mean of 19 μSv. Based on these findings, a set of fluoroscopy time reduction techniques was drafted and piloted over a subsequent six-month period, resulting in a mean reduction of 22% in fluoroscopy time without change in procedural success rate.

title: Implementation of a structured radiation dose optimisation protocol in an interventional cardiology unit: a before-and-after study
abstract: This paper describes the design and evaluation of a structured dose optimisation protocol introduced at the interventional cardiology unit of the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina in 2005. The protocol addressed frame rate selection, collimation practice, last-image-hold utilisation, and table height adjustment. Before-period data covered 420 procedures in 2004; after-period data covered 418 procedures in 2006. Primary operator collar doses were estimated from TLD measurements and DAP-to-dose conversion factors validated in the same suite. Mean DAP decreased from 58.3 Gy·cm² to 44.1 Gy·cm² (24% reduction; 95% CI: 19–29%). Estimated operator effective dose per procedure fell from 0.28 mSv to 0.19 mSv. Compliance with the protocol, assessed through observation checklists, reached 81% by the end of the after period. The study also found that frame rate reduction from 15 to 7.5 frames per second for standard diagnostic runs was achievable without reported loss of diagnostic confidence by attending cardiologists.

title: Eye lens dose to interventional cardiologists: measurements and comparison with the revised ICRP dose limit
abstract: Following the 2011 International Commission on Radiological Protection recommendation to lower the occupational eye lens dose limit to 20 mSv per year, this study measured eye lens doses for nine interventional cardiologists at two Vojvodina institutions over a 12-month period. HP(3) dosimeters were placed on custom headbands worn just above the lateral canthus. Eye lens dose was also estimated from collar TLD readings using a conversion factor derived from a Rando phantom experiment conducted in the same suite geometry. Directly measured HP(3) values ranged from 7.2 to 31.4 mSv over the study year; two operators exceeded the new 20 mSv annual limit. There was a systematic underestimation of eye lens dose when collar TLD readings were used with the conversion factor (mean ratio measured/estimated: 1.41). The paper argues for direct eye lens monitoring as standard practice rather than collar-based estimation for high-workload operators, and evaluates the feasibility of wearing protective eyewear.

title: Radiation dose optimisation in fluoroscopy-guided biliary drainage procedures: staff dose and patient dose considerations
abstract: Fluoroscopy-guided percutaneous biliary drainage (PBD) is performed predominantly by radiologists rather than cardiologists and involves prolonged intermittent fluoroscopy with varied angulation. This study examined both patient and operator doses in 87 PBD procedures at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina. Patient entrance skin dose was estimated from DAP and backscatter factors; operator doses were measured with TLD at collar and hand positions. Mean patient entrance skin dose was 312 mGy per procedure (range 84–890 mGy). Operator collar doses ranged from 0.08 to 0.62 mSv per procedure; hand doses for the primary operator averaged 1.14 mSv per procedure. The highest hand doses occurred during needle placement and guide-wire manipulation. Use of remote wire manipulation tools reduced mean hand dose by 34% in a subset of 22 procedures. Shielding audit identified that the available ceiling-suspended shield was used in only 47% of cases; compliance improved to 78% following a targeted training session.

title: A multicentre survey of radiation protection practices in interventional fluoroscopy units across Serbia and Bosnia-Herzegovina
abstract: This paper reports on a structured survey of radiation protection practices conducted at 14 interventional fluoroscopy units in Serbia and Bosnia-Herzegovina during 2012–2013. Unit physicists and lead radiologists at each site completed a standardised questionnaire covering equipment age, dose monitoring procedures, staff training records, shielding inventory, and protocol documentation. On-site measurements of scatter dose at standard positions were performed at eight of the 14 units using a calibrated ionisation chamber. Results showed that only five units had written dose optimisation protocols; staff personal dosimetry was conducted at all units but collar doses were routinely read at quarterly intervals rather than monthly at 10 of the 14 sites, delaying dose feedback. Equipment age ranged from 2 to 19 years; units with equipment older than 12 years produced scatter dose rates at the operator position 1.8 to 2.7 times higher than newer units for equivalent procedures. The paper provides a set of minimum practice standards derived from the survey findings.

title: Radiation protection in interventional fluoroscopy: a practical guide for clinical staff
abstract: This book chapter provides a practical, procedure-oriented overview of radiation protection measures applicable to fluoroscopy-guided interventional procedures. Topics covered include the physical basis of scatter radiation, occupational dose limits under Serbian and European regulatory frameworks, selection and correct use of personal protective equipment, optimisation of fluoroscopy technique parameters, monitoring of occupational doses, and special considerations for pregnant workers. Worked examples use dose data collected from clinical practice at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina. The chapter is intended for cardiologists, radiologists, and nurses who work in interventional suites and who may not have formal radiation physics training. Emphasis is placed on practical decision points encountered during procedures rather than theoretical derivations. A checklist for radiation protection audits and a template for local written protocols are included as appendices.

title: Long-term occupational dose trends in an interventional radiology department: a 20-year retrospective analysis
abstract: This retrospective analysis used personal dosimetry records held by the Serbian Radiation Protection and Nuclear Safety Agency to track annual occupational doses received by staff in the interventional radiology department of the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina from 1996 to 2016. Records covered 34 individuals across three professional categories: radiologists (n=11), radiographers (n=14), and nursing staff (n=9). Annual effective dose estimates were derived from collar dosimeter readings using standard conversion factors. Mean annual dose for radiologists declined from 4.8 mSv in 1997 to 1.2 mSv in 2016, coinciding with two equipment replacement cycles and the formal introduction of dose optimisation protocols. No individual exceeded the 20 mSv annual limit in any year; however, three radiologists showed cumulative 5-year doses exceeding 40 mSv in the period 1998–2005. The analysis highlights the measurable impact of protocol-driven dose management and equipment modernisation on long-term occupational dose.

title: Cryptographic Chaining in Database Audit Trails: Performance Trade-offs on OLTP Workloads
abstract: Adding per-record cryptographic chaining to a high-throughput OLTP database audit log introduces write latency that can affect transaction throughput. This paper reports controlled benchmark experiments conducted on a PostgreSQL 8.1 installation running on commodity server hardware, comparing four chaining strategies: no chaining, MD5 chaining in application middleware, SHA-256 chaining in a database trigger, and SHA-256 chaining in a dedicated log server receiving asynchronous replication. Workloads simulated a retail banking environment with between 200 and 1,800 transactions per second drawn from a parameterised synthetic generator calibrated against real workload traces provided by a partner institution. Results show that trigger-based chaining increases average transaction latency by 18–34 percent at 800 TPS, while the dedicated log server approach keeps latency overhead below 4 percent at the same throughput level, at the cost of a short consistency window of approximately 120 milliseconds. The paper recommends the asynchronous log server architecture for institutions processing more than 400 transactions per second, and provides configuration guidance for PostgreSQL streaming replication in this context.

title: Knowledge Management Maturity Across Post-Socialist Local Governments: A Comparative Survey in Serbia and Croatia
abstract: Using the six-dimension instrument developed in earlier work, this study compares knowledge management maturity levels across 28 local governments in Serbia and 19 in Croatia. Data were collected via self-administered questionnaires completed by department heads (N = 412) during 2014–2015. Descriptive statistics and Mann–Whitney U tests were applied to detect cross-country and size-related differences. Results show that average maturity scores in both countries fall in the second of five levels ('reactive'), with technology and measurement dimensions scoring consistently lowest. Croatian municipalities score marginally higher on the strategy dimension, a difference that is statistically significant (p < 0.05) but modest in effect size (r = 0.17). Institution size correlates positively with maturity on the process dimension (ρ = 0.41, p < 0.001). The paper discusses how shared administrative legacies coexist with divergent post-1990 reform trajectories to produce partially overlapping maturity profiles.

title: Zrelost upravljanja znanjem i apsorpcioni kapacitet u regionalnim razvojnim agencijama: iskustva iz Srbije i Rumunije
abstract: Istraživanje ispituje odnos između zrelosti upravljanja znanjem i apsorpcionog kapaciteta (ACAP) u dvanaest regionalnih razvojnih agencija – šest u Srbiji i šest u Rumuniji. Podaci su prikupljeni kombinacijom upitnika (N = 96 rukovodilaca i analitičara) i analize projektnih izveštaja u periodu od 2020. do 2021. godine. Zrelost upravljanja znanjem merena je prilagođenim šestodimenzionalnim instrumentom, a ACAP Zahra–George skalom adaptiranom za javni sektor. Korelaciona i regresiona analiza pokazale su da su dimenzije kulture i strategije upravljanja znanjem najjači prediktori apsorpcionog kapaciteta (β = 0,38 i 0,31, p < 0,01). Agencije s višim nivoom zrelosti pokazale su statistički značajno veću iskorišćenost EU fondova u posmatranom periodu (t = 2,91, p < 0,01). Nalazi se razmatraju u svetlu različitih reformskih putanja decentralizacije u dve zemlje.

title: Procena zrelosti upravljanja znanjem u zdravstvenim ustanovama: prilagođavanje okvira za upotrebu u domovima zdravlja u Vojvodini
abstract: Istraživanje ispituje mogućnost primene šestodimenzionalnog okvira zrelosti upravljanja znanjem u primarnoj zdravstvenoj zaštiti, na uzorku od osam domova zdravlja u Vojvodini. Okvir je adaptiran uvođenjem zdravstveno-specifičnih indikatora u dimenzijama procesa i kulture, na osnovu kvalitativnih intervjua sa 27 koordinatora i šefova službi. Kvantitativan deo istraživanja uključivao je anketiranje 183 zaposlena. Analiza pouzdanosti i eksploratorska faktorska analiza ukazuju na potrebu za razdvajanjem dimenzije kulture na dve posebne podskale: kultura razmene znanja između stručnjaka i kultura organizacionog učenja. Prosečan nivo zrelosti u uzorku odgovara trećem stepenu petostepene skale, što je viši rezultat nego u opštinskim upravama iz ranijih studija. Identifikovani su i specifični izazovi vezani za čuvanje medicinskog znanja u uslovima visoke fluktuacije lekara.

title: Conditional tail expectation for bivariate environmental risk under asymmetric dependence
abstract: The conditional tail expectation (CTE), also known as expected shortfall, is a coherent risk measure widely used in financial risk management but less frequently applied to environmental hazard quantification. This paper derives analytical expressions for the bivariate CTE when the dependence structure belongs to the class of Archimedean copulas with completely monotone generators, covering the Clayton, Gumbel–Hougaard and Joe families. The expressions are used to compute the expected discharge at one gauging station given that discharge at a second station simultaneously exceeds its empirical 95th, 99th and 99.9th percentiles, using records from eleven paired stations in the Tisza basin. Clayton copula fits indicate substantial asymmetry in lower and upper tail dependence, and the resulting CTEs are 12 to 38 percent higher than those implied by the bivariate Gaussian model with matched Kendall τ. Simulation experiments confirm the accuracy of the analytical results for sample sizes as small as n = 200.

title: Integracija Balanced Scorecard pristupa u prioritizaciju R&D portfolija: studija slučaja
abstract: Rad opisuje integraciju Balanced Scorecard (BSC) okvira s modelom prioritizacije R&D portfolija u jednom srednje velikom srpskom preduzeću iz sektora automatizacije industrijskih procesa, koje zapošljava oko 180 radnika. Studija slučaja zasnovana je na dvogodišnjoj saradnji (2017–2019) tokom koje je autorka učestvovala kao konsultant. Prikazano je kako su četiri BSC perspektive (finansijska, korisnička, interna, rast i učenje) prevedene u kvantitativne težine kriterijuma za AHP model prioritizacije. Inicijalni portfelj od 21 projektnog predloga sveden je na realizabilni skup od 12 projekata. Praćenjem realizacije tokom 18 meseci utvrđeno je da su projekti selektovani integrisanim BSC-AHP pristupom u proseku ostvarili 91% planiranih KPI vrednosti, u poređenju sa 74% kod projekata odobrenih ranije, bez formalnog modela. Rad ukazuje na vrednost iterativnih kalibracijskih sesija s menadžmentom kao ključnog faktora uspešne primene.

title: Grey Relational Analysis for Ranking Vegetable Oil Suppliers Under Incomplete Information
abstract: Supplier evaluation in the edible oil sector frequently involves incomplete or imprecise data, particularly for small and medium-sized enterprises that lack formalised procurement systems. This study applies grey relational analysis (GRA) to rank five sunflower oil suppliers for a mid-sized processing company in southern Vojvodina. Data were gathered through structured interviews and a review of procurement records spanning three years. Eight evaluation attributes were included: cost per tonne, moisture content of raw material, contract fulfilment rate, lead time variability, traceability documentation, proximity to plant, pesticide residue compliance, and supplier financial health. Grey coefficients and relational grades were computed, and a final ranking was derived. Results indicated that traceability documentation and pesticide residue compliance emerged as the most discriminating attributes. The paper also discusses the practical conditions under which GRA offers advantages over classical weighted-sum methods when attribute data are partially missing.

title: Perceived vs. Measured Resilience: A Comparison of Manager Self-Assessments and Financial Ratio Proxies in Serbian SMEs
abstract: Organizational resilience is often captured through manager self-reports, yet it is unclear how well subjective assessments correspond to observable financial indicators. This study compares resilience scores from a structured questionnaire administered to 93 managers of Serbian manufacturing SMEs with three financial ratio proxies—current ratio, interest coverage ratio, and operating profit margin—drawn from the Business Registers Agency of Serbia database for the same firms. Spearman correlations between self-reported resilience dimensions and financial proxies were weak to moderate (ρ = 0.18–0.41), with the strongest alignment observed between resource redundancy perceptions and the current ratio. Firm age and industry sector moderated several relationships. The findings suggest that survey instruments and financial proxies capture distinct facets of resilience and should be treated as complementary rather than interchangeable. Implications for measurement practice in transitional economy contexts are discussed, including data availability constraints that limit purely objective approaches in the region.

title: Budget-Aware Warm-Starting for Multi-Objective Hyperparameter Optimisation Across Related Tasks
abstract: When a team must tune a family of related models—such as the same architecture retrained on different regional subsets of sensor data—prior optimisation runs contain useful information that is typically discarded. This paper investigates warm-starting NSGA-III with Pareto fronts transferred from earlier runs on related tasks, measuring how transfer affects convergence speed and final solution quality under a fixed evaluation budget of 80 configurations per task. The testbed consists of six regression tasks derived from an industrial energy-consumption monitoring dataset with 14 input features and targets covering heating and cooling loads across building types. Search space includes learning rate schedule type, hidden layer widths (two layers), activation function, and batch normalisation placement. Transfer is implemented via population seeding combined with archive injection; three seeding ratios (25 %, 50 %, 75 % of initial population) are compared against cold-start NSGA-III and random search. At 50 % seeding the method reduces the number of evaluations needed to reach a reference hypervolume threshold by a median of 31 evaluations across tasks, without degrading diversity on tasks where source and target fronts differ substantially. A negative transfer case is identified when task correlation falls below 0.3 in a feature-based similarity metric.

title: Applying Local Differential Privacy to Aggregate Sales Reporting in a Food-Processing SME Cluster: A Simulation Study
abstract: This paper examines how local differential privacy (LDP) can be applied to aggregate sales figures shared among fifteen food-processing firms participating in a regional cluster in Vojvodina. The study uses synthetic transaction data calibrated against publicly available industry statistics from the Serbian Business Registers Agency for the period 2018–2021. Three LDP mechanisms are compared: randomised response, the Laplace mechanism, and the Piecewise mechanism. Privacy budgets ranging from ε = 0.5 to ε = 4.0 are tested against utility loss measured by mean absolute percentage error on cluster-level demand forecasts. At ε = 1.0, the Piecewise mechanism achieves a mean absolute percentage error of 6.8 percent on monthly demand aggregates, compared to 11.4 percent for randomised response at the same budget. The simulation covers 10,000 Monte Carlo runs per configuration. Results suggest that LDP is practically viable for cluster-level reporting tasks where individual firm figures need not be disclosed, but that tighter privacy budgets substantially degrade forecast accuracy for smaller sub-clusters of fewer than five firms. The paper concludes with a discussion of governance conditions under which cluster coordinators could administer the noise-injection step.

title: Stress intensity factor solutions for weld root cracks in cruciform fillet-welded joints under combined bending and axial load
abstract: Weld root cracks in cruciform fillet-welded joints are a common failure mode in steel bridge cross-girder connections yet SIF solutions for combined loading remain limited in the literature. This paper presents parametric finite element results for mode I stress intensity factors at weld root crack tips in cruciform joints with leg ratio a/T from 0.1 to 0.7 and plate thickness T from 12 to 40 mm, under 19 combinations of axial and in-plane bending loads. Three-dimensional models were built in Abaqus with refined meshes at the crack front using collapsed quadratic elements. Interaction integrals were used to extract KI values. The results were fitted to a polynomial correction function F(a/T, ρ, λ) with a maximum fitting error of 2.1% over the parametric space. Validation against three published experimental datasets showed mean deviation below 5%. The proposed solutions are intended for direct use in Paris-law integration routines for bridge connection fatigue assessment.

title: Audit Trail Completeness and Gender Outcomes in SME Loan Files: A Documentary Analysis
abstract: Credit audit trails—the accumulated paper and digital records justifying a lending decision—vary considerably in completeness across bank branches in Serbia. This study asks whether incomplete audit trails are associated with worse loan terms for female applicants, using a sample of 860 closed loan files obtained under a data-sharing agreement with two regional banks. We coded each file for 23 documentation items covering income verification, collateral appraisal, guarantor identity, and approval rationale. Incomplete files, defined as missing six or more items, were more common in rural branches and for loans below RSD 2 million. Regression analysis shows that female applicants whose files were incomplete received interest rate spreads 47 basis points higher than male applicants with equivalently incomplete files, while no significant gender gap appeared in complete-file loans. The finding suggests that discretionary judgement fills gaps left by missing documentation, and that this discretion operates in a gender-differentiated manner. Policy recommendations focus on minimum documentation standards for small business loans.

title: Does Digitalisation of Loan Applications Reduce Gender Gaps? Preliminary Evidence from Serbian Fintech Pilots
abstract: Several Serbian banks introduced fully digital SME loan application portals between 2019 and 2022, removing face-to-face loan officer contact for initial screening. This preprint reports preliminary findings from a difference-in-differences analysis comparing gender gaps in approval rates and collateral requirements before and after portal introduction at four banks, against a control group of six banks that retained in-person processing throughout the period. The sample covers 8,720 applications filed between January 2018 and June 2023. Early results suggest that digitalization reduced the gender gap in approval rates by approximately 7 percentage points and narrowed collateral differentials by 9 percentage points at treated banks, consistent with the hypothesis that removing discretionary face-to-face contact attenuates gender bias. However, digital applicants show positive selection on financial literacy, complicating interpretation. The analysis is ongoing and the current estimates should be treated as provisional pending full data cleaning and robustness checks.

title: Anti-Money-Laundering Obligations and Islamic Finance: Correspondent Banking Challenges in the Western Balkans
abstract: Islamic financial institutions in the Western Balkans face particular difficulties in maintaining correspondent banking relationships because their fee-based and profit-sharing income structures do not map cleanly onto the transaction-monitoring algorithms used by major European correspondent banks, which are calibrated for interest-bearing products. This study draws on structured interviews with compliance officers at six Western Balkan banks that handle Islamic finance-related transactions and reviews thirty-six suspicious transaction reports filed between 2018 and 2022 that originated from misclassification of legitimate Islamic finance transactions. The paper finds that approximately 40% of flagged transactions were later cleared as compliant, suggesting a significant false-positive rate driven by monitoring system design rather than genuine risk. Recommendations include FATF typology guidance tailored to profit-sharing structures and bilateral regulatory cooperation between national financial intelligence units in the region.
venue: Journal of Financial Crime and Compliance in Emerging Markets

title: Pollen germination capacity of six apricot cultivars after short-duration sub-zero temperature exposure
abstract: Pollen from six apricot cultivars grown in Vojvodina orchards was collected at full bloom and subjected to controlled freezing at −1, −2, −3, and −4 °C for durations of 30, 60, and 120 minutes in a programmable freeze chamber. Germination was assessed on agar-sucrose medium after 24 h at 25 °C. At −2 °C for 60 minutes, mean germination across cultivars dropped from a control value of 74.3 % to 41.8 %, with the cultivar 'Keckemetska ruža' showing the steepest decline (68.1 % to 28.4 %) and 'Novosadska rodna' the smallest (79.2 % to 62.7 %). Pollen tube length was reduced proportionally to temperature decrease and duration. Scanning electron microscopy revealed collapsed apertures in non-viable grains. Results indicate that cultivar selection alone can mitigate germination losses by up to 34 percentage points under mild frost events, providing a practical basis for variety replacement recommendations in the region.
venue: Acta Horticulturae Pannonica

title: Comparative polyphenol profiles of six Sambucus nigra accessions selected from the Pannonian Plain under identical orchard conditions
abstract: Six elderberry accessions maintained in a common-garden trial at the Faculty of Agriculture experimental orchard in Rimski Šančevi were evaluated over three seasons (2003–2005) for total polyphenol content (TPC), total anthocyanin content (TAC), chlorogenic acid, and DPPH radical scavenging capacity. Accessions were designated SN-PAN-01 through SN-PAN-06. TPC ranged from 523 to 1,024 mg GAE per 100 g FW. Accession SN-PAN-04 consistently exhibited the highest TAC (8.3 mg cyanidin-3-glucoside equivalents per g FW) and the strongest DPPH scavenging activity (IC50 = 0.31 mg mL−1). Chlorogenic acid was most abundant in SN-PAN-02 (5.8 mg g−1 DW). Year-to-year variation within accessions was generally smaller than between-accession variation, suggesting genetic rather than environmental factors as the primary driver of polyphenol profile in a uniform environment. The data supported selecting SN-PAN-04 for further stress physiology trials.
venue: Acta Horticulturae Pannonica

title: Loss Partitioning in a 7 kW Bidirectional CLLC Stage for a Second-Life Battery Pack
abstract: Second-life lithium-ion battery packs repurposed from electric vehicles exhibit a wider terminal voltage range and higher internal resistance spread than new cells, placing additional demands on the DC-DC interface converter. This paper reports a detailed loss partitioning study on a 7 kW bidirectional CLLC stage designed for a second-life pack with a nominal voltage of 72 V and an operating range of 55–88 V. Losses were separated into switching losses (measured via double-pulse test), conduction losses (derived from on-state resistance measurements at operating temperature), and magnetic losses (calorimetric method). At full load in forward mode, total converter loss was 218 W, with magnetic losses contributing 38 %, primary switching losses 29 %, secondary conduction losses 21 %, and gate drive and auxiliary supply 12 %. Across the battery voltage range, total loss varied by ±19 % relative to the nominal operating point. Frequency schedules that minimise total loss as a function of instantaneous battery voltage are computed and compared against constant-frequency and fixed-frequency-with-phase-shift strategies.
venue: Transactions on Power Conversion and Drives

title: A Rule-Based Explanation Layer for Support Vector Machine Classifiers in Tabular Medical Data
abstract: This paper describes a post-hoc explanation method for support vector machine (SVM) classifiers applied to tabular clinical datasets. The approach extracts conjunctive rules from the SVM decision boundary by sampling the margin region and fitting a compact rule set using a covering algorithm. Experiments were conducted on three publicly available datasets from the UCI repository covering diabetes screening, heart disease risk, and hospital readmission, comprising between 768 and 14 440 instances. The extracted rule sets achieve fidelity scores of 0.87–0.92 relative to the original SVM predictions while using on average 4.3 conditions per rule. A user study with eleven clinicians assessed rule interpretability on a five-point Likert scale; median ratings ranged from 3.8 to 4.4. The method is compared against LIME and a decision tree surrogate baseline. Results indicate that the rule-based approach is more consistent across repeated runs and produces shorter explanations, at a modest cost in fidelity. Limitations include sensitivity to the sampling density near the decision boundary and reduced performance on highly imbalanced classes.
venue: Journal of Intelligent Information Systems and Applications

title: Monotonicity Constraints as an Interpretability Tool in Gradient Boosting for Credit Scoring
abstract: Gradient boosting ensembles are widely used in credit scoring but are difficult to audit for regulatory compliance. This work studies whether enforcing monotonicity constraints during training serves as a practical interpretability mechanism without substantially degrading predictive performance. We experiment on a proprietary dataset of 120 000 loan applications from a regional bank, preprocessed under differential privacy guarantees to allow publication of aggregate statistics. Models with monotonicity constraints imposed on twelve economically motivated features show an area under the ROC curve of 0.791 compared with 0.803 for unconstrained models, a difference within one standard deviation across five cross-validation folds. Shapley value distributions under the constrained regime are more stable across data subsets, and the number of Shapley sign reversals—a proposed diagnostic for non-monotone influence—drops by 63 percent. We also show that constraint violations detected in unconstrained models correlate with demographic subgroup shifts in the test set. The findings suggest monotonicity constraints are a low-cost intervention for producing models that are easier to audit under the EU's algorithmic accountability guidelines.
venue: Proceedings of the Central European Conference on Data Mining and Machine Learning

title: Evaluating Attention Weights as Explanations in Sequence Classification Tasks
abstract: Attention weights in transformer-based sequence classifiers are frequently presented as explanations, but their relationship to model predictions is contested. This paper systematically evaluates attention-based explanations against gradient-based saliency maps and integrated gradients on four text classification benchmarks: news topic labelling, sentiment analysis, scientific claim verification, and legal clause categorisation. For each task, 500 explanations per method are assessed using three proxy faithfulness metrics: sufficiency, comprehensiveness, and input reduction accuracy. Across benchmarks, attention weights score lower on sufficiency (mean 0.61) than integrated gradients (mean 0.74) and are inconsistent with gradient-based saliency in 38 percent of instances at the token level. The gap narrows for longer sequences. We additionally collect human judgements on 200 explanation pairs per task; annotators prefer gradient-based explanations for legal and scientific text but show no strong preference for sentiment. The paper does not claim that attention is categorically uninformative, but argues that the choice of explanation method should be task-specific and empirically validated rather than chosen by convention.
venue: Journal of Language Technology and Computational Linguistics

title: Benchmarking Counterfactual Explanation Methods for Tabular Classifiers: A Comparative Study
abstract: Counterfactual explanations describe the minimal feature changes needed to obtain a different classifier output. This chapter surveys and benchmarks eight counterfactual generation methods on six tabular datasets spanning finance, healthcare, and public administration. Evaluation covers proximity (mean feature distance to the original instance), sparsity (average number of changed features), validity (fraction of counterfactuals that achieve the target class), and actionability (fraction respecting domain-defined immutable features). Methods tested include DICE, a growing spheres approach, a prototype-based method, and five research implementations. No single method dominates across all criteria: prototype-based approaches score highest on actionability (0.84) but lowest on proximity. Growing spheres produce the sparsest counterfactuals (1.9 changed features on average) but have lower validity for nonlinear boundaries. The chapter provides a decision guide mapping application requirements to method recommendations and identifies persistent gaps, particularly in handling heterogeneous mixed-type feature spaces and in generating diverse yet realistic counterfactual sets.
venue: Advances in Explainable and Trustworthy Machine Learning (edited volume, Springer Verlag)
