title: A Dataset for Sentence-Level Faithfulness Annotation in Abstractive Summarisation
abstract: This paper introduces SerbFaith-1K, a dataset of 1 200 abstractive summaries in Serbian and English generated from news and scientific abstracts, annotated at the sentence level for factual faithfulness. Each summary sentence is labelled as fully faithful, partially faithful, or hallucinated, with sub-labels indicating the error type (entity substitution, relation inversion, event fabrication, numerical distortion). Two trained annotators labelled all instances; inter-annotator agreement reached Fleiss's kappa of 0.71. The paper describes the annotation guidelines, the adjudication process for disputed cases, and an analysis of error type distributions, finding that numerical distortions are the most frequent error in scientific abstract summaries (34 percent of hallucination instances) while entity substitution dominates in news summaries (52 percent). Baseline experiments using NLI-based and question-answering-based faithfulness detectors on the dataset show F1 scores of 0.63 and 0.67 respectively. The dataset is released under a CC BY 4.0 licence.
venue: Proceedings of the Balkan Workshop on Natural Language Processing and Computational Linguistics

title: Natural Language Inference as a Proxy for Factual Consistency Checking in Generated Text
abstract: Factual consistency checking in automatically generated text is often framed as a natural language inference (NLI) task, treating the source document as premise and each generated sentence as hypothesis. This paper investigates how well off-the-shelf NLI models serve this purpose. We evaluate five multilingual NLI checkpoints on four existing faithfulness benchmarks and find that entailment scores correlate with human faithfulness ratings at Spearman ρ = 0.49–0.67, varying substantially across domains. Performance drops markedly on long source documents (over 800 tokens), where models tend to produce neutral labels even for clearly hallucinated sentences. We trace this degradation to attention saturation in the encoder and show that chunking the premise into paragraphs and aggregating with min-pooling raises ρ by 0.09 on average. We also construct a controlled adversarial subset by swapping named entities and reversing numerical values, finding that NLI models detect fewer than half of these manipulations. The analysis suggests NLI-based consistency checking is a useful but incomplete signal, and that domain-specific fine-tuning and length-handling strategies are necessary for reliable deployment.
venue: Journal of Language Technology and Computational Linguistics

title: Probing Intermediate Representations of Pre-Trained Language Models for Factual Knowledge
abstract: Pre-trained language models (PLMs) are known to encode factual knowledge in their parameters, but the distribution of this knowledge across layers is not well understood. This paper applies a probing classifier methodology to six PLMs of varying sizes, testing for subject–relation–object triples from a manually constructed knowledge base of 4 800 facts in four domains: geography, institutional history, scientific authorship, and legal norms. For each fact, linear probes are trained on the hidden states of every transformer layer. Probing accuracy peaks at middle layers for relational facts (mean 71 percent) and at upper layers for entity-centric facts (mean 68 percent). Larger models do not consistently outperform smaller ones on low-frequency facts. We further investigate whether facts that are poorly encoded by the probe are also more susceptible to hallucination at inference time, finding a moderate but consistent correlation (r = 0.44 across domains). The results have implications for strategies that selectively freeze or update layers during fine-tuning to reduce hallucination.

title: Uncertainty Quantification in Transformer Outputs Using Monte Carlo Dropout: A Study on Question Answering
abstract: This paper investigates whether Monte Carlo (MC) dropout can serve as a practical uncertainty estimate for transformer-based question answering (QA) models, and whether high uncertainty correlates with hallucinated or incorrect answers. Experiments use three QA datasets: one in English, one in Serbian, and one bilingual domain-specific dataset covering regulatory documents. MC dropout is applied at inference time with 30 forward passes; variance across answer span predictions is used as an uncertainty proxy. Models with high predictive variance are shown to produce incorrect answers at a rate 2.3 times higher than low-variance instances (p < 0.001). Calibration curves indicate that raw MC dropout variance is poorly calibrated (expected calibration error 0.18) but becomes usable after temperature scaling (ECE 0.07). For open-domain questions, uncertainty correlates more strongly with answer correctness than for closed-domain regulatory QA, where models tend to be overconfident. We discuss practical thresholds for triggering human review based on uncertainty estimates and the trade-off between coverage and abstention rate.
venue: Journal of Intelligent Information Systems and Applications

title: Towards Automatic Citation Grounding: Linking Sentences in Generated Reports to Source Passages
abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems retrieve source passages before generating text, but they do not reliably attribute each generated sentence to the passages that support it. This paper addresses citation grounding: the automatic identification of which retrieved passage, if any, provides evidence for a generated sentence. We formulate the task as a bi-encoder retrieval problem followed by a cross-encoder re-ranking step, and train on a newly constructed dataset of 9 400 (generated sentence, passage, label) triples drawn from generated financial and medical reports. Labels were produced by a two-stage annotation protocol combining automatic NLI pre-filtering with human adjudication. The bi-encoder alone achieves recall@3 of 0.79; adding the cross-encoder re-ranker raises it to 0.86. Grounding precision at rank 1 is 0.71. We find that sentences containing numerical claims are the most difficult to ground (precision 0.58), while definitional sentences are easiest (precision 0.83). The paper also introduces a simple attribution confidence score and shows it correlates with human judgements of citation quality (ρ = 0.61).

title: Detecting Hallucinations in Long-Form Language Model Outputs Using Decomposition and Atomic Claim Verification
abstract: Long-form text generated by large language models may contain a mixture of supported and unsupported claims within a single paragraph, making sentence-level faithfulness evaluation insufficient. This paper proposes a pipeline that decomposes generated paragraphs into atomic claims using a fine-tuned decomposition model, retrieves relevant evidence passages for each claim from a linked corpus, and classifies each claim as supported, contradicted, or unverifiable using a fine-tuned NLI model. The pipeline is evaluated on three long-form generation tasks: biographies, medical treatment summaries, and legal case descriptions. On a human-annotated test set of 480 generated documents, the pipeline achieves claim-level detection F1 of 0.74, compared with 0.61 for a sentence-level baseline. Error analysis shows that implicit presuppositions and vague quantifiers are the main sources of remaining false negatives. We further report that the fraction of unverifiable claims—those where no retrieved passage addresses the claim—is a useful document-level hallucination risk signal, correlating with human overall quality ratings at ρ = 0.58.

title: Retrieval Quality and Its Effect on Downstream Hallucination Rates in RAG Systems
abstract: In retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), the quality of retrieved context directly affects the faithfulness of generated outputs, yet the relationship is rarely studied in controlled settings. This paper designs a factorial experiment varying retrieval precision (high, medium, low, and adversarial) across three RAG configurations (BM25 only, dense retrieval only, and hybrid) and two generator sizes. Retrieval precision is operationalised by injecting passages with controlled relevance degradation into the retrieval pool. Hallucination rates are measured using the atomic claim verification pipeline from prior work. Moving from high to medium retrieval precision increases hallucination rate by an average of 11 percentage points; adversarial passages (containing plausible but incorrect facts) increase it by 28 percentage points relative to the high-precision baseline. Dense retrieval generators are more susceptible to adversarial passages than BM25 generators. Generator size moderates adversarial sensitivity: larger models (7B parameters) show smaller increases than smaller models (1.3B) under adversarial conditions. The results provide empirical grounding for retrieval quality requirements in production RAG deployments.

title: Post-Hoc Explanation Consistency Under Distribution Shift: An Empirical Study
abstract: Post-hoc explanation methods are typically evaluated on held-out data from the same distribution as the training set. This paper examines how LIME, SHAP, and integrated gradients behave when the test distribution shifts relative to training. We induce controlled distribution shifts in four classification tasks (text, tabular, image, and time-series) by progressively modifying covariate distributions. Explanation consistency is measured as the rank correlation between feature importance scores produced on original and shifted instances matched by prediction confidence. All three methods degrade under shift, but the rate and nature of degradation differ: SHAP explanations lose consistency faster on tabular data (rank correlation drops from 0.81 to 0.47 at moderate shift), while integrated gradients are relatively stable for text and image tasks. We also show that explanation inconsistency is a detectable signal for distribution shift itself, providing a potential monitoring use case. The study uses no proprietary data; all datasets and shift protocols are described in sufficient detail for replication.
venue: Journal of Machine Learning Research and Applications

title: GroundCheck: A Framework for Real-Time Citation Verification in RAG-Powered Document Assistants
abstract: Production document assistant systems built on retrieval-augmented generation need to verify that claims in their outputs are traceable to specific source passages before responses are shown to users. This paper describes GroundCheck, a modular verification framework that intercepts generation outputs, decomposes them into atomic claims, and runs lightweight verification against the retrieved context within a latency budget of 400 milliseconds per response on commodity hardware. The framework uses a distilled cross-encoder for claim–passage entailment checking (73M parameters) and a rule-based post-processing step to attach inline citation markers to verified claims. In an offline evaluation against manually annotated outputs from a legal document assistant, GroundCheck achieves precision 0.80 and recall 0.76 for correctly identified unsupported claims. A qualitative deployment study with 24 legal professionals found that citation markers increased perceived trustworthiness of the system on a seven-point scale by 1.4 points on average. Failure analysis highlights remaining difficulties with multi-hop reasoning chains and implicitly contradictory evidence.

title: Evaluating Explanation Fidelity Under Prompt Variation in Instruction-Tuned Language Models
abstract: Instruction-tuned language models can produce natural-language explanations for their own outputs on request, but it is unclear whether these self-explanations reflect the model's actual inference path or are generated independently of it. This paper measures explanation fidelity by comparing self-generated explanations to three external explanation methods (saliency, attention rollout, and a perturbation-based method) across 600 prompted classification and extraction tasks. Agreement between self-explanations and external methods, measured by normalised token-level overlap, averages 0.41 and varies substantially with prompt wording. Systematically varying the explanation prompt reveals that adding the phrase 'cite the exact words from the input that determined your answer' raises agreement to 0.55 without affecting task performance. We also find that self-explanations are more likely to be faithful when the model's output confidence is high and when the task is extractive rather than abstractive. The results have practical implications for the design of explanation prompts in deployed systems and suggest that external verification of self-explanations is necessary for high-stakes applications.

title: Constraint Propagation Strategies for Tile-Based Dungeon Layout Generation
abstract: This paper examines how different arc-consistency algorithms affect the quality and speed of procedurally generated tile-based dungeon maps. We implemented AC-3, MAC, and a custom directional variant within a backtracking CSP solver operating on a 32×32 grid of room tiles. Each cell carries domain variables encoding wall configuration, connectivity class, and enemy density. The directional variant reduced backtracking steps by 38% compared to AC-3 on a benchmark suite of 500 target layout specifications drawn from an existing game design corpus. Mean generation time dropped from 1.4 seconds to 0.6 seconds per map at this grid size. We also report how constraint weighting based on player-path criticality improves playability scores in a blind evaluation with 24 game-design students. The results suggest that propagation order informed by spatial topology is more effective than uniform propagation for room-network structures.

title: Skalabilnost OCSP stapling mehanizma u opterećenim TLS okruženjima: merenja i ograničenja
abstract: OCSP stapling prenet je u TLS 1.3 kao preferirani mehanizam provere statusa sertifikata, ali su njegova skalabilna ograničenja na strani servera nedovoljno istražena. Ovaj rad meri uticaj stapling operacija na propusnost TLS rukovanjem na serverima s različitim profilima sertifikata — kratkim, srednjim i dugim vekom trajanja. Testovi su sprovedeni na konfiguraciji s jednim poslužiteljem koji obrađuje do 20.000 TLS rukovanja u sekundi, koristeći nginx i prilagođeni omotač za OpenSSL. Mereno je zauzeće CPU-a, memorije i kašnjenje osvežavanja OCSP odgovora. Rezultati pokazuju da frekvencija osvežavanja OCSP odgovora direktno utiče na propusnost pri vrednostima ispod 30 sekundi perioda kešovanja, povećavajući CPU opterećenje za 9–17%. Rad predlaže adaptivni raspored osvežavanja zasnovan na tekućem opterećenju sistema.

title: Character-Level Neural Transliteration for Serbian: Training Data, Architecture Choices, and Error Analysis
abstract: Deterministic rule-based transliteration between Serbian Cyrillic and Latin scripts handles the majority of tokens correctly, but fails on foreign loanwords, abbreviations, and alphanumeric strings. This paper investigates whether a character-level sequence-to-sequence neural model can handle these exceptions while remaining accurate on regular tokens. We trained models on a corpus of 2.3 million aligned Cyrillic–Latin token pairs extracted from parallel editions of official gazettes, experimenting with LSTM encoder-decoder architectures with attention, as well as a character-level transformer. The transformer model achieved a character error rate of 0.4% on regular tokens and 3.1% on the exception classes, compared with 0.1% and 19.4% respectively for the deterministic baseline. We performed a detailed error analysis categorising 800 mistransliterated tokens by type. The paper concludes that a cascaded system — deterministic rules followed by the neural model for detected exceptions — outperforms either component alone, reaching a token error rate of 0.6% overall.

title: Ranking Renewable Energy Alternatives Using an Interval Type-2 Fuzzy TOPSIS Approach
abstract: This paper addresses the selection of renewable energy technologies for small municipalities in the Vojvodina region of Serbia using an interval type-2 fuzzy TOPSIS framework. Five criteria—cost, CO₂ emissions, land use, local employment impact, and technical maturity—were evaluated by a panel of seven domain experts whose linguistic assessments were encoded as trapezoidal interval type-2 fuzzy numbers. Three candidate technologies were assessed: small-scale wind turbines, rooftop photovoltaic arrays, and biomass combustion units. The upper and lower membership functions were constructed from expert responses collected via a structured questionnaire administered in 2022. After applying the extended TOPSIS ranking procedure, photovoltaic arrays ranked highest under four of the five weighting schemes tested in a subsequent sensitivity analysis involving 120 weight perturbation scenarios. The results were cross-validated against a crisp AHP ranking obtained independently, showing rank agreement in 83% of scenarios. The study highlights how inter-expert disagreement propagates through the type-2 framework differently than in type-1 fuzzy TOPSIS, particularly for the cost criterion where expert opinion variance was highest.
venue: Advances in Fuzzy Systems and Applications

title: Feature Construction via Symbolic Regression as a Preprocessing Step for Supervised Classification
abstract: This paper investigates whether symbolic regression can be used to construct informative nonlinear features from raw tabular inputs before training a standard classification algorithm. The proposed pipeline runs a population of grammar-guided GP individuals to minimise a surrogate fitness based on mutual information between the candidate feature and the class label, independently of any downstream classifier. Constructed features are then appended to the original feature set and used to train a logistic regression model and a k-nearest-neighbour classifier. Experiments on 25 UCI-style binary classification datasets show that adding one GP-constructed feature improves average area under the ROC curve by 0.031 for logistic regression and 0.044 for k-NN compared to baselines without feature construction. The improvement is statistically significant (paired t-test, p < 0.01) on 18 of 25 datasets. The method is most effective on datasets with strong nonlinear interactions between predictors and the target.

title: Influence of homogenisation pressure on emulsion stability prior to spray drying of flaxseed oil in sodium caseinate–lactose matrices
abstract: This study examined how inlet emulsion properties affect the encapsulation efficiency and oxidative stability of flaxseed oil microcapsules prepared by spray drying. Oil-in-water emulsions (20% w/w oil load) were homogenised at three pressures (50, 100, and 150 bar) using a two-stage valve homogeniser before atomisation. Droplet size d(4,3) decreased from 4.2 μm to 1.1 μm as pressure increased; however, microcapsule encapsulation efficiency peaked at 100 bar (91.3%) and declined slightly at 150 bar (88.7%), attributed to coalescence during atomisation. Peroxide values after four weeks of storage at 40°C were 12.4, 8.7, and 10.1 mEq O₂/kg oil for the three pressures respectively. The 100 bar treatment also yielded the highest α-linolenic acid retention (94.1%). These findings indicate that intermediate homogenisation pressures balance droplet refinement and wall coverage in protein-lactose spray-dried systems, providing practical guidance for process scale-up with oxidation-sensitive plant oils.

title: Effect of inlet air temperature on powder morphology and fatty acid profile retention in spray-dried evening primrose oil microcapsules
abstract: Evening primrose oil, rich in γ-linolenic acid (GLA, 9.2% of total fatty acids), was encapsulated in a whey protein concentrate–maltodextrin (DE 12) blend at a 1:3 weight ratio. Spray drying was performed at inlet temperatures of 150, 170, and 190°C, with a fixed feed rate of 5 mL/min and outlet temperature maintained between 65 and 80°C. Powder yield ranged from 67% to 79% across treatments. Scanning electron microscopy revealed increasingly spherical and smooth particles at higher temperatures, with fewer surface fissures. Gas chromatography–flame ionisation detection confirmed GLA retention of 93.1%, 91.4%, and 88.8% at 150, 170, and 190°C respectively. Malondialdehyde equivalents determined by TBARS after 56 days at 37°C showed significantly lower oxidation rates at 150°C inlet temperature. The study concludes that minimising thermal exposure during drying is critical for preserving sensitive polyunsaturated fatty acids in whey protein-based matrices.

title: Oxidative stability of encapsulated chia seed oil in protein–polysaccharide matrices under accelerated storage conditions
abstract: Chia seed oil, containing approximately 64% α-linolenic acid, was encapsulated by spray drying in three wall material combinations: whey protein isolate (WPI) alone, WPI with maltodextrin DE 18 at a 1:1 ratio, and WPI with gum arabic at a 1:1 ratio. Core-to-wall ratio was fixed at 1:4 (w/w). Encapsulation efficiency ranged from 85.4% (WPI alone) to 93.6% (WPI–maltodextrin). Rancimat induction periods at 80°C were 4.1, 6.8, and 5.9 hours for the three matrices respectively. After 90 days at 25°C and 57% relative humidity, conjugated diene values were lowest in the WPI–maltodextrin treatment. Particle size distributions showed monomodal profiles with volume-weighted mean diameters between 10 and 18 μm. The results confirm that the combination of film-forming protein and a high-molecular-weight polysaccharide filler substantially reduces interfacial oxygen permeability compared with protein alone.

title: Cold-pressed hemp seed oil: physicochemical characterisation and fatty acid profile as a function of cultivar and harvest year
abstract: Three hemp cultivars (Fedora 17, Tiborszállás, and a locally bred line designated NS-H3) grown in Vojvodina over two consecutive harvest years were cold-pressed and characterised for their physicochemical properties and fatty acid composition. Oil yield ranged from 28.3% to 31.7% (dry weight basis). All cultivars showed omega-6 to omega-3 ratios between 2.8:1 and 3.4:1, close to nutritional recommendations. Linoleic acid (C18:2n-6) constituted 54–57% and α-linolenic acid (C18:3n-3) 16–19% of total fatty acids as determined by GC-FID after transmethylation. Tocopherol content measured by HPLC-FLD varied significantly between cultivars (p < 0.01), with NS-H3 yielding the highest γ-tocopherol (68 mg/100 g oil). Phospholipid content (0.12–0.19%) and free fatty acid values (0.4–0.8%) were within accepted cold-pressed quality ranges. Harvest year had a smaller effect than cultivar on most parameters. These data provide baseline information for selecting hemp oil batches with consistent composition for subsequent encapsulation studies.

title: Spray drying of hemp seed oil emulsions: effect of whey protein–maltodextrin ratio on powder flowability and encapsulation efficiency
abstract: Cold-pressed hemp seed oil was emulsified at a 30% (w/w) oil load in aqueous solutions of whey protein isolate and maltodextrin (DE 10) at mass ratios of 1:1, 1:2, 1:3, and 1:4, maintaining total wall material concentration at 20% (w/v). Emulsions were spray-dried at an inlet temperature of 165°C. Encapsulation efficiency increased from 87.2% at a 1:1 ratio to a maximum of 94.5% at 1:3, with marginal improvement at 1:4. Powder bulk density increased with maltodextrin content (from 0.31 to 0.47 g/cm³), positively affecting flowability as assessed by the Carr Index. Surface oil, determined by solvent extraction, was lowest (1.8% of total oil) at the 1:3 ratio. X-ray diffraction confirmed amorphous particle structure across all ratios. The 1:3 WPI-to-maltodextrin ratio was identified as the optimum formulation, balancing structural integrity, powder handling properties, and protection of the omega-3 fraction during drying.

title: In vitro bioaccessibility of omega-3 fatty acids from spray-dried hemp seed oil microcapsules using a static three-phase digestion model
abstract: Spray-dried hemp seed oil microcapsules prepared in a whey protein isolate–maltodextrin (1:3) matrix were subjected to a static in vitro digestion protocol comprising oral, gastric, and intestinal phases according to a standardised INFOGEST procedure adapted for lipid analysis. Free fatty acid (FFA) release was monitored by pH-stat titration during the intestinal phase. Bioaccessibility of α-linolenic acid (ALA) was 61.3 ± 3.7% from microcapsules compared with 74.8 ± 4.1% from bulk (unencapsulated) oil, indicating partial protection of the wall matrix against lipase action. Lipolysis rate constants determined by first-order kinetic modelling were 0.041 and 0.063 min⁻¹ for encapsulated and bulk oil respectively. Micellar incorporation efficiency determined by ultracentrifugation was 48.2% for encapsulated and 56.9% for bulk oil. The protein matrix partially resisted pepsin digestion, slowing gastric lipid release, while pancreatin hydrolysis in the intestinal phase recovered the majority of FFA. These data demonstrate acceptable ALA bioaccessibility with the trade-off of somewhat reduced release kinetics.

title: Antioxidant capacity of whey protein–maltodextrin microcapsules loaded with hemp seed oil: DPPH, ABTS and FRAP comparisons before and after simulated digestion
abstract: This paper reports the antioxidant capacity of spray-dried hemp seed oil microcapsules measured by three complementary assays (DPPH radical scavenging, ABTS decolorisation, and FRAP ferric-reducing antioxidant power) before and after a simulated gastrointestinal digestion sequence. The wall material at WPI:maltodextrin ratios of 1:2 and 1:3 was tested at an oil load of 25 and 35% (w/w). Before digestion, DPPH inhibition ranged from 42 to 58%, with higher values at greater oil load. After simulated digestion, antioxidant capacity increased substantially (DPPH 61–79%), attributed to the release of bioactive peptides from whey protein during enzymatic hydrolysis and the simultaneous liberation of tocopherols from the oil fraction. The 1:3 ratio at 25% oil load showed the best combination of pre-digestion protection and post-digestion activity. These findings suggest the WPI–maltodextrin wall contributes an intrinsic antioxidant function beyond mechanical protection of the encapsulated oil.

title: Comparative performance of maltodextrin grades (DE 6, DE 12, DE 18) as co-wall materials with whey protein isolate in hemp oil spray drying: structural, thermal and oxidative outcomes
abstract: Three maltodextrin grades differing in dextrose equivalent (DE 6, DE 12, DE 18) were combined with whey protein isolate at a constant 1:3 ratio (WPI:MD) to encapsulate cold-pressed hemp seed oil at 30% core load by spray drying at 165°C inlet temperature. Differential scanning calorimetry revealed glass transition temperatures (Tg) of 78.4, 62.1, and 51.7°C for DE 6, DE 12, and DE 18 powders respectively. Higher Tg correlated with lower surface oil content (2.1, 3.4, and 5.6% respectively) and slower primary oxidation rates at 40°C. Encapsulation efficiency was highest with DE 6 (95.1%) and lowest with DE 18 (91.8%). In vitro bioaccessibility of ALA was inversely related to Tg, with DE 18 samples showing the highest FFA release (68.2%) during the simulated intestinal phase due to faster matrix dissolution. These opposing trends between oxidative protection and bioaccessibility with increasing DE value present a formulation trade-off that must be resolved based on the intended application.

title: Effect of lecithin addition on emulsion droplet size, surface coverage, and oxidative stability of spray-dried hemp seed oil in WPI–maltodextrin matrices
abstract: Sunflower lecithin was added at 0, 0.5, 1.0, and 1.5% (w/w, on emulsion basis) to hemp seed oil emulsions prepared in a WPI:maltodextrin DE 12 (1:3) wall system before spray drying at 165°C. Emulsion droplet diameter (d₃₂) decreased from 1.87 μm (no lecithin) to 0.94 μm at 1.0% lecithin addition, with no significant further reduction at 1.5%. Zeta potential became more negative with lecithin addition (from −24.7 to −38.2 mV), improving colloidal stability of the feed emulsion. Encapsulation efficiency improved from 93.2 to 96.8% at 1.0% lecithin. Rancimat induction periods at 80°C increased from 5.9 hours to 8.4 hours with 1.0% lecithin, while TBARS values at week 12 (40°C storage) were 1.8-fold lower relative to the lecithin-free control. In vitro bioaccessibility of ALA at 1.0% lecithin (67.4%) was higher than the control (61.3%), attributed to enhanced micellarisation facilitated by the phospholipid fraction during intestinal digestion.

title: Stability of encapsulated hemp seed oil in functional fermented milk beverages: pH-driven wall matrix swelling and lipid oxidation during 28-day refrigerated storage
abstract: Spray-dried hemp seed oil microcapsules (WPI:maltodextrin 1:3, 1.0% lecithin) were incorporated at 2% (w/w) into a fermented milk beverage (pH 4.2, titratable acidity 0.8%) produced with a commercial Lactobacillus acidophilus–Bifidobacterium longum co-culture. Microcapsule integrity, lipid oxidation markers, and ALA content were assessed on days 0, 7, 14, and 28 of refrigerated storage at 4°C. Confocal laser scanning microscopy with Nile Red staining showed progressive swelling and partial surface cracking of the protein matrix below pH 4.5, with visible oil release by day 14. Despite matrix disruption, ALA retention remained above 90% through day 28, attributed to the reducing environment of the fermented medium and the presence of lactic acid bacteria-derived antioxidant metabolites. Peroxide values in the beverage increased from 0.9 to 3.4 mEq O₂/kg fat by day 28, remaining within acceptable limits. These results indicate that WPI-based microcapsules require acid-resistant coating for long-term application in fermented dairy matrices.

title: Accelerated migration testing of triacetin from cellulose acetate films at elevated temperatures and its prediction at 4 °C refrigeration conditions
abstract: Triacetin is used as a plasticiser in cellulose acetate films applied to fresh pasta and soft-ripened cheese packaging. Accelerated migration tests were conducted at 40, 50, and 60 °C into ethanol 50% v/v simulant to predict migration at 4 °C refrigeration temperature via time–temperature superposition. Migration was quantified by GC-FID at 1, 3, 7, 14, and 28 days. The apparent activation energy derived from an Arrhenius fit was 54.7 kJ/mol, in agreement with literature values for small polar molecules in cellulose acetate. Predicted migration at 4 °C over 21 days (shelf life scenario) was 1.9 mg/dm², well below the specific migration limit. Uncertainty propagation from temperature measurement error (±0.5 °C) contributed ±12% to the 4 °C prediction. The study validates the use of accelerated protocols for low-temperature packaging applications and quantifies the prediction uncertainty explicitly, which is often omitted in compliance studies.

title: Simultaneous HPLC-DAD quantification of seven antioxidant additives in fatty food simulants extracted from complex multilayer snack-food packaging
abstract: Multilayer oriented polypropylene (OPP)/metallised OPP/polyethylene laminates used for potato crisps and extruded snacks typically contain mixtures of phenolic antioxidants and processing stabilisers in several layers. A reversed-phase HPLC-DAD method for simultaneous determination of BHT, BHA, AO-1076, AO-1010, AO-168, Tinuvin-P analogue, and DSTDP in isooctane fatty simulant was developed and validated. Linearity (R² > 0.999), limits of detection (0.01–0.08 mg/L), repeatability (RSD < 4.5%), and matrix spike recovery (92–107%) were established according to SANTE/11312/2021 guidelines. Migration experiments at 25 °C, 40 °C, and 60 °C over 14 days showed that BHT was the dominant migrant at all temperatures, reaching 3.2 mg/kg at 60 °C, while thioester DSTDP remained below the LOD across all conditions. The method is directly transferable to regulatory compliance laboratories and requires only standard HPLC instrumentation, making it accessible to routine testing facilities in the region.

title: Tabu Search Heuristics for the Heterogeneous Workforce Scheduling Problem
abstract: We describe a tabu search framework for constructing and improving feasible schedules for a heterogeneous workforce consisting of employees with partially overlapping skill sets. The problem arises in a light-manufacturing context where tasks require combinations of up to three certified competencies and must be completed within narrow time windows over a 28-day horizon. The benchmark set comprises 15 instances ranging from 30 to 120 employees, generated from anonymised data provided by an industrial partner in the Novi Sad economic zone. The tabu search uses a compound neighbourhood that combines shift swaps, skill-reassignment moves, and day-off exchanges. A frequency-based long-term memory component was included to diversify the search after prolonged stagnation. Computational experiments show that the heuristic finds solutions within 2.1% of a known lower bound on average across all instances, with a worst-case gap of 5.8%. Run times remain below 90 seconds on a standard desktop processor for instances with up to 120 employees.

title: Machine-Learning-Assisted Hyperbola Detection in GPR B-Scans for Routine Utility Survey Processing
abstract: Manual interpretation of GPR B-scans is time-consuming and operator-dependent, particularly for large-scale cadastre surveys producing hundreds of radargrams per day. This study trained and tested a convolutional neural network to detect hyperbolic reflections indicative of buried point and linear targets in B-scans collected with 500 MHz and 250 MHz antennas over urban streets in Novi Sad. A labelled dataset of 8,400 B-scan images with 22,310 annotated hyperbolas was assembled from three years of field surveys. The network achieved precision of 0.87 and recall of 0.84 on a held-out test set, outperforming a matched-filter baseline (precision 0.73, recall 0.71). False positive rate was highest for tree root reflections and reinforced concrete slab edges. Integration into a semi-automatic processing pipeline reduced per-radargram interpretation time from an average of 4.2 minutes to 1.1 minutes, with human expert review retained for flagged ambiguous cases. The labelled dataset is made available for benchmarking.

title: Assessing Positional Discrepancies Between As-Built GPR Surveys and Operator GIS Records for Low-Voltage Cable Networks in Vojvodina
abstract: Low-voltage distribution cable networks in Vojvodina were largely installed between 1965 and 1990 and digitised from paper sketches of variable quality. This study quantified positional discrepancies between independent GPR-based cadastre surveys and operator-held GIS records for 47.3 km of low-voltage cable routes across nine settlements of varying population density. A 500 MHz GPR system was used, with RTK-GNSS referencing. Discrepancies were decomposed into horizontal offset, depth-of-burial error and missing-segment rate. Mean horizontal offset was 0.81 m with a 95th percentile of 2.34 m; depth errors averaged 0.24 m. Missing segments constituted 8.4% of total surveyed length. Discrepancy magnitude was significantly correlated with settlement age and with the decade in which original records were created. Rural settlements with records predating 1980 showed missing-segment rates exceeding 15%. Findings support a prioritised re-survey programme targeting pre-1980 rural records.

title: Positioning Buried Electricity Distribution Cables Using RTK-GNSS and Depth Probes: Field Performance in Dense Urban Canyons
abstract: Real-time kinematic GNSS is the standard horizontal positioning method for utility cadastre surveys in Serbia, but signal obstruction in narrow urban streets degrades solution quality. This study evaluated horizontal positioning accuracy of RTK-GNSS for utility location work in three street types in Novi Sad: open boulevards, medium-density streets and narrow historic-centre lanes. A Leica GS18 receiver was used with a national reference network connection. Dilution of precision and fix rate were recorded continuously over 140 survey hours. In narrow lanes, fix rate dropped to 63% and horizontal RMS error increased from 1.7 cm to 9.4 cm. A workflow combining short RTK observation windows with constrained total-station traverses bridging signal gaps reduced the lane-canyon horizontal RMS to 3.8 cm. Depth of burial was measured using a direct-read sonde inserted through existing access points. The combined approach achieved 98% of survey points within the 5 cm horizontal accuracy threshold required by Serbian regulation.

title: Pregled modela zrelosti upravljanja znanjem: primenjivost u javnim preduzećima
abstract: Rad sistematizuje dvadeset i tri modela zrelosti upravljanja znanjem objavljenih između 1997. i 2010. godine i analizira u kojoj meri su prilagođeni specifičnostima javnog sektora. Pregled je izveden primenom protokola za sistematski pregled literature (PRISMA) na bazi Web of Science i Scopus. Kriterijumi za evaluaciju obuhvatali su: broj dimenzija zrelosti, metodu validacije, sektor primene i geografski kontekst. Utvrđeno je da svega četiri modela eksplicitno ciljaju javni sektor, a ni jedan nije testiran u postsocijalističkim institucijama. Rad zaključuje da dominantni okviri pretpostavljaju viši stepen organizacione formalizacije nego što je karakteristično za javna preduzeća u tranziciji, i predlaže set od sedam kriterijuma koje bi budući modeli trebalo da ispune kako bi bili upotrebljivi u tom kontekstu.

title: Tacit Knowledge Retention in Serbian Municipal Administrations: An Exploratory Study
abstract: This paper reports findings from semi-structured interviews conducted with 34 civil servants across six municipalities in Vojvodina between 2010 and 2011. The study examined how tacit knowledge held by long-serving employees is retained when those employees retire or resign, focusing on practices that were established informally during the socialist period and persist without documentation. Interviews were coded in ATLAS.ti using a grounded theory approach; 118 codes were reduced to 14 categories and four core themes. Results indicate that nearly 80 percent of knowledge-retention activity relies on informal mentoring relationships rather than codification or structured handover procedures. Smaller municipalities show higher dependence on single individuals, creating pronounced vulnerability. The paper argues that standard knowledge-transfer instruments derived from private-sector models are poorly suited to the administrative cultures observed, and proposes three context-specific retention mechanisms as starting points for further instrument development.

title: Razvoj instrumenta za dijagnostiku zrelosti upravljanja znanjem u organima lokalne samouprave
abstract: U radu je prikazana procedura razvoja i pilot-testiranja upitničkog instrumenta za procenu zrelosti upravljanja znanjem u organima lokalne samouprave. Instrument se oslanja na petostepeni model zrelosti izveden iz Crawfordovog CMM-I okvira, prilagođenog za postsocijalistički administrativni kontekst. Upitnik sadrži 54 stavke raspoređene u šest dimenzija: strategija znanja, kultura, procesi, tehnologija, merenje i liderstvo. Pilot-testiranje je sprovedeno u deset opština u Srbiji i Severnoj Makedoniji (N = 187 ispitanika). Konfirmatornom faktorskom analizom (CFA) potvrđena je šestofaktorska struktura (CFI = 0,94; RMSEA = 0,061). Cronbachov alfa koeficijent po dimenzijama kretao se od 0,71 do 0,86. Rad sadrži preporuke za dalju primenu instrumenta u regionalnim komparativnim studijama.

title: Organizacione prepreke uvođenja sistema upravljanja znanjem u javnim preduzećima: studija slučaja u energetskom sektoru Srbije
abstract: Rad analizira organizacione prepreke s kojima se suočavaju javna preduzeća u energetskom sektoru pri pokušaju uvođenja formalnih sistema upravljanja znanjem. Studija slučaja sprovedena je u tri javna preduzeća (ukupno 2.100 zaposlenih) primenom kombinovane metodologije: analiza internih dokumenata, posmatranje sa učešćem tokom tri meseca i 22 dubinska intervjua sa menadžerima i stručnjacima. Identifikovano je pet kategorija prepreka: otpor menadžmenta srednje linije, nejasna vlasnička struktura znanja, nedostatak podsticajnih mehanizama, fragmentisani IT sistemi i diskontinuitet strateškog liderstva. Utvrđeno je da prepreke nije moguće razumeti izolovano od specifičnog institucionalnog nasleđa, pre svega od hijerarhijske kulture i kratkih mandata rukovodilaca. Predložen je okvir za prioritizaciju intervencija koji uzima u obzir i resursna ograničenja karakteristična za javna preduzeća u tranziciji.

title: Integrating Knowledge Audit Methods into Public Sector Strategic Planning: Lessons from Two Vojvodina Pilot Projects
abstract: This chapter describes the design and outcomes of two pilot knowledge audits carried out in Vojvodina public institutions in 2016 and 2017 as part of a capacity-building initiative. The first pilot was conducted in a regional development agency (58 employees) and the second in a district administrative office (31 employees). Each audit combined a structured inventory of documented knowledge assets, network analysis of internal expertise flows, and individual competence mapping through a standardised card-sorting exercise. The chapter reports how findings were fed into each institution's three-year strategic plan and identifies the conditions under which audit results were actually used: senior management engagement, a dedicated knowledge coordinator role, and visible quick wins in the first six months. Conditions absent in one of the two pilots are linked to partial non-adoption of recommendations, illustrating the gap between diagnostic capacity and implementation readiness in under-resourced public bodies.

title: Merenje uticaja programa obuke na transfer znanja u opštinskim upravama: pre-post studija
abstract: Rad ispituje u kojoj meri strukturirani programi obuke dovode do merljivog transfera znanja u svakodnevnu praksu opštinskih službenika. Istraživanjem je obuhvaćeno 214 učesnika obuke u jedanaest opština u Srbiji tokom 2018. i 2019. godine. Primenom Kirkpatrickijevog četvorostepenog modela evaluacije, podaci su prikupljani na četiri tačke merenja: neposredno pre, neposredno posle, tri i šest meseci nakon završetka obuke. Instrumenti su uključivali standardizovane testove znanja, procenu nadređenih i analizu administrativnih ishoda (broj procesiranih predmeta, broj grešaka, vreme obrade). Rezultati pokazuju statistički značajan porast u znanju neposredno posle obuke (d = 0,74), ali znatan pad transfera na nivou prakse u šestomesečnom praćenju: samo 31% učesnika primenjivalo je stečene veštine. Kao ključni moderatori identifikovani su podrška neposrednog rukovodioca i prilike za primenu na radnom mestu.

title: Do E-Government Investments Translate into Knowledge Management Capability? Evidence from Serbian Municipalities 2015–2020
abstract: E-government projects are often justified partly on the grounds that digitisation of records and processes will improve organisational knowledge management. This paper tests that claim empirically using panel data from 120 Serbian municipalities over a five-year period. E-government investment levels were drawn from Ministry of Finance budget execution reports; knowledge management capability was operationalised using the six-dimension maturity instrument assessed at the beginning and end of the observation window (N = 720 matched responses from 1,440 municipal civil servants). Fixed-effects regression models show that investment in e-government is positively associated with improvements in the technology and process dimensions of knowledge management maturity (β = 0.28 and 0.21 respectively, both p < 0.01), but shows no significant association with the culture, strategy, or leadership dimensions. The paper argues that technology investment is a necessary but not sufficient condition for organisational knowledge capability, and that current e-government programmes in Serbia are not accompanied by the complementary organisational interventions needed for broader maturity gains.

title: Toward a Revised Maturity Framework for Knowledge Management in Post-Socialist Public Institutions: Theoretical Grounding and Empirical Refinement
abstract: This paper presents the theoretical foundations and empirical refinement of a revised five-level knowledge management maturity framework specifically designed for public institutions in post-socialist contexts. The revision draws on three sources: a critical review of existing frameworks (n = 31); expert consultation with 18 practitioners and academics from Serbia, Slovenia, Hungary, and Romania conducted via Delphi rounds; and item-level analysis of data from 490 respondents across four countries collected between 2019 and 2022. The framework retains six dimensions but reorganises subordinate indicators to reflect characteristics documented in post-socialist institutions: high procedural formalisation coexisting with low strategic coherence; strong interpersonal knowledge networks alongside weak documentation cultures; and recurrent disruption of learning cycles by leadership turnover. Confirmatory factor analysis and multi-group invariance testing across the four national samples support the revised factor structure (CFI = 0.96, RMSEA = 0.054). Implications for benchmarking and capacity-building programmes are discussed.

title: Knowledge Management Maturity and Organisational Resilience During Administrative Disruption: Evidence from Serbian Local Governments During 2020–2021
abstract: This paper examines whether pre-existing knowledge management maturity moderated the organisational resilience of Serbian local governments during the administrative disruptions of 2020–2021, a period combining public health crisis responses with a cycle of local elections. Resilience was operationalised as the ability to maintain service continuity, measured through administrative output indicators drawn from municipal reporting obligations. Knowledge management maturity scores from a 2019 baseline survey (N = 310 civil servants, 38 municipalities) were matched to 2020 and 2021 service output data. Multilevel regression models indicate that municipalities scoring in the top quartile on the leadership and culture dimensions of the maturity instrument maintained statistically higher service output continuity than those in the bottom quartile (difference = 14 percentage points, p < 0.05), controlling for municipality size, budget, and region. The effect was not significant for the technology dimension. Results suggest that relational and cultural aspects of knowledge infrastructure have practical consequences for public service robustness.

title: Multi-Criteria Decision-Making in Agri-food Supply Chains: Methods, Applications, and Open Problems
abstract: This book chapter surveys the application of multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) methods in agri-food supply chain management, with a focus on supplier selection, logistics partner evaluation, and procurement strategy formulation. The review covers studies published between 2005 and 2018 and categorises them by method family—deterministic, fuzzy, grey, stochastic, and hybrid—and by agri-food sector—cereals, dairy, meat, fruit and vegetables, and processed foods. A structured comparison table is provided for 43 reviewed studies, identifying the criteria sets used, the number of alternatives considered, and the data collection approach. The chapter identifies three recurring gaps: the underrepresentation of dynamic decision environments, the limited use of real procurement records as opposed to hypothetical expert judgements, and the near-total absence of post-hoc validation against actual supplier choices. Directions for future research are outlined, including the integration of demand forecast uncertainty and the use of simulation to stress-test supplier rankings.

title: Power-Aware Render-Pass Scheduling for Sustained Performance Under Thermal Throttling on Mobile Devices
abstract: Mobile devices operating under sustained GPU load reach thermal limits within minutes, triggering frequency scaling that reduces throughput by 30–60 %. Render-pass scheduling strategies that reduce peak power can defer throttling onset. We model the power draw of each render-pass type in a deferred rendering pipeline — depth prepass, G-buffer fill, lighting accumulation, post-process — using hardware counters and external current measurement at 1 kHz via a USB power monitor. Based on the model, we implement a scheduler that interleaves high-power and low-power passes to smooth instantaneous power draw without increasing total frame time by more than 2 ms. Tests on a Mali-G615 device running a 10-minute continuous workload show that the scheduler delays throttling onset by a median of 83 seconds and improves sustained frame-rate stability (σ of frame time) by 41 % compared to unmanaged submission order.

title: A Lexicon of Informal Serbian Morphological Variants for NLP Applications
abstract: The paper presents the construction and evaluation of a manually curated lexicon mapping 8,740 informal orthographic variants of Serbian word forms to their standard dictionary entries, along with their morpho-syntactic tags. Source material was drawn from three online registers: sports commentary forums, food review portals, and classified advertisement listings. Variants were identified by comparing tokenised text against a pre-existing standard Serbian morphological dictionary and manually reviewing unmatched tokens. Each entry records the variant form, the canonical lemma, the tag, the source register, and a confidence score based on annotator agreement. An inter-annotator agreement of κ = 0.81 was achieved across two annotators for lemma assignment. The lexicon was released under a CC-BY licence and integrated as an optional module into the Serbian TreeTagger pipeline. Lookup precision on a held-out test set of 1,200 tokens reached 91.3%. The resource is intended to support downstream tasks such as sentiment analysis and named-entity recognition on informal Serbian text.

title: Lexical Borrowing Patterns and Morphological Integration of English Loanwords in Serbian Tech-Sector Short Messages
abstract: This study examines how English loanwords are morphologically integrated in Serbian short messages produced by employees and customers in the information technology sector. A corpus of 7,800 messages was collected from two sources: internal project management tool threads from three IT companies operating in Novi Sad (shared under a data agreement with pseudonymisation) and publicly available technology product review pages. From this corpus, 2,140 loanword tokens were identified and classified according to their degree of morphological integration: unadapted citation forms, partially adapted forms retaining English plural marking, and fully integrated forms inflected according to Serbian nominal or verbal morphology. Results show that 38% of loanword tokens appear in unadapted form, 29% in partial adaptation, and 33% fully integrated. Integration rate correlates significantly with word frequency (Spearman r = 0.62) and with the part of speech, with verbs showing higher integration than nouns. Findings are discussed in relation to contact linguistics and as practical guidance for building normalization rules for Serbian tech-domain NLP pipelines.

title: Thermal Modelling of IGBT Power Modules in Railway Applications
abstract: This book chapter provides a systematic treatment of thermal modelling approaches for IGBT power modules deployed in railway traction inverters, covering one-dimensional RC network models, compact multi-port thermal models, and the boundary conditions appropriate for vehicle-mounted cooling systems. The chapter discusses how load profile characteristics specific to urban, suburban, and mainline rail services translate into distinct thermal cycling regimes and how these regimes affect solder-layer and bond-wire lifetime. Parameter extraction from thermal transient measurements is described step by step, and worked numerical examples using a 1200 V / 600 A half-bridge module are included. Interactions between thermal model fidelity and lifetime prediction accuracy are analysed quantitatively. The chapter is aimed at practising engineers in railway rolling-stock development who need to select or validate thermal models without access to specialised simulation tools.

title: A Taint-Guided Fuzzer for Discovering Memory Corruption in UPnP Service Handlers of Embedded Devices
abstract: UPnP service handlers in embedded devices parse complex XML-encoded SOAP messages and are historically prone to memory corruption. We present TaintFuzz, a grey-box fuzzer that uses dynamic taint analysis to identify which bytes of a UPnP SOAP request influence memory allocation sizes and buffer copy lengths inside the service handler binary. Taint-labelled byte offsets are fed back to the mutation engine as high-priority mutation targets, focusing energy on inputs that reach dangerous data-flow paths. TaintFuzz was compared against AFL++, Boofuzz, and a random baseline on 12 UPnP-enabled firmware images running under QEMU. TaintFuzz achieved a mean unique crash rate 2.3 times higher than AFL++ and 4.7 times higher than Boofuzz within a four-hour campaign per target. Seventeen previously unreported memory corruption bugs were found across eight firmware images; six were assessed as reachable from the local network without authentication. Proof-of-concept payloads were shared with affected vendors under a 90-day disclosure policy.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Predicting Judgment Outcomes: A Feasibility Study on Serbian Case Law
abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems combine a retrieval component with a generative model and have been applied to question answering in several legal jurisdictions, but their use for outcome prediction on small corpora remains unexplored. This preprint describes a feasibility study in which a dense retrieval index is built from 1,840 Serbian civil court decisions and used to condition a fine-tuned sequence-to-sequence model on retrieved precedents at inference time. Three retrieval configurations—BM25, dense passage retrieval with a multilingual encoder, and a hybrid combination—are compared on a 200-instance test set. The hybrid configuration achieves the highest accuracy (0.71) and macro F1 (0.63), compared to 0.65 and 0.57 for the no-retrieval baseline. Analysis of retrieved documents shows that recency and jurisdictional tier of retrieved cases are positively associated with prediction correctness. The study flags limitations arising from incomplete metadata and inconsistent anonymisation in the source corpus.

title: Open-Source Real-Time Target Benchmarking for Automotive HIL: A Five-Year Longitudinal Study
abstract: This paper presents a longitudinal comparison of open-source real-time platforms evaluated in the authors' laboratory between 2019 and 2024, updating earlier single-point benchmarks with data from newer hardware generations and kernel versions. Platforms assessed include x86 mini-ITX systems, Raspberry Pi 3 and 4, Beaglebone AI-64, and Xilinx Zynq UltraScale+ MPSoC. For each platform, worst-case and mean task latency, model execution capacity (maximum state count at 1 ms step), CAN frame throughput, and approximate acquisition cost are tabulated. The dataset covers 14 440 individual measurement sessions totalling over 12 000 bench-hours. Results show that the Zynq UltraScale+ with a Xenomai partition achieves the best latency-to-cost ratio for step sizes at or above 0.5 ms, while x86 platforms retain an advantage for large model complexity. The paper identifies kernel version transitions and hardware errata that caused discontinuities in the latency data and documents the workarounds applied. All raw data and measurement scripts are provided in a public repository.

title: Forced Heirship in Socialist Yugoslavia: Legislative Origins and Doctrinal Foundations
abstract: This article traces the legislative history of compulsory share provisions in Yugoslav succession law from the enactment of the 1955 Law on Inheritance through the constitutional reforms of the 1970s. Drawing on parliamentary records, published commentaries, and doctrinal writings of the period, the study identifies three distinct rationales that shaped the Yugoslav forced heirship model: socialist redistribution ideology, protection of surviving dependants, and continuity with pre-war civil law traditions inherited from the Kingdom of Yugoslavia. The article maps how each rationale was weighted differently across the six republics and argues that the resulting normative compromise—generous reserved portions combined with broad testamentary discretion over the freely disposable share—was inherently unstable and became a source of litigation after 1990. The analysis provides a baseline for subsequent comparative work on post-1990 reforms in successor states. Sources include the Official Gazette of the SFRY for the period 1945–1990 and selected first-instance court decisions published in regional law reviews.

title: The Serbian Law on Inheritance of 1995: A Reform Interrupted
abstract: Serbia's 1995 Law on Inheritance was enacted during a period of acute political and economic instability, and this article examines how that context limited the scope of reform. Using a combination of legislative history analysis and structured comparison with the contemporaneous Hungarian and Croatian inheritance statutes, the study shows that Serbian lawmakers retained the socialist-era reserved portion of one-half for close relatives with only minor adjustments to the class of protected heirs. The article reconstructs the parliamentary debate through stenographic records and identifies three failed amendment proposals that would have introduced greater testamentary freedom. It further documents how notarial practitioners in Vojvodina adapted contract-based instruments—particularly the contract on lifetime maintenance—to achieve outcomes that strict testamentary rules did not permit. Forty-three published notarial decisions from the period 1996–2008 are coded and analysed. The article concludes that the 1995 law represents a missed opportunity for deeper liberalisation and sets out criteria for evaluating any future reform.

title: Testamentary Freedom and Its Limits: A Comparative Survey of Seven Post-Socialist Central European Jurisdictions
abstract: This book chapter presents a structured comparative analysis of testamentary freedom rules in Bulgaria, Croatia, the Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland, Serbia, and Slovenia as of 2012. For each jurisdiction the chapter identifies: the size of the freely disposable share, the categories of heirs entitled to a forced portion, the legal consequences of violation, and mechanisms available to reduce or waive the forced share by agreement. Data were collected from primary legislation, constitutional court decisions, and academic commentaries in the respective national languages. The chapter finds that the seven countries cluster into two broad groups: those that retained large compulsory shares broadly comparable to the socialist baseline (Bulgaria, Serbia) and those that reduced or restructured forced heirship to emphasise claims-based rather than automatic share entitlement (Czech Republic, Hungary post-2013 draft). The chapter also notes a common trend across all jurisdictions toward expanded recognition of freedom of testation for childless testators. The analysis is intended as a reference tool for law reform commissions and comparative law scholars.

title: Disinheritance Clauses in Serbian Wills: An Empirical Study of Notarial Records 2000–2015
abstract: Serbian law permits testators to exclude compulsory heirs from the estate only on grounds expressly listed in the Civil Code, including serious criminal offences against the testator and deliberate failure to provide support. This article reports findings from a systematic review of 318 notarised wills deposited with four notary offices in Novi Sad and Subotica between 2000 and 2015 in which a disinheritance clause was present. The study codes each clause according to the stated ground, the kinship category of the disinherited heir, the estimated estate size, and whether the clause was subsequently challenged in contentious proceedings. Key findings: 71 per cent of disinheritance clauses cited lack of contact rather than a legally recognised ground, rendering them formally invalid; only 23 per cent of challenged clauses were ultimately upheld by first-instance courts; clauses targeting children were challenged at twice the rate of those targeting siblings. The article argues that the narrow statutory grounds for disinheritance are out of step with contemporary family structures and recommends a reform that introduces a general estrangement ground, as has been adopted in Austria and the Czech Republic after 2015.

title: The Austrian Succession Law Reform of 2015: Lessons for South-Eastern European Jurisdictions
abstract: Austria's Erbrechts-Änderungsgesetz 2015 introduced the most substantial revision of Austrian succession law since 1811, including a reduced and claims-based forced share, an estrangement ground for disinheritance, and new rules on gifts made during the testator's lifetime. This article examines the reform in detail and evaluates its potential as a model for South-Eastern European countries that retain the older forced heirship structure. The analysis proceeds in three stages: a doctrinal exposition of the Austrian changes; a structured comparison with Serbian, Croatian, and Slovenian rules; and an assessment of the socio-economic preconditions—especially pension system coverage and elderly care arrangements—that condition the feasibility of reducing forced shares. The article draws on Austrian parliamentary materials, the official explanatory memorandum, and published commentary by Viennese notarial practitioners. The conclusion is that a claims-based model is technically compatible with Serbian private law doctrine but would require simultaneous reform of elder care legislation to avoid adverse welfare effects for elderly parents.

title: Pact on Future Succession in Serbian Private Law: Prohibition, Circumvention, and Reform Prospects
abstract: Serbian law, following the socialist civil law tradition, prohibits contracts concerning a living person's future estate. This prohibition, enshrined in Article 102 of the 1995 Law on Inheritance, is subject to only one narrow exception: the contract on lifetime maintenance. This article maps the scope of the prohibition through an analysis of 87 published Supreme Court of Cassation and appellate court decisions issued between 1996 and 2020. It documents recurring patterns of circumvention through sale-of-future-claim agreements, gift instruments with reversion clauses, and mixed-type contracts. The article then examines the progressive relaxation of the prohibition in German, Austrian, and Czech law and assesses whether a limited admission of succession pacts—covering only spousal agreements and family business transfers—would be compatible with the Serbian constitutional framework and with EU succession regulation No. 650/2012. A draft statutory provision is proposed and its implications for forced heirship protection are assessed. The study relies on doctrinal analysis and comparative legal method; no primary empirical data were collected.

title: Cross-Border Succession in the Western Balkans: Jurisdictional Conflicts and the Reach of EU Regulation 650/2012
abstract: EU Succession Regulation 650/2012 applies to the estates of EU citizens dying after August 2015 but does not bind non-member states. For decedents with assets in both EU member states and Western Balkan non-member states (Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia), the regulation creates asymmetric conflict-of-law outcomes. This conference paper analyses three categories of recurring conflict: (i) characterisation disputes over whether a deceased's habitual residence was in an EU state or in Serbia; (ii) forced heirship renvoi problems when the applicable law points to Serbian law but the estate includes immovable property in Hungary or Croatia; and (iii) recognition of European Certificates of Succession in Serbian administrative proceedings. The paper draws on 14 interview transcripts with notaries practising in Subotica, Sombor, and Kikinda—border areas with a high incidence of cross-border estates—supplemented by documentary analysis. The paper recommends that Serbia conclude bilateral succession treaties with Hungary and Croatia as an interim measure pending potential EU accession.

title: Testamentary Capacity and Cognitive Decline: Medical Evidence in Serbian Inheritance Litigation
abstract: Challenges to testamentary capacity on grounds of dementia or other cognitive impairment have become more frequent in Serbian courts as the population ages. This article examines 102 first-instance judgments from Novi Sad, Subotica, and Zrenjanin basic courts issued between 2010 and 2021 in which testamentary capacity was contested. Using content analysis, the study maps what categories of medical evidence were presented, how courts weighted psychiatric expert reports against earlier notarial assessments of capacity, and what the outcome distribution was across different dementia diagnoses. Findings show that psychiatric expert testimony was determinative in 68 per cent of cases; courts relied exclusively on the notarial record in only 9 per cent. Will invalidation rates were substantially higher (58 per cent) for holographic wills than for notarial wills (22 per cent). The article evaluates these patterns against comparative standards applied in Austrian and German courts and proposes procedural guidelines for Serbian notaries examining elderly testators.

title: Family Business Succession in Serbia: Gaps in Private Law and Practical Workarounds
abstract: Succession to small and medium-sized family businesses in Serbia is poorly served by the existing inheritance and company law framework. This article identifies four structural gaps: the prohibition on succession pacts, the absence of business continuation agreements, the mandatory equal division among forced heirs, and the lack of estate administration procedures suited to ongoing business assets. The analysis draws on 27 semi-structured interviews with business owners, notaries, and lawyers in Vojvodina conducted between 2019 and 2021, combined with a review of legislative materials and comparative examples from Slovenia (2019 Companies Act amendments) and Hungary (2013 Civil Code provisions on business succession). The interview data reveal that practitioners routinely combine lifetime gift contracts, company share restructuring, and loan agreements to simulate the economic outcome of prohibited succession pacts. The article evaluates these workarounds against the forced heirship rules and argues that reform of both succession law and company law is needed simultaneously. A legislative agenda is outlined, with reference to the EU Commission's 2006 Recommendation on business transfers.

title: The Reserved Share as a Percentage: Comparing Quantum Rules Across Twelve European Jurisdictions
abstract: This article compiles and compares the quantitative dimension of forced heirship across twelve European jurisdictions: Austria, Bulgaria, Croatia, Czech Republic, France, Germany, Hungary, Poland, Romania, Serbia, Slovakia, and Slovenia. For each country the article records the current statutory fraction of the estate reserved for each category of heir, the treatment of inter vivos gifts in the calculation base, and the procedural mechanism through which a shortfall is remedied (automatic reduction, personal claim, or action for supplement). Data were drawn from current legislation, official legal databases, and published academic commentaries, all verified as of January 2024. The article constructs a comparative index of restrictiveness that ranks the twelve systems and finds that Serbia and Romania rank as the most restrictive, while Germany and the Czech Republic rank as least restrictive among the sampled group. The index controls for differences in gift claw-back rules and debtor-protection exemptions. The article does not advocate a particular reform direction but provides a reference tool intended to be used in policy discussions.

title: Succession Law Reform and the Serbian Civil Code Project: An Assessment of the 2023 Draft Provisions
abstract: The Serbian Ministry of Justice's ongoing Civil Code drafting project published succession law provisions in a consultative draft in late 2022. This article provides a systematic assessment of those provisions against the background of the existing 1995 Law on Inheritance, the comparative literature, and the results of empirical research conducted by the author over the preceding decade. The draft introduces three significant changes: a reduction of the reserved share for descendants from one-half to one-third of the intestate share; a new estrangement ground for disinheritance; and a limited recognition of succession pacts between spouses for the matrimonial home. The article evaluates each change for internal consistency, alignment with EU succession regulation requirements, and adequacy of transitional provisions. It identifies six ambiguities in the draft text that are likely to generate litigation and proposes specific textual corrections. The analysis is based on the published draft, the explanatory memorandum, and comparative material from Austria, Croatia, and the Czech Republic.

title: Digital Assets in Post-Socialist Succession Law: Conceptual Problems and Preliminary Observations
abstract: The inheritance of digital assets—cryptocurrency holdings, online business accounts, subscription services, and social media profiles—raises questions that post-socialist civil codes were not designed to answer. This preprint surveys the existing legal framework in Serbia, Croatia, and Hungary and identifies three structural difficulties: the characterisation of digital assets as property within civil law categories, the evidentiary challenge of locating and accessing assets whose existence may be unknown to heirs, and the interaction between platform terms of service and forced heirship rules where the platform operates under a foreign governing law. The paper draws on published court decisions from Germany and the United States, guidance documents from notarial associations in Austria and France, and 12 interviews with IT lawyers and notaries in Novi Sad and Zagreb conducted in 2024–2025. The paper is framed as a problem survey rather than a conclusions article; it is intended to inform an ongoing legislative working group convened by the Faculty of Law, University of Novi Sad. Comments are invited before final submission.

title: Autonomous Systems in Construction Contracts: Risk Allocation and Supervision Duties
abstract: Automated construction management systems increasingly control scheduling, procurement, and quality monitoring on large infrastructure projects in Serbia. This article examines how the standard FIDIC contract forms and Serbian construction law allocate risk when these systems produce erroneous outputs leading to cost overruns or defects. The analysis covers three anonymised construction disputes from the period 2018–2022 involving infrastructure projects on the Corridor 10 and Corridor 11 road networks. Using a doctrinal method supplemented by structured interviews with five construction law practitioners, the article maps the duty of supervision under Serbian construction regulations against the outputs of automated project management tools. It finds that existing contractual risk matrices do not adequately address situations where no human reviewer checked an automated recommendation before it was acted upon, and proposes model contractual language for future procurements.

title: The EU AI Act and Serbian Contract Law: Liability Consequences of High-Risk AI System Classification
abstract: The EU AI Act (2024) introduces a risk-based classification of AI systems and imposes conformity obligations on providers and deployers, with high-risk systems facing the most stringent requirements. This article examines how the obligations of deployers of high-risk AI systems under the AI Act interact with contractual liability toward affected natural persons under Serbian law in the context of Serbian EU accession negotiations. The author analyses the supply chain of obligations from AI provider to deployer to end user, and identifies three contract law problems: (i) how deployer conformity obligations translate into implied contractual terms; (ii) whether non-conformity constitutes a breach giving rise to damages claims by contractual partners; and (iii) how limitation clauses in provider–deployer agreements will be assessed for validity. The article uses a hypothetical case study involving an HR screening platform deployed by a Serbian employer and traces liability pathways for a rejected job applicant.

title: Co-Ownership of Common Parts in Multi-Unit Buildings: A Comparative Analysis of Serbian and Croatian Legislation
abstract: This article examines the statutory frameworks governing co-ownership of common parts in multi-unit residential buildings in Serbia and Croatia, focusing on the period following the adoption of Serbia's Law on Housing and Building Maintenance (2016) and Croatia's Ownership and Other Real Rights Act. The study employs doctrinal legal analysis and comparative methodology, drawing on primary legislative texts, commentary literature, and selected case law from both jurisdictions. Eighteen cases from Serbian municipal courts and twelve from Croatian county courts were reviewed to identify patterns in judicial interpretation of proportional share calculations and maintenance cost allocation. Results indicate significant divergence in how the two systems define the boundaries of exclusive versus common ownership, particularly regarding load-bearing structures, roof surfaces, and basement utility rooms. The article argues that the Serbian framework's reliance on building area ratios creates practical difficulties when buildings contain mixed residential and commercial units, and it proposes clarifying amendments modelled partly on the Croatian approach.

title: Frequency-Domain Analysis of Load Buffering Effectiveness in Supercapacitor–Battery Hybrids for Variable-Speed Compressor Drives
abstract: Variable-speed compressor drives present a load spectrum with energy concentrated at the fundamental switching frequency of the drive (typically 20–100 Hz mechanical cycles) and at lower frequencies corresponding to pressure regulation dynamics. This paper quantifies the load buffering effectiveness of a supercapacitor–battery hybrid using power spectral density analysis of battery current before and after hybrid insertion under different control bandwidths. A 3 kW compressor drive was operated under pressure-cycling conditions reproducing a refrigeration duty cycle on a test bench. Spectral analysis of battery current showed that a 600 F supercapacitor bank inserted with a cut-off frequency of 0.2 Hz reduces battery current spectral power in the 0.2–5 Hz band by 14 dB and in the 5–50 Hz band by more than 22 dB. The relationship between cut-off frequency and harmonic distortion factor of battery current is characterised, and a design guideline for selecting the cut-off frequency as a function of dominant load cycle frequency is derived.

title: Pretraga u realnom vremenu nad tokom vesti na srpskom jeziku s mešovitim pismom
abstract: Sistemi za pretragu u realnom vremenu nad tokovima vesti zahtevaju inkrementalno ažuriranje indeksa s niskim kašnjenjem. Kada tok vesti dolazi iz više izvora koji koriste različita pisma, inkrementalni indekser mora da normalizuje pismo svake pristigle stavke pre umetanja. Ovaj rad opisuje arhitekturu sistema koji obrađuje do 1 200 novinskih članaka u minuti, sa prosečnim kašnjenjem indeksiranja od 340 ms na jednom serverskom čvoru s 16 jezgara. Normalizacija pisma i fonemska kanonizacija implementirane su kao paraleln cevovod koji dodaje manje od 15% vremenske cene u odnosu na sistem bez normalizacije. Evaluacija preciznosti pretrage sprovedena je na simuliranom toku od 2,1 miliona članaka prikupljenih tokom 30 dana. Sistem je prilagodljiv i može se horizontalno skalirati dodavanjem čvorova za normalizaciju nezavisno od čvorova za indeksiranje.

title: Evaluating Pretrained Multilingual Embeddings for Mixed-Script Serbian Document Retrieval
abstract: Pretrained multilingual transformer models encode text at the subword level and might be expected to handle script variation implicitly, since their vocabularies cover both Serbian scripts. This paper measures to what extent this expectation holds in practice. We fine-tuned three publicly available multilingual models of different sizes on SrMIR-1, the mixed-script Serbian retrieval benchmark, and compared their nDCG@10 scores against a script-normalizing BM25 baseline and a hybrid model. Without fine-tuning, the multilingual models rank below the BM25 baseline on mixed-script queries. After fine-tuning on 12 000 query–passage pairs, the best model reaches nDCG@10 of 0.601, above the hybrid BM25 baseline of 0.587. However, for queries and documents that mix scripts within a single sentence, fine-tuned models underperform by up to 9 percentage points relative to their performance on single-script inputs, indicating that subword tokenization does not fully resolve the alignment problem. We release the fine-tuning splits and evaluation scripts.

title: Semantic Heterogeneity in Serbian Public Procurement Notices: An Empirical Analysis
abstract: This study examines the degree of semantic heterogeneity present in machine-readable procurement notices published on the Serbian Public Procurement Portal between 2008 and 2011. A corpus of 18 340 notices was parsed and their textual fields tokenised and lemmatised using a custom Serbian-language NLP pipeline. Cluster analysis identified 214 terminological clusters with overlapping intended meanings but inconsistent labelling, particularly in works and services categories. The paper quantifies homonymy and synonymy rates per procurement category and correlates heterogeneity scores with contracting authority type (ministry, local government, public enterprise). Local government notices exhibit the highest heterogeneity index (0.71 on a 0–1 scale) compared to ministries (0.44). Findings provide an empirical baseline for ontology normalisation efforts and suggest that mandatory use of a reference vocabulary would reduce ambiguity in approximately 62 % of problematic notice fields.
