title: Mutation Operators for Finite State Machine Specifications of Embedded Control Software
abstract: This paper defines a catalogue of 18 mutation operators tailored to finite state machine (FSM) specifications commonly used in embedded control firmware. Operators cover state deletion, transition guard modification, action substitution, and reset-condition negation. An experiment was conducted on four open-source microcontroller firmware projects totalling approximately 14,000 lines of C code. Mutants were seeded automatically using a custom Python tool, and an existing hand-written test suite was used as the baseline oracle. Mutation scores ranged from 41% to 67% across the four subjects, revealing systematic gaps in transition coverage. The paper reports the proportion of equivalent mutants identified through static analysis (approximately 12% of all seeded mutants) and discusses the effort required for manual equivalence classification. The results motivate the need for specification-driven test generation rather than ad hoc test suite growth.

title: Deriving Test Suites from UML Statecharts: A Comparison of Three Path-Selection Strategies
abstract: Model-based test generation from UML statecharts can follow different path-selection criteria, each yielding test suites of different size and fault-detection capability. This study compares all-transitions, all-transition-pairs, and boundary-interior path selection applied to a set of seven industrial-scale statechart models provided by a regional automotive supplier. Models ranged from 12 to 89 states and 18 to 204 transitions. Test cases were generated automatically and executed against seeded mutation faults. All-transition-pairs coverage detected 14% more mutants on average compared with all-transitions, while increasing test suite size by a factor of 3.1. Boundary-interior selection offered a middle ground but showed inconsistent results across subjects. Execution times on target hardware were measured to assess whether suite sizes remain feasible under real-time constraints. The paper recommends a hybrid strategy that applies all-transition-pairs only to safety-critical subsystems and all-transitions elsewhere.

title: Automated Regression Test Selection for Firmware After Incremental Source Changes
abstract: Regression testing of embedded firmware is expensive because full test suite execution on hardware targets can take hours. This paper presents a lightweight change-impact analysis technique that identifies which tests in an existing suite are affected by a given firmware patch without requiring full re-execution. The method instruments the firmware binary at basic-block granularity to record coverage during an initial full run, then uses static call-graph differencing to predict which blocks are reachable from changed functions. On a dataset of 120 patches drawn from the version history of three open-source firmware projects, the technique retained on average 31% of the original test suite while missing 2.1% of fault-detecting tests. False negative rates are characterised per patch type. The implementation is released as a set of scripts wrapping GCC and a custom binary instrumentation tool. Practical integration into a continuous integration pipeline is described.

title: Contract-Based Specification of Interrupt-Driven Firmware for Model-Based Test Generation
abstract: Interrupt-driven firmware presents challenges for model-based testing because interleaving of interrupt service routines (ISRs) with the main execution thread produces combinatorial state spaces. This paper proposes a contract language, IFContract, that allows engineers to annotate ISR entry and exit conditions, shared-variable invariants, and timing constraints using a syntax embedded in C comments. A parser translates annotations into an extended FSM representation. Test cases covering pairwise ISR–main-thread interactions are generated from this model. The approach was evaluated on firmware for a battery management unit implemented on an ARM Cortex-M4 microcontroller. The generated suite comprised 147 test cases and detected all 38 manually seeded interface faults. Compared with a randomly generated suite of the same size, the model-based suite found 23% more faults. Annotation effort was measured at 2.3 lines of contract per 10 lines of ISR code on average.

title: Model-Based Testing for Embedded Systems
abstract: This book chapter surveys the state of practice in model-based testing (MBT) as applied to embedded and cyber-physical systems. It covers modelling notations including UML statecharts, extended finite automata, and timed automata, and maps them to corresponding test generation algorithms. Coverage criteria are categorised into structural, fault-based, and requirements-based families. A discussion of toolchain integration addresses challenges specific to embedded targets: cross-compilation, hardware-in-the-loop execution, and limited observability. Two worked examples illustrate applying MBT to an automotive body control module and an industrial motor controller. The chapter closes with a discussion of open problems including scalability to large state spaces, handling of real-time constraints, and the lack of standardised interfaces between modelling and test execution tools.

title: Measuring the Cost of Test Suite Maintenance Over Multiple Firmware Releases
abstract: Automated test suites generated from formal models must be updated as firmware specifications evolve, yet the maintenance cost of model-based suites is rarely quantified empirically. This study tracks five firmware products through 8 to 14 release cycles, recording the time engineers spent updating model specifications, regenerating test cases, and resolving obsolete test oracles. On average, model update effort represented 18% of total release testing effort, compared with 27% for manually maintained suites managing the same products in a parallel control group. The study also records the number of regression faults detected per release and finds that model-based suites detected faults 1.4 releases earlier on average. Threats to validity related to the single-organisation setting and self-reported effort data are discussed. The dataset, anonymised, is made available for further analysis.

title: Automating Oracle Construction for Hardware-in-the-Loop Firmware Tests Using Signal Temporal Logic
abstract: Specifying correct output behaviour for hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) firmware tests is labour intensive because engineers must manually define acceptable signal ranges and timing windows for each scenario. This paper investigates the use of Signal Temporal Logic (STL) formulas as automatically checkable test oracles in HIL test environments. STL formulas are mined from a set of passing execution traces using a template-guided parameter synthesis procedure. The synthesised formulas are then used as oracles for new test runs. The approach was evaluated on a DC motor control firmware and a temperature regulation firmware, each executed on physical target hardware. Oracle construction time dropped from a median of 47 minutes per scenario (manual) to under 4 minutes (automated). False positive and false negative rates of synthesised oracles were 3.1% and 1.8% respectively across 310 test scenarios. Limitations related to non-deterministic hardware timing are discussed.

title: Integration of Formal Specification Review into the Firmware Development Workflow: A Case Study at a Serbian Industrial Electronics Firm
abstract: Adopting formal specification practices in industry requires integrating review steps into existing development workflows without excessive overhead. This paper reports a two-year action research study conducted with a Serbian firm that develops programmable logic controllers. The study introduced a lightweight formalism based on communicating extended finite automata (CEFA) for specifying firmware modules, along with a peer-review checklist and a set of automated consistency checks. Defect data were collected for 34 firmware modules developed before and after adoption. Post-adoption modules showed a 29% reduction in defects found during system integration testing. Developer survey data indicate that engineers found the notation acceptable after a two-day training course. Barriers including tool fragmentation and version control of model artefacts are documented. The paper provides a replication package containing the checklist, consistency check scripts, and anonymised defect logs.

title: SpecMutate: A Framework for Specification-Level Mutation Testing of Extended Finite Automata Models
abstract: Most mutation testing tools operate at the source code level, but for model-based testing workflows it is useful to seed faults into the formal model rather than the implementation. SpecMutate is a framework that applies 23 mutation operators directly to extended finite automata (EFA) models serialised in an XML interchange format. Operators include guard weakening, output-action swapping, state-merge, and variable initialisation faults. The framework integrates with an open-source model-based test generator and reports the model mutation score alongside the implementation mutation score. An experiment on six firmware EFA models with a combined 312 states found that model mutation scores and code mutation scores diverged significantly for three of the subjects, indicating that the model had lower fidelity than assumed. Runtime for model mutation analysis was under two minutes per model on a standard workstation, making it suitable for pre-commit checks.

title: Regression Test Prioritisation for Firmware Using Historical Fault Localisation Data
abstract: Test prioritisation orders a regression suite so that fault-detecting tests execute earlier, reducing feedback latency. This paper proposes a history-based prioritisation strategy that weights tests by the fault-localisation entropy of the code regions they cover across previous test campaigns. Coverage and fault data from nine firmware projects with histories spanning 12 to 31 releases were used to train and evaluate the strategy. The proposed approach achieved an average percentage of faults detected (APFD) of 0.78, compared with 0.61 for random ordering and 0.71 for a coverage-based baseline. Computational overhead of computing prioritisation order was below 90 seconds for all subjects. The paper also analyses how quickly the historical model degrades after a major refactoring event and proposes a simple reset heuristic triggered by structural change thresholds.

title: Combining Model-Based Test Generation with Large Language Model Suggestions for Uncovered Firmware Scenarios
abstract: Model-based test generation is constrained by the completeness of the formal model: scenarios not captured in the specification are not tested. This preprint explores a workflow where an LLM is prompted with natural-language firmware documentation and existing EFA models to suggest additional test scenarios that may correspond to specification gaps. Suggested scenarios are reviewed by engineers and, if accepted, formalised as model extensions. The approach was piloted on three firmware modules from an industrial PLC project. Engineers accepted 41% of LLM suggestions after review; of those, 17 were formalised and added to the model. Subsequent mutation analysis showed an increase in model mutation score of 6.3 percentage points on average. The paper does not claim that LLM suggestions are reliable in general but characterises conditions under which they are useful as a complement to structured specification review.

title: Automated Generation of Compatibility Test Cases from Android Permission Change Logs
abstract: Android's permission model underwent significant restructuring between API levels 22 and 23 with the introduction of runtime permissions, causing widespread behavioural incompatibilities in deployed applications. This paper presents PermGen, a tool that parses Android SDK change logs and permission usage declarations in application manifests to automatically generate JUnit-based test cases targeting permission-related execution paths. The tool was evaluated on 45 applications from the Google Play Store's productivity category, generating on average 17.3 test cases per application. Execution of generated suites on a physical device pool covering API levels 21 through 27 revealed 83 previously undocumented permission-handling defects across 31 applications. Compared to manually authored test suites covering the same permission scenarios, PermGen achieved 78% of the fault detection rate at 12% of the authoring effort, measured in developer-hours. Limitations regarding obfuscated code and dynamically requested permissions are discussed.

title: Predictive Maintenance Scheduling for Small Wind Turbines Using Gradient-Boosted Survival Models on Vibration and SCADA Data
abstract: Small wind turbines installed on agricultural and industrial premises in Serbia are often maintained reactively due to the absence of dedicated condition monitoring. This paper fits gradient-boosted survival models—specifically, a discrete-time hazard model and a random survival forest—to a combined dataset of SCADA telemetry and tower-mounted accelerometer readings from 17 turbines over five years. Predictors include nacelle vibration root-mean-square in three frequency bands, rotor speed deviation, and nacelle temperature differential. The discrete-time hazard model achieved a concordance index of 0.73 on a held-out cohort, outperforming a Cox baseline at 0.65. Predicted 30-day failure probability was used to generate ranked maintenance schedules, which were evaluated in a retrospective simulation against actual maintenance logs, showing an estimated 22 % reduction in unscheduled downtime hours.

title: Incremental Model-to-Text Generation for PLC Software: Handling Configuration Changes Without Full Regeneration
abstract: Full regeneration of PLC source code from a configuration model is straightforward but can be impractical in projects where manually authored customisation sections exist alongside generated code. This paper presents an incremental generation strategy that identifies which model elements have changed between two configuration revisions and regenerates only the affected Structured Text compilation units, preserving protected regions in unaffected units. Change detection is implemented as a model differencing step operating on XMI serialisations of feature model configurations, producing a delta structure that drives selective Xtend template invocation. The strategy was evaluated on a synthetic benchmark of 50 configuration pairs derived from a packaging-machine product line model with 41 features. Regeneration time was reduced by a mean of 74% compared to full regeneration, with no instances of incorrect code produced across 1,200 generated file revisions as verified by a regression test suite. The paper formalises the notion of generation dependency to characterise when incremental regeneration is sound.

title: Measuring Coupling in Polyglot Repositories: A Metric Suite Based on Cross-Language Dependency Edges
abstract: Standard coupling metrics such as afferent/efferent coupling and instability were designed for single-language object-oriented systems. In polyglot repositories, cross-language calls—for example, from Python orchestration scripts into compiled C extensions, or from JVM-hosted Kotlin into native libraries via JNI—create dependency edges that existing metrics ignore. We define an extended metric suite that accounts for cross-language edge weight, directionality, and language-pair asymmetry. We computed the suite on 23 open-source polyglot repositories and validated its discriminative power against manually assigned architectural quality ratings provided by eight independent evaluators. Cross-language instability correlated more strongly with subjectively rated architectural fragility (Spearman ρ = 0.71) than standard within-language instability alone (ρ = 0.48). We provide a reference implementation for the metric suite as a command-line tool.

title: Survey of Adaptive Bitrate Algorithms for 360-Degree Video: From Heuristic to Learning-Based Approaches
abstract: This survey reviews approximately 60 published ABR algorithms proposed specifically for omnidirectional video streaming between 2016 and 2022. Algorithms are classified into four families: buffer-based heuristics, model predictive control approaches, reinforcement learning methods, and hybrid schemes that combine learned viewport prediction with classical rate control. For each family the review discusses design assumptions, computational requirements, and reported QoE gains. A unified evaluation framework is described in which algorithm descriptions are mapped onto five common axes: prediction horizon, tile granularity, network model type, QoE target metric, and deployment complexity. The survey identifies three open problems: the lack of standardised public head-tracking datasets for fair comparison, the absence of energy consumption metrics in most evaluations, and the limited treatment of multi-user shared-link scenarios. A table of 38 datasets used in surveyed papers is included.

title: Skill-Based Robot Programming: Methods, Representations, and Deployment Tools
abstract: This book chapter surveys the state of skill-based approaches to robot programming, covering three main representation styles: procedural skill trees, ontology-based capability models, and learning-from-demonstration encodings. For each style the chapter reviews published implementations, discusses deployment tool support, and compares the programmer effort required for initial authoring versus reuse. A structured comparison table covers 31 selected systems published between 2005 and 2021. The chapter then describes in detail the authors' own ontology-driven tool chain, walking through the workflow from skill library construction to executable program generation for a KUKA KRC4 controller. Two worked examples illustrate the workflow: a palletising task and a camera-guided bin-picking task. The chapter concludes with a discussion of open challenges including handling of run-time exceptions, scalability of the ontology to large libraries, and integration with digital twin environments. It is intended as a reference for graduate students and practicing engineers entering the field.

title: A Retiming-Aware Operator Binding Algorithm for HLS with Heterogeneous DSP Blocks
abstract: Modern FPGA families include DSP blocks with configurable pre-adder and post-accumulator pipelines that can absorb retiming registers, reducing the LUT cost of retimed datapaths. Existing HLS tools treat DSP blocks as fixed-latency operators and do not exploit this flexibility during binding. This paper presents a binding algorithm that models DSP pre-adder and accumulator optionality, integrates retiming feasibility checks derived from the bound schedule, and selects binding assignments that maximise internal DSP pipeline use. The algorithm is implemented as a post-synthesis pass processing netlists exported from Vitis HLS 2024.1 in Verilog form. Evaluated on twelve arithmetic-heavy signal processing kernels targeting a Versal AI Core VC1902, the pass reduces registered LUT count by 9–22% with no change in clock period. Compile-time overhead is under 8 seconds per kernel.

title: FPGA-Based Analog Front-End Emulation for Knock Sensor Signal Generation in Engine HiL Testing
abstract: Knock sensors produce broadband vibration signals in the 5–15 kHz range that engine ECUs process through bandpass filters and envelope detectors to identify combustion knock events. Emulating these signals accurately on a HiL bench requires waveform generation with sufficient bandwidth and amplitude resolution. This work presents an FPGA-based waveform generator implemented on an Artix-7 device that produces synthetic knock and non-knock signals based on parameterised cylinder pressure traces from a four-cylinder naturally aspirated engine model. The generator uses a 16-bit DAC at 250 kS/s per channel and a lookup-table synthesis approach with four independently configurable channels. Signal quality was assessed by comparing spectra from the emulated output against recordings taken from a motored engine on a dynamometer test bench. Spectral flatness error within the 5–15 kHz band was below 1.8 dB. An ECU under test correctly classified knock events in 97.3% of 600 injected test cases. The paper details the fixed-point filter coefficients, DAC interface timing, and calibration procedure.

title: Formalising EU Drivers' Hours Rules as a Constraint Satisfaction Problem
abstract: Regulation (EC) No 561/2006 defines a set of interlocking time constraints governing driving periods, breaks, and rest intervals for professional drivers. This paper presents a formal representation of those rules as a constraint satisfaction problem (CSP), using finite-domain variable assignment to encode driving and rest states over a rolling two-week window. The model was implemented in SWI-Prolog and validated against 112 manually annotated driver activity logs collected from a Serbian long-distance carrier. The system correctly identified the compliance status of 108 of the 112 logs, with four cases involving ambiguous multi-manning situations that required manual resolution. The paper discusses the structural complexity introduced by derogations and discusses how partial observability of cross-border rest periods complicates automated reasoning. The approach is compared to a rule-tree baseline, showing a reduction in false-positive violation flags from 14.3% to 3.6%. The work provides a formal basis for subsequent automated auditing tools.

title: Audience Behaviour Segmentation Using Recurrent Neural Networks on Longitudinal Engagement Logs
abstract: Long short-term memory (LSTM) networks can capture audience behaviour patterns that fixed-window statistical models miss. This paper trains LSTM-based sequence encoders on 18 months of per-user engagement logs (reactions, comments, shares, view durations) from a regional streaming and content platform with 340,000 registered users in Serbia and Bosnia-Herzegovina. Encoded representations were fed into a k-means layer to derive behavioural segments. Six stable segments emerged from a sweep of k from 3 to 10, evaluated by silhouette score and external validation against self-reported survey preferences collected from 2,100 users. The LSTM-derived segments outperformed segments produced by aggregated frequency-recency-monetary (FRM) features on prediction of next-week content consumption category (macro-F1: 0.61 vs 0.48). Segment profiles—labelled binge viewers, topical dippers, passive scrollers, commenter-contributors, share-motivated readers, and lapsed returnees—are described and their implications for personalised push-notification scheduling are discussed.

title: Reusing the Core Criterion and Evidence Vocabulary in Western Balkan ESPD Implementations
abstract: The European Single Procurement Document (ESPD) relies on the Core Criterion and Evidence Vocabulary (CCCEV) to express exclusion grounds and selection criteria as machine-readable structured data. This paper examines whether CCCEV can be reused in Western Balkan ESPD implementations where the underlying legal criteria differ from EU directives. The analysis focuses on Serbia and Bosnia-Herzegovina. A comparison of CCCEV criterion types against national exclusion ground lists reveals that 68 % of Serbian grounds can be expressed using existing CCCEV patterns without modification. For the remaining 32 %, new criterion subclasses are specified. A prototype ESPD form generator was built using Apache Jena and tested with procurement officers from three Serbian ministries; usability evaluation with 18 participants produced a mean System Usability Scale score of 72.4, classed as acceptable. The paper concludes with recommendations for a regional CCCEV extension registry.

title: Towards a Unified Security Profile for Over-the-Air Firmware Update in IEC 62443 Compliant Industrial Installations
abstract: IEC 62443 defines security levels and component requirements for industrial automation and control systems but provides limited normative guidance on firmware update mechanisms. This paper analyses firmware update security requirements implied by IEC 62443-3-3 and IEC 62443-4-2 at Security Levels 1 through 3, identifying 23 specific requirements that a compliant OTA firmware update subsystem must satisfy. For each requirement, the paper maps existing technical mechanisms — from HMAC-based integrity checking to certificate-based authentication and monotonic rollback counters — and identifies three areas where current practice does not clearly satisfy the standard's intent: cryptographic agility, update transaction atomicity across power loss events, and audit logging on Class 1 devices. A reference architecture for a compliant firmware update service is outlined, and the paper estimates implementation effort in person-months for each architectural component at three device capability tiers. The analysis is illustrated using data from two anonymised industrial deployments reviewed during the study.

title: A Lightweight Authenticated Bootloader Protocol for Wireless Sensor Nodes in Industrial SCADA Environments
abstract: This paper describes the design and evaluation of an authenticated bootloader protocol intended for 8-bit microcontroller-based sensor nodes communicating over IEEE 802.15.4 radio links in industrial SCADA deployments. The protocol uses HMAC-SHA256 for image authentication and a two-phase commit scheme to prevent partial writes during interrupted transmissions. Experimental evaluation was conducted on a testbed of 24 nodes deployed across a simulated substation environment, with artificial packet-loss rates ranging from 5% to 40%. Mean firmware delivery time for a 64 KB image increased from 38 seconds under ideal conditions to 147 seconds at 40% packet loss, while no corrupted images were accepted across 2 400 delivery trials. Code size overhead on the target MCU was 3.2 KB of flash. The paper also discusses replay-attack resistance and the limitations of symmetric key management at scale, proposing a zone-based key hierarchy as a practical mitigation for deployments with up to 500 nodes.

title: Delta Patching for Constrained Devices: Reducing Over-the-Air Update Payload on Low-Rate Wireless Links
abstract: Firmware images for constrained devices rarely change more than a few percent between successive releases, yet most over-the-air update mechanisms transmit full images. This paper evaluates three binary delta algorithms — bsdiff, VCDIFF, and a purpose-built block-aligned differencer — applied to firmware images from four representative industrial sensor product lines. Patch sizes across 38 consecutive release pairs averaged 11.4% of full image size for bsdiff and 14.7% for the block-aligned approach, with the latter requiring 40% less RAM during reconstruction. Transmission time over a simulated 1.2 kbit/s channel, representative of 868 MHz narrowband industrial radio, was reduced from an average of 4.1 minutes to 28 seconds. Reconstruction failure rates under 10% artificial bit-error conditions were below 0.3% for all schemes when combined with a 16-bit CRC per block. The paper includes a complexity analysis and discusses applicability to devices with less than 8 KB of available RAM.

Протокол је моделован у Прометеловом језику, а верификација је обухватила 14 безбедносних и животних особина формулисаних у линеарној темпоралној логици. Исправљени протокол је верификован без кршења постављених особина у простору стања са до 2,1 × 10⁸ стања. title: Key Distribution Schemes for Large-Scale Industrial Wireless Sensor Networks: A Comparative Study
abstract: Managing cryptographic keys across hundreds of constrained field devices is a practical bottleneck in industrial wireless deployments. This paper systematically compares five key distribution schemes — pre-shared master key, pairwise key pre-distribution, a Blom matrix scheme, a hierarchical certificate authority approach adapted for 6LoWPAN, and an elliptic-curve Diffie–Hellman bootstrapping protocol — across three criteria: memory footprint on a Cortex-M0 class device, time to complete key establishment after node power-on, and resilience to node capture. Measurements were taken on a physical testbed of 60 nodes. The Blom scheme achieved the best balance for networks under 200 nodes, requiring 1.8 KB RAM and completing key establishment in under 400 ms. The ECC bootstrapping protocol was the only scheme providing forward secrecy but demanded 14 KB RAM and 2.3 seconds for key exchange, making it unsuitable for the lowest-tier devices. Practical recommendations are derived for three deployment tiers based on device capability.

title: Firmware Delivery Reliability Over LoRa at Sub-kbit/s Data Rates: Measurement Study in an Urban Industrial Site
abstract: LoRa physical layer spreading factors SF7 through SF12 offer data rates from roughly 250 bit/s to 5.5 kbit/s at the expense of airtime, a constraint with direct implications for over-the-air firmware update feasibility. This paper reports on measurements conducted at a chemical plant in Novi Sad over six weeks using a network of 18 end-devices at distances between 80 m and 1.4 km from a single gateway. Packet delivery ratio at SF12 averaged 91.3% under normal plant operation but dropped to 73.8% during periods of heavy crane and conveyor activity. A store-and-forward segmentation protocol with per-segment HMAC authentication was deployed, and mean time to complete a 32 KB firmware update was measured at 22 minutes at SF12. The paper proposes an adaptive spreading-factor selection policy that reduced average update time to 9.4 minutes while maintaining delivery success above 97% across all trials.

title: Replay Attack Taxonomy and Countermeasure Classification for Over-the-Air Firmware Update Protocols
abstract: Replay attacks against firmware update protocols can result in downgrade to vulnerable firmware versions, denial of service, or unnecessary device reboots in safety-critical industrial settings. This book chapter surveys replay attack vectors specific to constrained wireless devices, classifying them along four axes: attacker capability (passive monitor, active injector, insider), network topology (star, mesh, multi-hop), device state (idle, update-in-progress, post-install reboot), and available countermeasure class (nonce-based, timestamp-based, monotonic counter, challenge–response). For each combination, the chapter provides an analysis of effectiveness and implementation cost in terms of RAM, non-volatile write cycles, and required time synchronization infrastructure. Fourteen representative firmware update protocols from research literature and three from open-source embedded projects are mapped onto the taxonomy. The chapter concludes with a decision framework that assists protocol designers in selecting countermeasure combinations appropriate to their threat model and device constraints.

title: Integrity Verification of Incremental Firmware Patches Using Merkle Hash Trees on Cortex-M Microcontrollers
abstract: Applying binary patches to firmware in the field requires verification mechanisms that can detect partial or corrupted patch delivery without storing the complete expected image. This paper proposes a Merkle hash tree construction adapted for delta patches, where leaf nodes correspond to fixed-size patch chunks and the root hash is authenticated by an ECDSA signature over NIST P-256. The scheme was implemented on an STM32L4 series microcontroller with 64 KB RAM. Hash tree construction over a 16 KB patch (32 leaves) required 210 ms and consumed a peak of 4.1 KB stack space. Verification of a partial delivery — detecting one corrupted chunk among 32 — required fewer than 50 ms. The paper compares this approach against full-image HMAC and rolling-hash alternatives in terms of detection granularity, storage requirements, and recovery strategy. A discussion of the tradeoffs in choosing tree depth is included, with measurements at depths 3, 4, and 5.

title: Effect of Duty-Cycle Restrictions on OTA Firmware Update Latency in the 868 MHz ISM Band: An Analytical Model
abstract: Regulatory duty-cycle limits in the European 868 MHz ISM band constrain transmission time to 1% in sub-band 1, directly affecting over-the-air firmware update completion times for LPWAN devices. This paper develops a queuing-theory-based analytical model for firmware delivery latency under duty-cycle constraints, accounting for segmentation overhead, retransmission probability, and concurrent traffic from non-update messages. The model is parameterised using empirical measurements from a 30-node LoRaWAN testbed. Analytical predictions of mean delivery time matched measurements within 8% across all tested configurations. The model predicts that for a 64 KB image at SF10, mean delivery time under 1% duty cycle is 4.7 hours in a lightly loaded network and rises to over 18 hours under moderate concurrent telemetry load. A scheduling strategy that prioritises update segments during predicted low-traffic windows is described and shown analytically to reduce mean delivery time by 31%.

title: Secure Multicast Firmware Delivery for Co-Located Industrial Sensor Clusters Over Zigbee
abstract: When many co-located devices require the same firmware update simultaneously, unicast delivery multiplies airtime linearly with node count. This paper describes a secure multicast delivery scheme for Zigbee-based industrial sensor clusters, using AES-128 CCM* group encryption with individual per-device session key wrapping to prevent one node from decrypting another's update confirmation. The protocol was implemented on CC2530-based nodes and evaluated in a testbed of 8 and 16 node clusters. For a 48 KB image, multicast delivery to a 16-node cluster completed in 6.8 minutes versus 41.3 minutes for sequential unicast, a factor of 6.1 improvement. Delivery success rate was 98.7% at 16 nodes under representative packet loss of 8%. The paper analyses the key management overhead introduced by per-device key wrapping and discusses the session key refresh interval as a function of assumed node compromise rate.

title: Certificate-Based Firmware Authentication for Resource-Constrained Devices Without Persistent Internet Connectivity
abstract: Public-key certificate validation normally depends on online revocation checking, which is infeasible for industrial field devices that communicate only intermittently. This paper proposes an offline certificate validation scheme for firmware authentication in which short-lived leaf certificates, valid for a configurable window of 24–168 hours, are bundled with the firmware image and verified against a pre-installed intermediate CA certificate stored in device ROM. Certificate revocation is handled by expiry rather than CRL or OCSP. The scheme uses X.509 profiles trimmed to fit within 512 bytes using a custom DER subset. Implementation and evaluation were performed on an ARM Cortex-M3 device with 32 KB RAM; certificate parsing and verification completed in 310 ms using a software ECC library. The paper analyses the security implications of the short-lived certificate approach under various attacker models, including the case where the attacker can delay delivery to extend a certificate's apparent validity.

title: Протокол за верификацију ланца испоруке фирмвера у вишестепеним телеметријским мрежама
abstract: У вишестепеним индустријским мрежама фирмвер може проћи кроз неколико посредничких чворова — концентратора и гетвеја — пре него што стигне до крајњег уређаја. Свaki посреднички чвор представља потенцијалну тачку манипулације. Овај рад предлаже протокол за верификацију ланца испоруке у коме сваки посреднички чвор потписује потврду о пријему и прослеђивању фирмверског сегмента, формирајући верификабилни низ потврда. Коначни уређај верификује цео ланац пре инсталације. Протокол је анализиран у моделу са до четири посреднička нивоа. Поред безбедносне анализе, рад мери додатно кашњење које уносе операције потписивања на различитим класама чворова: 28 ms по потпису на концентратору са Cortex-M4 процесором наспрам 190 ms на Cortex-M0+ чвору. Предложена је хибридна шема у којој само концентраtори потписују ланац, а крajnji уређаји верификују само коренски потпис произвођача, чиме се кашњење своди на прихватљив ниво.

title: Benchmarking Post-Quantum Signature Schemes for Firmware Authentication on Class 1 IoT Devices
abstract: Anticipated deployment lifetimes of industrial sensor nodes of 10–20 years motivate evaluation of post-quantum signature algorithms for firmware authentication on severely constrained hardware. This paper benchmarks four NIST post-quantum signature candidates — CRYSTALS-Dilithium2, Falcon-512, SPHINCS+-SHA2-128s, and a lattice-based scheme submitted to the ongoing standardisation process — on two representative Class 1 IoT platforms: an ARM Cortex-M0+ at 48 MHz with 32 KB RAM and a Cortex-M4 at 120 MHz with 256 KB RAM. Metrics collected include signature verification time, public key and signature sizes, and peak RAM consumption. On the Cortex-M0+ platform, Falcon-512 verification completed in 480 ms consuming 28 KB RAM peak, which exceeds available memory, while SPHINCS+-SHA2-128s verified in 1 140 ms with 6.2 KB peak RAM, making it the only scheme feasible on the lower-end device. Dilithium2 was feasible on the Cortex-M4 at 94 ms. The paper discusses the practical tradeoffs for protocol designers choosing between these schemes given device capability distribution in a deployment.
venue: Journal of Cryptographic Engineering

title: Adaptive Segmentation and Retransmission Scheduling for Firmware Delivery Over NB-IoT in Deep-Indoor Industrial Environments
abstract: NB-IoT deployment in basement-level and shielded industrial environments produces highly variable signal conditions, with RSRP measurements in one monitored processing facility ranging from −85 dBm to −138 dBm across 22 fixed sensor positions. This paper describes an adaptive firmware delivery protocol that adjusts segment size and retransmission window based on real-time channel quality indicator reports available in the NB-IoT stack. Segment sizes were varied between 64 and 512 bytes; the adaptive scheme selected optimal sizes per device per update session. In a 22-device testbed deployment over four months, the adaptive protocol reduced total update time by 38% compared to a fixed 128-byte segment baseline and reduced the number of incomplete update sessions from 11.4% to 2.1%. Energy consumption per completed update was also measured on battery-powered nodes, with the adaptive scheme consuming 12% less energy due to fewer retransmissions. A lightweight predictor using a 5-point CQI moving average was sufficient to achieve near-optimal segment sizing.

title: Morphological Disambiguation in Serbian: A Maximum Entropy Approach on a Balanced News Corpus
abstract: This paper describes the construction and annotation of a 200,000-token Serbian newspaper corpus and the training of a maximum entropy morphological disambiguator on it. Serbian presents particular challenges for disambiguation due to its free word order, extensive inflectional paradigms, and syncretism across several case forms. The corpus was sampled from three regional dailies covering the period 2005–2009 and annotated manually by two linguists following an adapted MULTEXT-East tagset. Inter-annotator agreement reached κ = 0.87 on the full tagset. The maximum entropy model trained on 80% of the data achieved a per-token accuracy of 91.3% on the held-out test set, outperforming a rule-based baseline by 4.1 percentage points. Error analysis showed that the remaining errors cluster heavily around nominal case syncretism in neuter nouns and verbal aspect ambiguity. The annotated corpus and tagger are made available under a Creative Commons licence.

title: Annotation Consistency in Dependency Treebanks: A Case Study on Serbian and Croatian Parallel Texts
abstract: Consistent syntactic annotation across closely related language varieties is essential for cross-lingual experiments, yet disagreements between annotation teams are common even when shared guidelines are nominally in use. This study examines annotation consistency in a 50,000-token parallel Serbian–Croatian dependency treebank constructed as part of a bilateral research effort. Five annotators from two institutions independently labelled a common 5,000-token subset, and discrepancies were systematically catalogued and attributed to guideline ambiguity, language-variety differences, or genuine annotator uncertainty. We propose a set of revision criteria for eleven frequently disputed dependency relation categories and demonstrate that applying them retrospectively raises the macro-averaged labelled attachment score (LAS) agreement from 76.4% to 83.1% across the full annotator set. The revised guidelines and the reconciled treebank subset are released alongside the paper. Findings are relevant to any team maintaining parallel treebanks for closely related South Slavic varieties.

title: Transferring POS Taggers Across the Slavic–Finno-Ugric Boundary: Experiments with Serbian and Hungarian
abstract: This paper investigates how much morphological tagging accuracy can be retained when a tagger trained on Serbian is transferred—without any target-language labelled data—to Hungarian, and vice versa. Despite the typological distance between a South Slavic language and a Finno-Ugric agglutinative language, both exhibit rich morphology, which motivates the comparison. We map the MULTEXT-East tagsets of the two languages onto a reduced shared feature schema covering part of speech, number, and case, then apply three transfer strategies: direct model transfer, feature projection via word alignments, and self-training with a small unlabelled Hungarian/Serbian target corpus. Using Serbian SETimes-derived text and a Hungarian news corpus of comparable size (circa 180,000 tokens each), we find that self-training with 20,000 unlabelled target tokens recovers roughly 60% of the performance gap relative to a fully supervised target-language model. Results suggest shared morphological feature spaces are an effective bridge even across unrelated families.

title: A Spoken Serbian Corpus for Sociolinguistic and Computational Research: Design, Recording, and Transcription Protocol
abstract: This book chapter describes the methodology behind the Spoken Serbian Resource Corpus (SpoSReC), a 120-hour collection of semi-spontaneous speech recorded across four dialect regions of Serbia and Vojvodina between 2013 and 2016. The chapter covers microphone selection, recording environment norms, speaker recruitment targeting balanced age, gender, and education profiles, and the transcription annotation scheme adapted from CHAT with additional tiers for dialect-specific phonological features. Transcription was performed by twelve trained student annotators following two rounds of calibration; a 5% re-annotation sample showed token-level accuracy above 94%. The chapter discusses particular challenges around code-switching with Hungarian in the Vojvodina sub-corpus, which accounts for roughly 18% of recorded hours. Intended uses include sociolinguistic analysis of dialect contact, acoustic modelling, and as a complement to written corpora in multilingual NLP pipelines. The corpus is deposited at the CLARIN.SI repository.

title: Zero-Shot Dependency Parsing of Bosnian Using a Serbian Transition-Based Parser
abstract: Bosnian and Serbian share the majority of their grammar and lexicon, yet separate standardisation efforts mean that available NLP models almost never target Bosnian explicitly. This paper evaluates whether a transition-based dependency parser trained exclusively on a 90,000-token Serbian treebank can parse Bosnian texts without any adaptation. We test on a newly constructed 8,000-token Bosnian web-text gold standard annotated in Universal Dependencies (UD) format. Unlabelled attachment score (UAS) reaches 81.7% and LAS 74.2%, which we compare against two multilingual baselines (mBERT fine-tuned on Serbian UD data, and a delexicalised cross-lingual parser). We also report results for a shallow domain-adaptation step that replaces Bosnian-specific orthographic conventions and select lexical items, which raises LAS by 2.4 points. The work argues for treating Bosnian, Croatian, and Serbian as a resource-sharing cluster within UD rather than as fully independent treebank targets.

title: Evaluating Multilingual BERT Representations for Serbian Morphosyntactic Tagging Across Domains
abstract: Contextualised word representations from multilingual pretrained transformers have shown strong performance on many NLP tasks, but their behaviour on morphologically complex languages with limited training data in the pretraining corpus is not well understood. We fine-tune multilingual BERT (mBERT) and XLM-RoBERTa on Serbian morphosyntactic tagging across four domains: news, parliamentary proceedings, social media, and legal text, using gold-standard data sets totalling approximately 130,000 tokens. Results show that mBERT fine-tuned on news data drops from 94.1% accuracy on in-domain test data to 87.6% on social media text, with the largest error categories being unknown tokenisation units and non-standard inflected forms. XLM-RoBERTa is more robust across domains, with a 3.2-point smaller drop on social media. We also test both models on a 15,000-token Pannonian Rusyn test set as an extreme low-resource condition and observe that XLM-RoBERTa achieves 71.3% even without any Rusyn fine-tuning data, apparently through transfer from Serbian and Ukrainian subword overlap.

title: Annotation of Aspect and Actionality in Serbian Verbal Predicates: Guidelines and a Pilot Corpus
abstract: Grammatical aspect in Serbian interacts with lexical actionality (Aktionsart) in ways that create persistent disagreements among annotators and inconsistencies across existing resources. This paper presents a detailed annotation scheme for aspect-actionality combinations in Serbian verbal predicates, developed iteratively over eighteen months through repeated annotation cycles on a pilot corpus of 25,000 tokens drawn from fiction and journalistic prose. The scheme distinguishes five aspectual classes and four primary actionality types, with explicit rules for handling borderline prefixation patterns that shift a verb from imperfective to perfective without clear lexical change. Inter-annotator agreement after guideline stabilisation reached κ = 0.81 for aspect and κ = 0.74 for actionality. We report a frequency distribution of the resulting cross-classifications and show that approximately 12% of verb tokens in our pilot corpus are genuinely ambiguous under context, requiring discourse-level cues for resolution. The annotated pilot corpus and guidelines are released publicly.

title: Cross-Lingual Propagation of Named Entity Annotations from Serbian to Macedonian via Bilingual Lexicons
abstract: Named entity recognition (NER) for Macedonian is severely constrained by the lack of annotated training data. This paper investigates whether named entity labels from a 95,000-token Serbian NER corpus can be projected onto a parallel Macedonian corpus through automatic word alignment combined with bilingual lexicon filtering, producing usable silver-standard training data. We compare three projection strategies and train a BiLSTM-CRF model on the resulting Macedonian silver data, evaluating on a 3,000-token manually annotated Macedonian gold test set. The best projection strategy yields an F1 of 68.4% for the three-class scheme (PER, ORG, LOC), compared to 51.3% for a naive direct-transfer baseline. We further show that adding 2,000 manually corrected tokens to the silver training set pushes F1 to 76.1%, pointing to a cost-effective data-creation strategy. Macedonian gold test data are released through the CLARIN infrastructure.

title: A Morphological Lexicon for Pannonian Rusyn: Construction, Coverage, and Integration into an NLP Pipeline
abstract: Pannonian Rusyn is a regional language spoken by approximately 15,000 people in Vojvodina, Serbia, and parts of Croatia. It has received almost no computational treatment despite holding official minority language status in Serbia. This paper describes the construction of a morphological lexicon for Pannonian Rusyn containing 28,400 lemmas with full inflection tables generated by a hand-crafted finite-state transducer. Lexicon coverage was evaluated against a 40,000-token web-crawled corpus: the lexicon covers 84.6% of tokens and 61.3% of types, with the largest coverage gap in recent borrowings from Serbian and English. We integrate the lexicon into a simple morphological analysis pipeline and report tagging accuracy of 78.9% on a 2,500-token gold standard. Challenges specific to the language include dialectal spelling variation across the Bačka and Srem sub-varieties and the absence of a stable computational orthography standard. The lexicon is deposited at CLARIN ERIC and licensed under CC BY 4.0.

title: Sentence Boundary Detection in Historical Serbian Church-Slavonic Texts: Rule-Based and Statistical Approaches Compared
abstract: Historical digitisation projects increasingly produce raw OCR output from Serbian Church-Slavonic manuscripts, but standard sentence segmentation tools trained on modern text fail on these materials due to inconsistent punctuation, abbreviation conventions, and interlinear glosses. This paper evaluates three segmentation strategies on a 60,000-character corpus of digitised 18th-century ecclesiastical texts: a rule-based approach built on paleographic knowledge, a CRF model trained on 8,000 manually segmented characters, and a fine-tuned multilingual sentence segmenter. The CRF model achieves the best balance of precision (91.2%) and recall (88.7%), while the rule-based system has higher precision (94.1%) but lower recall (81.3%). We also quantify the downstream effect of segmentation errors on a subsequent keyword-in-context (KWIC) retrieval task, finding that even a 5% boundary error rate reduces KWIC precision by roughly 9 percentage points. The annotated subset and CRF model are shared via the project repository.

title: Benchmarking Low-Resource Multilingual Transformers on Four Vojvodina Minority Languages
abstract: Vojvodina hosts several small language communities—Hungarian, Slovak, Rusyn, and Romanian—each with official status but minimal NLP resources. This paper constructs a unified benchmark covering three tasks (morphosyntactic tagging, named entity recognition, and sentence-level sentiment classification) for all four languages, using data sets of 10,000–18,000 tokens per language assembled from local newspaper archives and social media under appropriate licences. We evaluate five multilingual transformer models (mBERT, XLM-R base, XLM-R large, a Slavic-focused model, and a model pre-trained on Hungarian) under three data regimes: zero-shot, 500-example few-shot, and full fine-tuning. Results confirm that language family proximity to high-resource languages in the pre-training data is a stronger predictor of zero-shot performance than script similarity. Hungarian achieves the highest zero-shot scores benefiting from the Hungarian-focused model; Rusyn consistently scores lowest across all models and tasks. The benchmark data, evaluation scripts, and all fine-tuned model checkpoints are released publicly.

title: Towards a Unified Annotation Scheme for Information Structure in Serbian, Croatian, and Bosnian Treebanks
abstract: Information structure—the encoding of topic, focus, and contrast in discourse—is systematically marked in South Slavic languages through word order variation, prosodic prominence, and particle placement, yet no shared annotation scheme currently covers Serbian, Croatian, and Bosnian simultaneously. This paper proposes such a scheme, derived from a comparative analysis of 120 ambiguous sentences drawn from parallel news texts in all three varieties. The scheme distinguishes topic span, narrow focus, broad focus, and contrastive topic using a two-tier annotation model compatible with the Universal Dependencies extended relation framework. We report pilot annotation statistics on a 6,000-token shared sample involving annotators from three institutions and discuss the main sources of disagreement, particularly around verum focus and the annotation of cleft-like constructions. A revised annotation manual and the pilot sample are submitted to the UD repository as a discussion document for community feedback.

title: Interjections in Serbian Prose Dialogue 1890–1940: Form, Function, and Editorial Normalisation
abstract: Interjections in Serbian dialogue of the early twentieth century form a heterogeneous class that has received little systematic corpus attention. This paper identifies and classifies 2,340 interjection tokens from the dialogue-annotated SerbProsRef corpus, grouping them into expressive, responsive, and discourse-structuring subtypes. Formal analysis documents considerable orthographic and morphological variation across publishers, with some interjections appearing in up to seven spelling variants across the corpus. Diachronic frequency analysis shows that expressive interjections decline after 1920 relative to corpus size while responsive interjections (confirmations, rejections, hesitations) remain stable, suggesting that later dialogue writing reduced overt emotional signalling in favour of conversational exchange patterns. A comparison of interjection density across genres (popular serial fiction vs. literary short fiction) confirms that popular serial fiction maintains approximately 1.8 times the interjection rate of its literary counterpart throughout the period.
venue: Zbornik Matice srpske za filologiju i lingvistiku

title: A Comparative Review of Recommendation Approaches for Sparse Purchase Histories in Small Retail
abstract: This paper surveys techniques applied to recommendation tasks where transaction logs contain fewer than twenty interactions per user on average, a condition common in independent and small-chain retail settings. The review covers memory-based collaborative filtering, content-based methods using product attribute vectors, and several hybrid architectures published between 2005 and 2013. Evaluation metrics across surveyed studies are standardised to precision at five and normalised discounted cumulative gain to allow comparison. The analysis identifies consistent shortcomings in purely collaborative approaches when item catalogues exceed a few hundred products but user bases remain small. Content-based methods show more stable baseline performance under these conditions but tend to over-specialise recommendations. The paper concludes by outlining criteria for selecting hybrid strategies depending on catalogue density, session length, and the availability of product metadata, offering a structured decision guide intended for practitioners in the regional retail sector.
venue: Journal of Applied Business Informatics

title: Evaluating Large Language Models for Semi-Automated Population of Procurement Ontologies from Unstructured Tender Documents
abstract: A substantial proportion of procurement information in Western Balkan portals is embedded in free-text PDF attachments—technical specifications, terms of reference, evaluation criteria—rather than structured fields. This paper evaluates four large language models (two multilingual, two Serbian-language fine-tuned) for extracting ontology-conformant instances from 240 unstructured tender documents spanning four sectors: road construction, medical supplies, IT services, and school catering. Extraction performance is measured against a gold standard annotation produced by two domain experts. F1 scores across all entity types range from 0.53 to 0.79 depending on model and sector. Performance is highest for numeric quantity extraction (F1 0.82) and lowest for procedure type classification (F1 0.51). Post-processing with SHACL constraint validation catches a further 18 % of entity errors not penalised by F1. The paper discusses implications for ontology population workflows in low-resource Slavic language settings.

title: Prediction of long-term physical stability of amorphous solid dispersions using accelerated isothermal crystallisation data and the Arrhenius equation
abstract: A predictive framework was developed to estimate room-temperature crystallisation half-lives of spray-dried amorphous dispersions from accelerated isothermal DSC crystallisation experiments conducted at three temperatures above Tg (Tg + 10, Tg + 20, Tg + 30 °C). Five systems were studied: fenofibrate–PVP VA64, carbamazepine–HPMC-AS MF, griseofulvin–Soluplus, piroxicam–PVP K30, and nifedipine–HPMC E15, all at 30 wt% drug loading. Activation energies for crystallisation ranged from 96 to 218 kJ mol−1. Extrapolated half-lives at 25 °C and 40% RH agreed with observed 30-month stability outcomes to within a factor of 1.8 for four of five systems; the griseofulvin–Soluplus system was underestimated by a factor of 3.2, possibly due to antiplasticisation effects not captured by the Arrhenius model. The method requires approximately 48 hours of DSC measurement per system and offers a practical early-stage stability screen.
venue: Pharmaceutical Solid-State Research

title: Integrating design space construction with MSPC dashboards for day-to-day operation of a pan coating line: practical framework and pilot implementation
abstract: This paper describes a practical framework for integrating quality-by-design design space information with real-time MSPC monitoring in a pan coating operation at pilot scale. The design space for aqueous ethylcellulose sustained-release coating of 500 mg metformin hydrochloride tablets was established using a Definitive Screening Design (12 runs) exploring five process parameters, yielding a Bayesian design space with 95% probability of meeting dissolution specifications at 2 h and 8 h. MPCA monitoring models built from 17 reference batches within the design space were deployed alongside the design space boundary in a unified dashboard for the pan coating operator. A six-month pilot implementation period covered 41 production batches. The dashboard correctly flagged all four batches that subsequently failed dissolution testing, while generating two false alarms. Integration of design space contour overlays with MPCA scores provided operators with directional guidance for corrective action that pure MSPC charts do not supply. Operator feedback collected via structured interviews is reported.

title: Continuous enzymatic phospholipid synthesis in a packed-bed reactor: residence time distribution and productivity analysis
abstract: A continuous packed-bed reactor (PBR) packed with Thermomyces lanuginosus lipase immobilised on acrylic beads (20 g, bed volume 45 mL) was evaluated for phosphatidylcholine synthesis as an alternative to batch operation. Substrate feed (lysophosphatidylcholine and oleic acid, 1:3 molar ratio in tert-amyl alcohol/water 96:4 v/v) was delivered at flow rates of 0.2–1.5 mL/min. Residence time distribution was characterised by tracer experiments with acetone, yielding a Bodenstein number of 28, indicating near-plug-flow behaviour. At 0.5 mL/min, PC yield was 65.8 ± 2.3% at steady state, with a volumetric productivity of 4.1 g PC/L·h, approximately 2.4-fold higher than comparable batch experiments. Enzyme half-life in continuous mode was 22 days compared with 14 days in batch mode. The PBR approach reduces downstream processing volume and improves throughput, making it attractive for scale-up to pilot level.

title: Comparing SMOTE and ADASYN on Short Legal Texts with Fewer Than 500 Training Instances
abstract: Resampling techniques designed for tabular data are often applied to text feature vectors without assessing whether interpolation in high-dimensional TF-IDF space produces semantically coherent synthetic documents. This paper applies SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE, and ADASYN to a dataset of 487 Serbian misdemeanour rulings represented as 2,000-dimensional TF-IDF vectors, with minority classes containing as few as 31 samples. Classification performance is assessed using stratified five-fold cross-validation with SVM and gradient boosting classifiers. ADASYN yields the highest macro F1 improvement (from 0.34 to 0.51 for SVM), but manual inspection of 50 synthetic vectors shows that 38% contain feature combinations absent in any real document. The paper proposes a nearest-neighbour coherence filter that removes synthetic points deviating beyond two standard deviations from their class centroid, recovering coherence while retaining 81% of generated samples. This filtered variant outperforms unfiltered ADASYN on two of three evaluation metrics.

title: A Comparison of Krylov and POD Subspace Methods for Parametric Model Order Reduction in Structural Acoustics
abstract: Parametric model order reduction (pMOR) methods based on Krylov subspaces and proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) are compared on a benchmark plate-cavity structural-acoustic problem. The full model has 8 400 structural and 3 100 acoustic degrees of freedom. The parameter of interest is the plate thickness, ranging from 3 mm to 8 mm in steps of 0.5 mm. Krylov-based reduction at a single expansion frequency preserves acoustic transfer functions to within 1.8 % across the 20–400 Hz band, but deteriorates above 600 Hz. POD bases constructed from 22 snapshot solutions at parameter samples achieve 0.9 % relative error across the full 20–800 Hz range with a basis of dimension 18. Computational speed-up relative to the full-order solve is 47× for POD and 31× for Krylov. Both methods are implemented in MATLAB and benchmarked on a shared server. Recommendations for selection between the two approaches based on available snapshots and frequency range requirements are given.
venue: Journal of Computational Acoustics and Mechanics

title: Mapping Common Procurement Vocabulary Codes to a Regional OWL Ontology: A Pilot Study
abstract: The Common Procurement Vocabulary (CPV) code system used in EU public procurement is not directly adopted in Western Balkan national portals, creating alignment barriers for cross-border suppliers. This paper describes the construction of a regional OWL 2 ontology that maps CPV 2008 codes to the procurement classification schemes of Serbia, Bosnia-Herzegovina, and North Macedonia. Using manual expert mapping supplemented by string-similarity heuristics, 4 812 CPV leaf classes were aligned to 3 290 regional counterparts, achieving a coverage ratio of 68.4 %. A prototype SPARQL endpoint was used to validate alignment consistency against 1 200 historical tender notices. Results show that direct equivalence mappings account for 51 % of aligned pairs, while skos:narrowMatch and skos:broadMatch account for 28 % and 21 % respectively. The paper discusses limitations arising from inconsistent national classification updates and proposes a lightweight governance model for maintaining the mapping over time.

title: Towards an Interoperability Reference Architecture for Western Balkan e-Procurement Portals
abstract: Interoperability between national e-procurement portals in the Western Balkans is constrained by divergent data models, legal frameworks, and technical standards. Drawing on the European Interoperability Framework (EIF) as a structural template, this chapter proposes a four-layer reference architecture covering legal, organisational, semantic, and technical dimensions specific to the region. The semantic layer centres on a shared core procurement ontology expressed in OWL 2 DL, with national extension modules accommodating jurisdiction-specific requirements. The organisational layer specifies a proposed regional coordination body and update procedures. The architecture is evaluated against three use cases: cross-border supplier registration, tender notice aggregation, and contract award transparency reporting. A gap analysis comparing the architecture against the then-current state of portals in Serbia, Montenegro, and Albania identifies 27 concrete technical barriers, of which 14 are classified as addressable through ontology alignment alone.

title: Alignment of the eProcurement Ontology with the Serbian Law on Public Procurement: A Formal Gap Analysis
abstract: The eProcurement Ontology (ePO) developed under the EU's ISA² programme formalises the concepts of the EU public procurement directives. Serbia's Law on Public Procurement, revised in 2012, shares many structural elements with EU directives but diverges in areas such as negotiated procedure thresholds, domestic preference provisions, and complaint handling. This paper conducts a systematic formal gap analysis by comparing ePO version 1.0 class and property definitions against the Serbian legal text, encoded as a structured glossary of 312 defined terms. Using a modular OWL extension pattern, 47 Serbia-specific classes and 19 properties are added to a national profile ontology, while 23 existing ePO classes require scope restriction through hasValue or allValuesFrom axioms. Reasoning experiments with HermiT 1.3 confirm that the extended ontology remains consistent and that the added axioms do not introduce unsatisfiable classes.

title: Using SPARQL Federation to Query Heterogeneous Procurement Linked Data Across Multiple Balkan Portals
abstract: When procurement data from multiple national portals is published as RDF linked data, federated SPARQL queries provide a mechanism for cross-border retrieval without requiring a centralised data warehouse. This paper reports on a controlled experiment in which RDF datasets derived from Serbian, Montenegrin, and Macedonian procurement portals—comprising 6 200, 2 100, and 3 800 notices respectively—were loaded into separate Virtuoso 7.1 instances. Eleven cross-portal query templates of varying complexity were executed using SPARQL 1.1 federation extensions. Query execution times ranged from 0.4 s for simple lookups to 187 s for multi-hop award-chain queries. Query rewriting strategies that push FILTER clauses closer to remote endpoints reduced average execution time by 34 %. The paper identifies cardinality estimation as the principal bottleneck and discusses practical trade-offs between federation and materialised integration for operational deployment.

title: Ontology-Based Validation Rules for Procurement Notice Quality Assurance in Transition Economies
abstract: Procurement notice data quality in transition economies is frequently undermined by incomplete fields, inconsistent classification, and erroneous date entries. This paper proposes a set of 58 SHACL constraint shapes derived from ePO and Serbian national profile axioms to validate procurement notices at point of submission. The constraint set was applied retrospectively to a random sample of 5 000 Serbian portal notices from 2013–2015. Validation identified at least one violation in 61 % of notices; the most frequent violations concern missing contracting authority NUTS codes (38 %), mismatched procedure type and estimated value (22 %), and absent award date in completed contracts (17 %). A subset of 12 constraints was implemented as a browser-based pre-submission checker and piloted with four contracting authorities during a three-month field trial. Pilot participants reduced validation failures by 74 % relative to a control group.

title: Controlled Vocabularies for Public Works Procurement in Serbia: Current State and Harmonisation Scenarios
abstract: Public works procurement in Serbia relies on a mixture of sector-specific classification schemes inherited from Yugoslav-era standards and informal thesauri maintained by individual contracting authorities. This paper surveys 11 distinct controlled vocabularies currently in use across central government, local government, and public enterprise procurers, covering approximately 9 400 distinct terms. Vocabulary characteristics—scope, granularity, maintenance body, machine-readability—are systematically compared. Three harmonisation scenarios are evaluated: (i) adoption of the EU CPV works subhierarchy without modification, (ii) a mapped national thesaurus preserving existing terms as preferred labels, and (iii) a federated polyhierarchy linking national and CPV terms through SKOS mappings. A survey of 34 procurement officers at the Serbian Public Procurement Office suggests scenario (ii) as the most practically acceptable, with 71 % of respondents indicating preference for familiar terminology.

title: Cross-Border eTendering Between Serbia and Hungary: Technical and Semantic Barriers
abstract: The Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia cross-border programme funds public infrastructure projects jointly managed by contracting authorities on both sides of the border. In practice, joint tendering is rare because of incompatible eTendering platforms and divergent semantic models. This paper documents the technical and semantic barriers through structured interviews with 12 contracting authorities and a comparative technical analysis of the Hungarian EKR and Serbian portal APIs. Semantic barriers include: incompatible bidder qualification ontologies, different XML schemas for technical specification attachments, and conflicting currency handling. A total of 31 barriers are catalogued. A semantic mediation layer based on RDF mappings and a shared SKOS qualification vocabulary is prototyped and demonstrated for the simplified procedure type applicable to joint infrastructure contracts. The prototype reduced manual re-keying of bidder data from an average of 4.2 h to 0.6 h per tender.

title: Ontology Modularisation Strategies for National Profile Extensions of the eProcurement Ontology
abstract: The eProcurement Ontology (ePO) is designed as a core ontology intended to be extended by national profiles. This paper evaluates three modularisation strategies—monolithic extension, module-per-jurisdiction, and aspect-oriented slicing—against criteria of reasoning scalability, maintainability, and alignment robustness. Experiments use synthetic datasets of 10 000, 50 000, and 200 000 procurement instances loaded into OWL 2 RL materialisation pipelines. Monolithic extension causes a 3.8× increase in reasoning time at 200 000 instances compared to module-per-jurisdiction. Aspect-oriented slicing reduces ontology load time by 61 % when only the qualification aspect is needed. A decision matrix for profile ontology architects is derived. The paper also reports on applying the module-per-jurisdiction strategy to produce a validated Serbian ePO national profile covering 89 % of the scope of the national procurement law.

title: Semantic Annotation of Procurement Contract Award Notices for Corruption Risk Detection: A Feasibility Study
abstract: Contract award notices contain structured signals that civil society organisations and oversight bodies use to assess corruption risk, but manual review is labour-intensive and inconsistent. This feasibility study explores whether semantic annotation of award notices with a purpose-built risk indicator ontology (PRIO) can support semi-automated risk scoring. PRIO defines 24 risk indicator classes derived from the academic literature and the OECD integrity framework. A sample of 3 600 Serbian award notices from 2017–2020 was annotated semi-automatically using a pipeline combining SHACL-derived feature extraction with a random forest classifier trained on 800 manually labelled notices. Precision and recall on a held-out test set of 400 notices were 0.78 and 0.71 respectively. The paper discusses ontological design choices that affect recall, particularly the granularity of single-bidder procedure classes, and proposes three ontology revisions to improve coverage.

title: Mapping eProcurement Ontology 3.1 to the OpenContracting Data Standard: A Bidirectional Alignment
abstract: The eProcurement Ontology (ePO) and the Open Contracting Data Standard (OCDS) both describe public procurement lifecycles but differ in their conceptual scope, granularity, and serialisation format. ePO is an OWL ontology targeting semantic reasoning; OCDS is a JSON Schema targeting publication and data exchange. This paper documents a bidirectional alignment between ePO 3.1 and OCDS 1.1.5. Alignment is expressed using a combination of SKOS mapping properties and SPARQL CONSTRUCT rules that generate OCDS-conformant JSON from ePO RDF instances. Coverage analysis shows that 83 % of OCDS fields can be populated from ePO triples without information loss, while 17 % require supplementary provenance or process fields absent from ePO. A reverse alignment from OCDS JSON to ePO RDF achieves 91 % property coverage. The alignment artefacts are tested on 420 Serbian and 310 Montenegrin procurement records.

title: A Linked Data Publication Framework for Western Balkan Public Procurement Registers: Design and Pilot Deployment
abstract: Western Balkan countries are under gradual pressure from EU accession conditionality to publish procurement data as open linked data. This paper describes the design and pilot deployment of a linked data publication framework, RegiLink, covering Serbia and Montenegro. The framework ingests data from national portals via REST APIs, applies RML mapping rules to convert portal records to ePO-conformant RDF, mints persistent URIs following a regional URI policy, and exposes the resulting datasets via a Virtuoso-based SPARQL endpoint and a Linked Data Fragments server. A pilot dataset covering 2022–2024 and containing 284 000 Serbian and 61 000 Montenegrin notices was published and validated. End-to-end latency from portal publication to triple store availability averages 4.1 hours. A user study with 11 data journalists and civil society analysts assessed the usability of the SPARQL interface and Linked Data Fragments client, finding the fragments interface preferable for exploratory querying by non-technical users.

title: A Metamodel for Compositional Enterprise Integration Patterns
abstract: Enterprise integration patterns (EIPs) are widely used as building blocks in message-oriented middleware, yet no formally grounded metamodel existed that captured their compositional semantics. This paper proposes a UML-profile-based metamodel covering 47 patterns drawn from canonical pattern catalogues, extended with OCL constraints that encode valid composition rules. The metamodel was validated against six open-source integration projects by manually mapping their routing logic to the proposed meta-level; conformance was measured at 89% of constructs successfully represented. A comparison with two earlier informal taxonomies shows that the proposed approach catches eight categories of composition error that the informal approaches do not distinguish. The work provides a foundation for automated tooling that checks integration model well-formedness before deployment.

title: Formal Verification of Message-Routing Compositions Using Alloy
abstract: Routing logic in enterprise integration systems can exhibit subtle deadlocks and message-loss faults that surface only under specific load conditions. This paper encodes a subset of EIP routing patterns—splitter, aggregator, content-based router, and filter—as Alloy signatures and predicates, allowing exhaustive bounded-scope analysis. Seventeen integration scenarios derived from production healthcare data-exchange systems were modelled; the Alloy Analyzer found counterexamples in four scenarios within scopes up to size 8, two of which were confirmed as real faults in the reference implementations. The encoding approach is described in sufficient detail to be reproducible, and the full Alloy models are provided as supplementary material. Execution times on a standard workstation ranged from 1.2 seconds to 47 minutes depending on scope and constraint density.

title: Survey of Model Transformation Approaches for Integration Architecture Migration
abstract: Legacy integration architectures are frequently migrated to service-oriented or event-driven platforms, yet the model transformation techniques employed are rarely compared systematically. This survey analyses 63 peer-reviewed papers published between 2003 and 2012 that describe transformation-based migration approaches. Papers are classified along five dimensions: source and target architectural style, transformation language used, degree of automation, evaluation method, and domain of application. ATL and QVT-Relations account for 54% of the surveyed approaches combined. Only 19 of the 63 papers report quantitative evaluation with more than one industrial case. The survey identifies gaps in traceability preservation and in handling of non-functional constraints during transformation, and proposes a research agenda for the subsequent five years. A replication package including the classification spreadsheet is available.

title: Interface Contract Specification for Event-Driven Microservices Using a Formal Pattern Language
abstract: Microservice architectures that rely on asynchronous messaging lack a standardised means of expressing interface contracts that go beyond data schema. This paper introduces a formal pattern language, denoted IPL-EDA, in which each interface contract specifies permitted message sequences, routing obligations, and timing constraints using a combination of regular expressions over message types and linear temporal logic formulae. IPL-EDA contracts are expressed as annotations on a service's OpenAPI-style description and checked automatically using a prototype contract verifier. An evaluation against a synthetic benchmark of 120 service pairs and a real logistics platform with 14 services shows that the verifier detects 91% of injected contract violations with a false-positive rate of 3.2%. Annotation overhead averages 38 additional lines per service description.

title: Towards a Formal Semantics for the Saga Pattern in Distributed Transaction Management
abstract: The Saga pattern decomposes a distributed transaction into a sequence of local transactions with compensating actions, but existing descriptions in the literature are informal and implementation-dependent. This paper gives a formal operational semantics for Sagas using labelled transition systems, covering both choreography-based and orchestration-based variants. Fifteen Saga implementations taken from open-source repositories were encoded in the formal model; model checking with SPIN revealed two previously unreported scenarios in which compensating actions could be skipped under concurrent failure. The formalisation also clarifies the relationship between Sagas and the classical two-phase commit protocol, showing that two-phase commit is a degenerate Saga under additional locking assumptions. The paper is intended as groundwork for future tool support rather than an industrial deployment guide.
venue: Electronic Notes in Theoretical Computer Science (Balkan Series)
