title: Model-Driven Configuration of API Gateways from Architectural Intent
abstract: API gateway products such as reverse proxies and service meshes require extensive low-level configuration that must remain consistent with a system's intended integration architecture. This paper proposes a two-layer approach: an architecture-level model expressed in a lightweight DSL captures routing intent, authentication boundaries, and rate-limiting policies; a set of ATL transformations then generates gateway-specific configuration files for two target platforms. An evaluation conducted on a medium-sized e-commerce platform with 31 services compared manually written configuration with generated configuration on seven quality criteria. Generated configuration had fewer inconsistencies (4 vs. 19) and reduced configuration size by 28% on average through deduplication of repeated policy blocks. Round-trip regeneration after architectural change took under 90 seconds for the largest tested model.

title: Consistency Checking Between Architectural Models and Runtime Integration Behaviour
abstract: Architectural drift—the divergence between a documented software architecture and the system as actually deployed—is a common maintenance problem. This paper addresses drift detection in integration-heavy systems by instrumenting message brokers to capture runtime message-flow graphs and comparing them against the architectural intent model using a graph-homomorphism-based matching algorithm. The approach was evaluated on two industrial systems: a logistics information platform and a public-sector document-exchange infrastructure. In the logistics system, 11 undocumented message paths and three deprecated routes still receiving traffic were detected automatically within a 72-hour observation window. Precision was 94% and recall 88% relative to manually verified ground truth. The paper also discusses how detected deviations can be fed back to update the architectural model semi-automatically.

title: Interface Adaptation Strategies for Heterogeneous IoT Device Integration: A Model-Driven Study
abstract: Industrial IoT deployments regularly combine devices that communicate over incompatible protocols—MQTT, CoAP, Modbus, and proprietary serial formats are common simultaneously. This paper applies the model-driven adapter generation framework developed in earlier work to IoT device integration, extending the original finite-state-machine interface model with data-type coercion rules and timing constraints specific to sensor data streams. Twelve device pairs from a smart-factory pilot in Vojvodina were used as test cases; nine generated adapters functioned correctly without modification, two required minor timing adjustments, and one could not be handled due to a stateful proprietary protocol. Adapter round-trip latency overhead was measured at 1.8 ms median on a Raspberry Pi 4, which was acceptable for all non-real-time use cases in the pilot.

title: Specification and Automated Verification of Choreography Contracts in Event-Driven Systems: Lessons from Three Industrial Cases
abstract: Choreography-level contracts define the observable interaction obligations of multiple participants in a distributed system without centralising control. This paper reports on the application of a contract specification language based on multiparty session types to three real industrial systems: a regional healthcare interoperability platform, a customs document exchange service, and a retail supply-chain event bus. For each system, existing informal specifications were re-expressed as session-typed choreographies and checked for well-formedness and progress guarantees. The process uncovered two liveness violations in the healthcare system and one safety violation in the customs system that had manifested as intermittent timeout errors in production. The paper discusses the practical friction involved in eliciting the information needed for formal specification from integration teams unfamiliar with formal methods, and proposes a lightweight elicitation protocol.

title: Occlusion-Aware LOD Transitions Without Popping Artefacts Using Temporal Blending in WebGPU
abstract: Abrupt LOD transitions produce visible popping artefacts that degrade user experience in 3D web applications, particularly during camera motion. This paper proposes a temporal blending strategy in which the outgoing and incoming LOD meshes are both rendered for a short overlap window and their contributions linearly interpolated using a per-pixel alpha accumulated in a history buffer. The approach is implemented entirely in WebGPU using a two-attachment render pass and a resolve compute pass. Five transition scenarios were tested: flyover, close approach, lateral pan, static scene with dynamic lighting, and object rotation. A 28-participant study comparing temporal blending with three alternative anti-popping methods (alpha testing, morphing via vertex attributes, dithered cross-fade) found that temporal blending received the highest fidelity ratings in three of five scenarios. Frame overhead of the resolve pass was 0.9 ms at 1920×1080 on a mid-range discrete GPU. Limitations under rapid camera motion and high polygon-count transitions are discussed.

title: Benchmarking Embedded Lossy Compressors for Structural Health Monitoring on a 32-Node Piezoelectric Sensor Array
abstract: Structural health monitoring of bridges and tunnels increasingly relies on dense piezoelectric sensor arrays generating sustained data rates of hundreds of kilobytes per second. This paper benchmarks seven embedded lossy compressors — including DPCM, adaptive PLA, Haar filterbank, spectral peak preservation, and three variants of learned vector quantisation — on a 32-node wireless array deployed on a pedestrian footbridge in Novi Sad over four weeks. Evaluation metrics include compression ratio, reconstruction SNR, preservation of guided-wave arrival time picks (used for damage localisation), and energy per sample. The learned vector quantiser with 256-centroid codebook trained offline on historical data achieved the best damage-localisation accuracy (mean error 4.8 cm at 8:1 compression) but required 24 kB of flash for the codebook. Adaptive PLA achieved competitive localisation accuracy (mean error 6.1 cm) with only 2.1 kB of code and data memory. Practical trade-off recommendations are given for deployment scenarios constrained by either memory or localisation precision requirements.

title: Latency-Bounded VNF Placement Under Fluctuating Traffic in Regional ISP Networks
abstract: Meeting end-to-end latency budgets for latency-sensitive VNF chains in regional ISP networks requires placement decisions that account for traffic variability. This paper proposes a two-stage stochastic programming model where the first stage determines VNF-to-server assignment and the second stage routes traffic across scenarios sampled from a 30-day flow-level measurement trace collected from a mid-sized Serbian ISP with 22 PoPs. Scenarios are reduced to 50 representative samples using k-medoids clustering on traffic matrices. The stochastic model is compared against a deterministic peak-load formulation and a reactive re-placement heuristic. The stochastic approach reduces constraint violations by 37% versus deterministic placement under median traffic conditions while using 12% fewer server resources. The paper characterises which VNF types (firewall, DPI, NAT) are most sensitive to traffic variability and recommends placement policies for each.

title: Detecting Implicit Dependencies Introduced by Code Generators in Polyglot Build Pipelines
abstract: Code generation steps—protocol buffer compilation, OpenAPI client generation, lexer/parser generation—introduce implicit dependencies that are absent from hand-written BUILD files. If these are not recorded, incremental build systems may silently produce stale artifacts. We present a dynamic tracing approach that intercepts file-system calls during a full build to discover implicit edges, then infers a static approximation using file naming conventions and generator invocation patterns. Applied to eleven repositories using at least two distinct code generators each, the tracing step uncovered a median of 47 undeclared edges per repository. We evaluated whether the static approximation, computed without tracing, could recover these edges, achieving an F1 score of 0.84 averaged across repositories. Cases where the static approach failed are categorised and used to motivate three proposed BUILD file annotations that would make implicit dependencies machine-readable.

title: Izgradnja invertovanog indeksa za srpske tekstove sa mešovitim pismom: osnovna metodologija
abstract: U radu se opisuje metodologija izgradnje invertovanog indeksa koji istovremeno obrađuje ćirilična i latinična pojavljivanja srpskih reči bez prethodnog potpunog prevođenja u jedno pismo. Predloženi postupak uključuje korak normalizacije tokena kojim se za svaki token generiše kanonska forma zasnovana na fonemskoj reprezentaciji, a zatim se fonemski ključevi koriste kao primarni identifikatori u indeksu. Eksperimenti su sprovedeni na korpusu od 120 000 novinskih članaka preuzetih iz tri srpska dnevna lista u periodu 2000–2008. Mere preciznosti i odziva upoređene su s dva bazična sistema koji koriste isključivo ćirilični, odnosno isključivo latinični indeks. Predloženi sistem postiže F1 vrednost od 0,81 u zadatku ad-hoc pretrage, što je povećanje od 14 procentnih poena u odnosu na bolji od dva bazična sistema. Rad takođe razmatra pitanje memorijskog otiska hibridnog indeksa i predlaže strategiju kompresije rečnika.

title: Phoneme-Based Token Canonicalization for Serbian Script Unification
abstract: Serbian is officially written in both Cyrillic and Latin scripts, and documents frequently contain tokens in both scripts within a single sentence or paragraph. This paper presents a token canonicalization procedure in which each token is mapped to a phoneme sequence using deterministic grapheme-to-phoneme rules derived from Serbian orthographic conventions, and the resulting phoneme string serves as the canonical form for retrieval purposes. We evaluated the approach on a manually annotated gold standard of 4 200 query–document relevance pairs drawn from a legal corpus of 38 000 court decisions. The phoneme-based canonical form reduced the out-of-vocabulary rate from 9.3% to 2.1% compared with a Latin-only baseline and from 11.7% to 2.4% compared with a Cyrillic-only baseline. Precision at rank 10 improved by 8 percentage points over both baselines. Edge cases involving foreign loanwords and proper nouns are discussed, and a set of override rules is proposed for the 230 most frequent exceptions identified in the corpus.

title: Cross-Script Query Expansion Using Transliteration Variants in Serbian Web Search
abstract: Users searching Serbian-language web content often type queries in one script while relevant documents are stored in the other. This paper studies the effect of automatically expanding queries with their transliteration variants before submission to an inverted index. We constructed a test collection of 1 800 queries and 210 000 web pages crawled from .rs domains, with relevance judgments pooled from four assessors. Three expansion strategies were compared: (1) appending the full transliteration variant, (2) appending only tokens whose transliteration differs from the original by more than two characters, and (3) expanding only named entities detected by a rule-based tagger. Strategy 3 achieved the best mean average precision of 0.497, versus 0.431 for no expansion, while reducing index bloat to 6% over the baseline index size. We also report retrieval latency measurements on a commodity server, showing that the overhead introduced by expansion remains under 12 ms at the 95th percentile for queries up to eight tokens.

title: Automatska detekcija i korekcija nedoslednosti pisma u srpskim digitalnim arhivima
abstract: Digitalni arhivi srpskih novina i institucionalnih dokumenata često sadrže nedoslednosti gde je isti dokument delom u ćirilici, a delom u latinici, ponekad zbog grešaka pri skeniranju ili uredničkih intervencija. Ovaj rad predlaže metod automatske detekcije takvih nedoslednosti na nivou rečenice, korišćenjem klasifikatora koji kao atribute uzima raspodelu skriptnih blokova, učestalosti bigrama i morfosintaksičke signale. Klasifikator je treniran na 9 400 ručno označenih rečenica iz arhive jednog novosadskog lista i testiran na 2 100 rečenica iz arhive beogradskog lista. Postiže preciznost od 0,91 i odziv od 0,88 u klasi nedoslednih rečenica. Korak korekcije primenjuje fonemsku transliteraciju na detektovane nedosledne tokene. Eksperiment na donstremu (pretragom dokumenta) pokazuje da korigovana verzija arhive daje veću tačnost od nekorigovane za 7 procentnih poena u prosečnoj preciznosti.

title: A Benchmark Corpus for Mixed-Script Serbian Information Retrieval
abstract: Reproducible evaluation of retrieval systems for Serbian requires a shared test collection that explicitly accounts for mixed-script documents. This paper describes the construction of SrMIR-1, a benchmark corpus comprising 95 000 documents from four genres — news, law, literature, and social media — with 600 topics and graded relevance judgments produced by 12 trained assessors following TREC-style pooling at depth 30. Approximately 41% of documents contain tokens in both scripts. Inter-assessor agreement, measured by Cohen's kappa, was 0.73 across all topics. The paper reports baseline results for five retrieval models: BM25, language modelling with Dirichlet smoothing, a transliteration-aware BM25 variant, a neural dense retrieval model fine-tuned on Serbian, and a hybrid sparse–dense model. The transliteration-aware BM25 variant achieves the highest nDCG@10 of 0.531 among sparse models, while the hybrid model reaches 0.587. The corpus is publicly available under a Creative Commons licence.

title: Indeksiranje pravnih dokumenata sa heterogenim pismom: studija slučaja sudske prakse u Srbiji
abstract: Sudske odluke u Srbiji nastajale su kroz nekoliko decenija u različitim pisarskim praksama i sistemima za obradu teksta, što je rezultovalo korpusom u kome se isti pravni termin pojavljuje u ćiriličnom i latiničnom obliku, ponekad unutar istog paragrafa. Ovaj rad opisuje sistem za pretragu koji je prilagođen ovoj karakteristici i koji se koristi u pilot projektu jednog regionalnog suda. Sistem koristi troslojan pristup: normalizaciju pisma, pravno-specifičnu listu sinonima i rangirač koji uvažava strukturu dokumenta (izreka, obrazloženje, dispozitiv). Evaluacija je sprovedena na 5 800 upita sudskog osoblja tokom tromesečnog pilot perioda. Sistem je postigao prosečnu preciznost od 0,74, uz korisničku ocenu zadovoljstva 4,1 od 5. Rad diskutuje tehničke i organizacione izazove uvođenja pretražnog sistema u pravnu praksu.

title: Script-Aware Passage Retrieval for Serbian Question Answering
abstract: Open-domain question answering over Serbian-language document collections requires a passage retrieval component that is robust to the script in which both the question and the passage are written. This paper describes an adaptation of a BM25-based passage retrieval pipeline in which the tokenizer applies script normalization before indexing and at query time. We built an evaluation set of 340 factoid questions with 1 to 4 correct passages each, drawn from a mixed-script encyclopedia-style corpus of 180 000 passages. We compared four configurations: BM25 with no normalization, BM25 with script normalization, a dense bi-encoder model trained on Serbian data, and a hybrid of the latter two. The script-normalized BM25 retrieves at least one correct passage in the top 20 for 72% of questions, a gain of 17 percentage points over unnormalized BM25. The hybrid model reaches 81%. Failure analysis highlights questions containing transliterated foreign proper nouns as the main remaining challenge.

title: Normalizacija skripte u kontekstu pretraživača internih dokumenata za mala i srednja preduzeća: iskustva iz prakse
abstract: Mala i srednja preduzeća u Srbiji čuvaju interne dokumente — ugovore, zapisnike, izveštaje — u mešovitom pismu bez konzistentne politike. Ovaj rad opisuje iskustva iz tri pilot implementacije interne pretrage zasnovane na open-source pretražnom okviru dopunjenom modulom za normalizaciju pisma razvijenim u okviru naše istraživačke grupe. Pilot kompanije imale su kolekcije između 8 000 i 45 000 dokumenata. Merili smo preciznost pretrage pre i posle uvođenja normalizacije, korisnički odaziv i troškove uvođenja. U svim slučajevima normalizacija je poboljšala preciznost za najmanje 11 procentnih poena. Administrativni troškovi uvođenja bili su niski jer je modul integrisan kao dodatak bez izmene ostatka sistema. Rad identifikuje i ograničenja: module treba ažurirati kada kompanija uvede novu terminologiju u jednom pismu, jer inicijalni rečnik sinonima nije potpun.

title: SrMIR-2: Extending the Mixed-Script Serbian Retrieval Benchmark to Social Media and Administrative Registers
abstract: SrMIR-1, released in 2017, covered news, law, literature, and general web content. Since then, social media posts and administrative e-government documents have become important retrieval targets, both exhibiting pronounced script mixing and informal orthography. This paper describes SrMIR-2, which adds two new document registers to the benchmark: 60 000 posts from a Serbian microblogging platform and 28 000 administrative forms and decisions from three municipal e-government portals. We created 280 new topics for these registers with relevance judgments from six trained assessors (kappa = 0.69). Baseline experiments show that script-normalizing BM25 outperforms unnormalized BM25 by a larger margin on social media (22 percentage points in nDCG@10) than on administrative documents (9 points), attributable to the higher rate of informal transliteration in social media. The benchmark is released with code for reproducible evaluation. We also report an ablation study isolating the contribution of named-entity handling in the normalization pipeline.

title: Latency–Accuracy Trade-offs in Script-Normalizing Retrieval Pipelines Under Production Load
abstract: Deploying script-normalizing retrieval in production requires careful attention to latency, especially when normalization involves neural components. This paper presents a systematic study of trade-offs along the latency–accuracy spectrum for five pipeline configurations ranging from a purely deterministic rule-based normalizer to a full transformer-based normalizer, tested on a simulated production workload derived from query logs of a Serbian news aggregator with peak loads of 340 queries per second. We measure mean reciprocal rank, P@5, and end-to-end latency at the 50th, 90th, and 99th percentiles on a server cluster of four nodes. The deterministic normalizer adds 3 ms median latency with MRR of 0.61. The transformer-based normalizer achieves MRR of 0.68 but adds 47 ms at the 99th percentile. A cascaded configuration — deterministic normalizer with neural fallback triggered only for out-of-vocabulary tokens — reaches MRR of 0.66 with a 99th-percentile latency overhead of only 9 ms. Detailed profiling data and configuration files are provided.

title: A Corpus Study of Designer Intent Encoding in Commercial Game Level Data
abstract: Understanding how human designers encode intent in level geometry is necessary for building generators that align with design goals. We manually annotated 620 levels from six released commercial-style games distributed under open licenses, tagging 14 categories of spatial intent including chokepoint placement, reward pacing, and difficulty escalation. Inter-annotator agreement reached Cohen's κ = 0.71 across three annotators. Statistical analysis reveals that chokepoint density correlates negatively with level width-to-length ratio (Pearson r = −0.43, p < 0.001) and that reward pacing patterns cluster into four archetypes by k-means on pacing-curve descriptors. We use these findings to propose a vocabulary of 14 soft-constraint templates that can be embedded in a CSP-based generator. Preliminary generation tests using three templates show that 73% of generated levels are classified into the intended archetype by a trained SVM classifier.

title: Sampling Theorems on Homogeneous Trees via Spectral Theory of the Laplace Operator
abstract: Homogeneous trees of degree q+1 carry a natural group structure when q is a prime power, allowing the application of harmonic analysis on p-adic groups. This paper establishes a Whittaker–Shannon-type sampling theorem for band-limited functions on such trees, where band-limitation is defined via the spherical Fourier transform and the spectrum of the combinatorial Laplacian. We prove that the critical sampling density for exact reconstruction equals (q+1)/2q per vertex in the natural metric on the tree, and provide an explicit interpolation formula using spherical functions as kernels. Stability under perturbation of sample locations is quantified in terms of the tree's girth. Numerical experiments on trees with q = 2, 3, 5 show that the interpolation formula converges in at most 15 iterations of a conjugate-gradient scheme to relative errors below 10^{-8}.
venue: Proceedings of the Applied Harmonic Analysis Conference (AHAC 2021), online

title: A Comparison of Signature Truncation Depths for Short Financial Price Paths
abstract: The path signature of a continuous or piecewise-linear path provides a graded sequence of features whose informational content grows with truncation depth. In practice, choosing a truncation depth involves a trade-off between feature dimensionality and expressive power. We study this trade-off systematically on intraday foreign-exchange price paths of varying length, constructed from one-minute mid-price data over a 24-month window covering four currency pairs. For each path length (30, 60, 120, and 240 minutes) and truncation depth (2 through 6), we train a regularised logistic regression to predict direction of the subsequent 15-minute return, reporting area under the ROC curve across 500 walk-forward validation windows. Depth 4 consistently offers the best accuracy-to-dimensionality ratio across all path lengths tested, with depth 5 providing marginal gains at substantially higher cost when the number of channels exceeds 5. We further show that lead-lag transformation of the bivariate price-volume path before signature extraction improves AUC by an average of 0.023. These findings provide practical guidance for practitioners applying signature methods to financial tick data without access to large computational budgets.

title: A PC-Based Real-Time Target for Engine Control Unit Testing Using RTAI-Linux and a Low-Cost DAQ Board
abstract: This paper describes the construction and validation of a low-cost hardware-in-the-loop (HiL) test bench built around a standard x86 PC running RTAI-Linux 3.8 and a commercially available 16-channel analog/digital acquisition board. The setup was used to emulate the sensor and actuator environment of a diesel engine management ECU supplied by a regional automotive Tier-1 supplier. A mean-value engine model with six state variables was implemented and executed at a fixed step size of 1 ms, achieving worst-case jitter below 35 µs across a 4-hour continuous run. CAN communication between the real-time host and the ECU was handled through a standard USB-to-CAN adapter operating at 500 kbit/s. Forty-two ECU software variants were tested against a library of 180 deterministic test cases covering cold-start, idle, and wide-open-throttle scenarios. The paper reports pass/fail statistics, timing overhead, and the cost breakdown of the bench, which totaled under 1 200 EUR in hardware. Limitations related to I/O bandwidth and USB latency are discussed and partly mitigated through interrupt coalescing.

title: Modelling and Real-Time Implementation of a Brushless DC Motor Drive for HiL Emulation of Electric Power Steering Loads
abstract: Electric power steering (EPS) systems place demanding requirements on HiL test benches because the steering column torque sensor and motor current feedback must be emulated at update rates below 500 µs. This work presents a BLDC motor model parameterised from bench measurements on a 48 V, 400 W motor taken from a mid-class passenger car. The model captures back-EMF harmonics up to the 7th order and includes a thermal sub-model with two lumped time constants. It was compiled to a Xilinx Spartan-6 FPGA using a fixed-point arithmetic pipeline operating at 50 MHz, achieving a simulation step of 20 µs. Analog outputs were generated through on-board 16-bit DACs. A comparison between the FPGA model and a reference floating-point Simulink simulation showed RMS current errors below 1.2% over standard SAE J266 steering manoeuvres. The paper also quantifies resource utilisation: 31% of available LUTs and 18% of DSP48 blocks on the target device.

title: Fault Injection Framework for Automotive Body Control Module Testing on an Open-Source HiL Platform
abstract: Body control modules (BCMs) must tolerate a range of electrical faults including open circuits, shorts to battery and shorts to ground on their I/O lines. Commercial HiL systems provide programmable fault relays, but their cost is prohibitive for small development teams. This paper presents a fault injection board designed around solid-state relay arrays and a microcontroller interface, integrated with a Beaglebone Black running a Xenomai real-time patch as the simulation host. The board supports 32 independent fault channels switchable within 2 ms. A BCM with 28 digital outputs and 14 analog inputs was tested under 96 fault combinations derived from ISO 26262 FMEA tables. The framework detected seven previously unreported software anomalies in the BCM firmware relating to debounce timer behaviour under simultaneous multi-line faults. Replication cost for the fault injection hardware was 340 EUR per board. The design files and driver code are released under a permissive open-source licence.

title: Latency Characterisation of Open-Source Real-Time Kernels for Automotive HIL Applications
abstract: Several open-source options exist for turning a general-purpose Linux system into a deterministic real-time platform: RTAI, Xenomai 3, and the PREEMPT_RT patch. This paper provides a systematic comparison of all three on two hardware platforms—a standard Intel Core i5 desktop and an ARM Cortex-A9 single-board computer—under automotive HiL workloads. Latency was measured using a hardware timer circuit with 100 ns resolution over 72-hour test windows while simultaneously running a 23-state vehicle dynamics model, a CAN stack, and a UDP telemetry stream. Xenomai 3 with the Cobalt core achieved the lowest worst-case latency on the x86 platform at 18 µs, while PREEMPT_RT showed marginally better throughput at the cost of 47 µs worst-case. On the ARM platform, Xenomai 3 and PREEMPT_RT performed comparably. The paper provides configuration recipes, kernel version numbers, and patch sets used, making the results reproducible. Recommendations are given for selecting a kernel flavour based on step-size and I/O bandwidth requirements.

title: Integration of a FlexRay Bus Interface into a Low-Cost FPGA-Based HiL Bench for Chassis Domain ECU Testing
abstract: FlexRay is used in safety-critical chassis domains such as active suspension and brake-by-wire. Integrating a FlexRay interface into a low-cost HiL platform is non-trivial because commercially licensed IP cores are expensive. This work documents the integration of an open FlexRay communication controller implemented in VHDL on a Xilinx Artix-7 FPGA with a Linux-based simulation host connected via PCIe. The controller supports static segment scheduling with a cycle time of 5 ms and up to 64 frame slots. Two ABS/ESC ECUs from a regional supplier were used as devices under test. The paper reports successful execution of 214 scheduled test sequences covering wheel speed sensor emulation, hydraulic pressure command injection, and inter-ECU synchronisation checks. Timing accuracy of the FlexRay frames was within ±250 ns of nominal, verified with a dedicated bus analyser. Integration effort and remaining limitations regarding the dynamic segment are also discussed.

title: A Semi-Automated Test Case Generation Method for ECU Validation Based on Boundary-Value Analysis of CAN Signal Databases
abstract: ECU test suites are typically assembled manually from specification documents, which is time-consuming and incomplete. This paper describes a tool that parses CANdb++ DBC files to extract signal definitions—including physical ranges, factors, offsets, and initial values—and automatically generates boundary-value and equivalence-partition test cases for each signal. The tool was applied to two DBC databases: one covering a powertrain domain (312 signals, 47 message IDs) and one covering a body domain (198 signals, 31 message IDs). Test case counts of 1 847 and 1 203 were produced respectively and executed on the low-cost HiL bench described in earlier work. Execution time per test case averaged 4.3 seconds on the powertrain database. Twelve defects were identified in the body domain ECU firmware that manual testing had not found, including three out-of-range handling errors and two incorrect default value responses. The paper discusses integration with a lightweight Python-based test management framework and export to an XML format compatible with standard reporting tools.

title: Power Consumption Profiling of Real-Time Simulation Targets Under Variable ECU Testing Workloads
abstract: HiL test benches in embedded development teams often run continuously for extended periods. Understanding their power draw is important for infrastructure planning and for estimating operational costs. This paper presents power measurements taken on four representative real-time targets—an x86 mini-ITX board, a Raspberry Pi 4, a Beaglebone AI, and a Xilinx Zynq-7020 SoC board—while running engine, transmission, and body domain simulation workloads at step sizes of 0.5, 1, and 2 ms. Power was logged at 1 Hz using a calibrated USB power meter and a bench power supply with current monitoring. The x86 platform consumed 38–54 W depending on workload, while the Zynq SoC consumed 4.1–6.8 W for equivalent model complexity. Thermal imaging was used to identify hot spots on each board. The paper also discusses the trade-off between determinism margin and power saving modes, noting that CPU frequency scaling degraded worst-case latency by up to 90 µs on the x86 platform when not properly managed.

title: Containerised Deployment of Real-Time ECU Test Environments Using Docker and Xenomai on Embedded Linux Platforms
abstract: Reproducing a specific HiL software environment across multiple bench instances and over time is a persistent problem in automotive software development. This paper investigates whether Docker containers can be used to encapsulate the user-space components of a Xenomai 3 real-time application—model binaries, CAN stack configuration, test scripts—while the host kernel retains the Cobalt real-time core. Experiments were conducted on two identical Raspberry Pi 4 platforms running an identical Xenomai-patched kernel. Containerised and native deployments were compared for latency, throughput, and deployment time across three ECU test suites. Worst-case latency overhead introduced by the container runtime was 3 µs in all measured cases, considered acceptable for step sizes of 1 ms and above. Deployment time was reduced from approximately 45 minutes of manual setup to under 6 minutes. The paper also describes a versioning workflow using a private registry and discusses limitations when hardware access to GPIO and CAN interfaces is required inside the container.

title: Ethernet-Based Time-Sensitive Networking as a Backbone for Distributed Automotive HiL Benches: Feasibility Assessment
abstract: As automotive architectures shift toward Ethernet-based in-vehicle networks, HiL benches must emulate Ethernet traffic alongside classical fieldbuses. This preprint reports preliminary measurements on using IEEE 802.1AS time synchronisation and 802.1Qbv time-aware shaper on a three-node distributed HiL bench where each node hosts a partial vehicle subsystem model. Nodes are connected through a managed switch with TSN support. Clock synchronisation accuracy between nodes was measured at 120 ns RMS over a 48-hour window using a shared GPS-disciplined reference. Model state exchange over scheduled Ethernet frames at 1 ms intervals showed zero missed deadlines in a 24-hour test. The preprint describes the network configuration, measurement methodology, and a preliminary cost comparison against dedicated real-time Ethernet solutions. Limitations include the current absence of a fault simulation capability for the TSN link itself. Full journal submission is planned after completing automotive protocol conformance tests.

title: A method for simultaneous identification of geometric and thermal error parameters using a laser tracker and redundant joint sensors
abstract: Standard kinematic calibration and thermal error identification are usually performed as sequential, separate procedures, which introduces coupling errors when both geometric drift and thermal expansion are active simultaneously. This paper formulates a unified parameter identification problem that simultaneously estimates the 24 DH parameters and 12 thermal expansion coefficients from a single measurement campaign. A Gauss–Newton algorithm with regularisation was used to solve the combined 36-parameter system. The measurement campaign consisted of 480 TCP position measurements acquired with a FARO laser tracker at six thermal states ranging from cold start to full thermal equilibrium. Compared with sequential identification, the unified approach reduced the RMS TCP error on a 240-point validation set from 0.13 mm to 0.09 mm. Condition number analysis confirmed that geometric and thermal subspaces are distinguishable provided measurements are taken at a minimum of four distinct thermal states. The method is compatible with standard industrial laser tracker workflows without requiring specialised fixturing.

title: Adaptive Safety Distance Margins Under Varying Human Motion Speed: An Online Estimation Approach
abstract: Fixed safety distance margins in speed-and-separation monitoring are conservative because they are sized for the fastest plausible human motion. This paper investigates an online estimation scheme that continuously updates the human velocity upper bound used in the margin calculation based on a sliding window of measured velocities from the current work session. A robust estimator based on exponentially weighted order statistics is applied to 200 ms velocity windows, producing an updated margin every control cycle. The scheme was tested in a 90-minute laboratory experiment with 18 participants performing assembly tasks at self-selected pace. Compared to the ISO/TS 15066 worst-case fixed margin, the adaptive scheme reduced the mean protective distance by 13 cm without any margin underestimations relative to the participant's actual worst-case velocity in that session. Safety guarantees under the scheme are discussed with reference to the assumptions required for the estimator to remain conservative.

title: Effect of imposed soil water deficit on phenylpropanoid pathway gene expression and anthocyanin yield in Sambucus nigra
abstract: Twelve elderberry cuttings of a single Pannonian-origin accession were subjected to four levels of soil water potential (−0.03, −0.1, −0.3, and −0.8 MPa) in a controlled greenhouse experiment over 60 days. Leaf gas exchange, shoot elongation, and berry dry mass were monitored weekly. At harvest, total anthocyanin content in berries increased by 34% under the −0.3 MPa treatment relative to well-watered controls, while it declined sharply at −0.8 MPa, coinciding with a 62% reduction in berry fresh mass. Reverse transcription PCR targeting chalcone synthase and dihydroflavonol 4-reductase transcripts showed up-regulation at moderate stress and suppression at severe stress. The results indicate a threshold response, with moderate water deficit acting as a mild elicitor of polyphenol accumulation without substantially compromising yield. Implications for irrigation management in commercial elderberry cultivation are discussed.

title: Comparative evaluation of feature descriptors for outdoor point cloud classification: FPFH, SHOT, and learned local features
abstract: Classical handcrafted feature descriptors and early learned representations are compared on a benchmark comprising five outdoor scenes captured with a Velodyne HDL-64E mobile scanner in Novi Sad and Subotica. The dataset contains roughly 4.5 million labelled points across eight semantic classes including ground, building, vegetation, vehicle, and street furniture. Fast Point Feature Histograms (FPFH) and Signature of Histograms of Orientations (SHOT) are evaluated alongside a shallow PointNet-style encoder trained from scratch. Mean intersection-over-union (mIoU) scores are 51.4% for FPFH with a random forest classifier, 54.9% for SHOT, and 62.8% for the learned encoder, all using identical training and test splits. Error analysis reveals that the building class benefits most from learned features due to heterogeneous surface textures, whereas ground and vegetation classification is robust across all three approaches. The benchmark data and evaluation scripts are released publicly.

title: Fitting Heavy-Tailed Severity Distributions to Internal Operational Loss Data: A Comparison of Lognormal, Pareto and Weibull Specifications
abstract: This paper evaluates three parametric families—lognormal, generalised Pareto, and Weibull—for modelling the severity of operational loss events recorded in the internal loss database of a mid-sized Central European bank over 2001–2008. The dataset comprises 1 147 loss observations across six Basel II event-type categories. Parameters are estimated by maximum likelihood and L-moments; goodness-of-fit is assessed via Anderson–Darling and Kolmogorov–Smirnov statistics. For the external fraud and internal fraud categories, the generalised Pareto distribution with shape parameter estimated between 0.31 and 0.47 provides the best fit at the 5% significance level. For technology-related events, the lognormal remains competitive. The paper discusses implications for regulatory capital calculation under the Advanced Measurement Approach and recommends a mixed strategy in which the severity model is selected per business-line and event-type cell rather than applied uniformly. Sensitivity of Value-at-Risk at the 99.9% confidence level to distributional choice is shown to be substantial, with differences reaching 34% of the point estimate.

title: Poisson versus Negative Binomial Frequency Models for Operational Risk Event Counts: Evidence from a Serbian Banking Panel
abstract: Accurate frequency modelling is a prerequisite for credible operational Value-at-Risk estimation. This study tests whether the Poisson assumption for annual event counts is tenable using a balanced panel of eight Serbian commercial banks observed over 2005–2011, yielding 56 bank–year observations and 4 312 individual loss records obtained under a data-sharing agreement with the National Bank of Serbia. Likelihood-ratio tests and Vuong's statistic consistently reject equidispersion for five of the seven event-type categories examined, favouring the negative binomial specification. Estimated dispersion parameters range from 0.18 to 1.63 across categories. Monte Carlo experiments with 100 000 replications show that using Poisson instead of the negative binomial inflates the 99.9th-percentile aggregate loss estimate by 8–22% depending on severity tail weight. The paper recommends routine overdispersion testing as part of model validation procedures.

title: Threshold Selection for Extreme Value Modelling of IT Security Incident Costs in Financial Institutions
abstract: Applying extreme value theory to information security loss data requires a principled choice of threshold above which the generalised Pareto distribution is fitted. This paper compares four threshold selection methods—mean excess plot inspection, the Hill estimator stability plot, the automated metric of Danielsson and de Vries, and a minimum-distance criterion—using a synthetic dataset of 2 000 IT security incident costs constructed to resemble patterns reported in industry loss databases. The distribution of costs follows a mixture with a light-bodied bulk below USD 50 000 and a heavy tail above. Results show that automated methods select thresholds 15–30% higher than graphical inspection, leading to shape parameter estimates that differ by up to 0.12 and to 99th-percentile loss estimates differing by up to 28%. A bootstrap confidence interval procedure for the threshold-conditional GPD fit is proposed and illustrated. The findings have direct relevance for cyber risk capital allocation in small and medium financial institutions.

title: Operational Risk Capital Models Under Basel III: A Textbook Treatment with Worked Examples
abstract: This book chapter provides a structured exposition of the Loss Distribution Approach as implemented under Basel III requirements, written for graduate students in banking and finance. It begins with the actuarial foundations of compound distributions, proceeds through parameter estimation and Monte Carlo aggregation, and concludes with capital allocation across business lines using the Euler principle. Worked numerical examples use publicly available ORX consortium summary statistics. The chapter also covers the Standardised Measurement Approach introduced in the 2017 Basel Committee consultative document and discusses the tension between model complexity and supervisory comparability. An appendix provides annotated R code for a complete LDA workflow including fitting, simulation, and sensitivity analysis. The chapter is intended as course material for advanced risk management modules.

title: Estimating the Annual Frequency of Data Breach Events in European Financial Services: A Regression-Based Approach Using Publicly Reported Incidents
abstract: This study models the annual frequency of externally reported data breach events affecting European financial services firms over the period 2008–2015 using count regression applied to a hand-collected database of 341 publicly disclosed incidents drawn from regulatory notifications, press reports, and specialised security databases. Explanatory variables include firm size (log total assets), country-level cybersecurity maturity index scores, and year fixed effects. Negative binomial regression yields a significant positive elasticity of breach frequency with respect to firm size (coefficient 0.41, standard error 0.09) and a significant negative effect of cybersecurity maturity (coefficient −0.27, standard error 0.11). The model is validated on a holdout sample of 2016 events; predictive accuracy as measured by mean absolute percentage error is 19.3%. The results are used to construct a parametric frequency prior for Bayesian LDA models where internal event histories are sparse, which is typical for smaller institutions and emerging event categories such as ransomware.

title: A Scenario-Based Impact Estimation Framework for Ransomware Attacks on Small and Medium Enterprises
abstract: Small and medium enterprises have limited actuarial loss history to parameterise LDA models for ransomware risk. This paper proposes a structured scenario elicitation and quantification framework in which expert judgements are converted into truncated lognormal severity distributions using the SHELF protocol. Six scenario categories are defined—file encryption, operational downtime, recovery costs, reputational damage, regulatory fines, and third-party liability—and combined into a total impact distribution via Monte Carlo simulation with 500 000 trials. The framework is illustrated using data from 14 scenario workshops conducted with risk managers and IT security personnel at SMEs in the Vojvodina region, with total scenario coverage of 38 firms. The resulting aggregate loss distribution has a median of EUR 47 000 and a 95th percentile of EUR 310 000. Sensitivity analysis identifies operational downtime as the dominant contributor to tail risk, accounting for 58% of 99th-percentile loss variance. The framework is designed to be implementable without specialist software.

title: Bayesian Updating of Operational Loss Severity Parameters Using External Consortium Data
abstract: Institutions with short internal loss histories face the problem of sparse data in the tail, leading to high parameter uncertainty in fitted severity distributions. This paper develops a Bayesian framework that uses external consortium loss statistics as a prior and updates it with institution-specific internal data. The prior is elicited from ORX-style summary statistics (mean, standard deviation, and selected quantiles of annual aggregate loss by event category) using moment matching onto a lognormal hyperprior for the scale parameter. The posterior is approximated by Markov Chain Monte Carlo using a Metropolis–Hastings algorithm with 200 000 draws after a 50 000 draw burn-in. The framework is applied to a dataset from a Serbian savings bank with only 87 IT security loss observations over six years. Posterior predictive 99.9th-percentile estimates are compared to MLE-based estimates; the Bayesian approach reduces the coefficient of variation of the capital estimate from 0.61 to 0.29. The paper provides R code for all computations.

title: Measuring Cyber Resilience Loss in Critical Infrastructure: An Actuarial Perspective on Event Duration and Recovery Cost
abstract: Traditional operational risk models focus on direct financial loss and neglect recovery trajectory. This paper introduces an extended loss representation that appends to each event a recovery duration (days) and an associated daily cost, modelled jointly with the primary loss via a bivariate lognormal distribution. Parameters are estimated from 203 publicly documented cyber incidents affecting energy, transport, and financial infrastructure in Europe between 2012 and 2019, sourced from ENISA incident reports. The bivariate model is fitted by maximum likelihood; the correlation between log-severity and log-duration is estimated at 0.48 (standard error 0.07). A simulation study with 1 000 000 trials generates aggregate annual resilience-loss distributions for a stylised critical infrastructure operator. The 99th-percentile aggregate cost, integrating both direct and recovery components, exceeds the direct-only estimate by 37%. The paper concludes that ignoring recovery costs leads to systematic underestimation of the economic burden of cyber incidents.
venue: Journal of Infrastructure Risk and Finance

title: Comparing the Standardised Measurement Approach and the Loss Distribution Approach for Cyber Risk Capital: A Simulation Study for Balkan Banking Sectors
abstract: The Basel Committee's 2017 decision to replace internal models with the Standardised Measurement Approach (SMA) for operational risk capital was contested by practitioners who argued it would disconnect capital from actual risk profiles. This paper uses a simulation study to compare SMA and LDA capital estimates for cyber risk specifically, using calibrated loss scenarios representative of banking sectors in Serbia, Croatia, and Slovenia. For each of 50 simulated bank profiles varying in size and cyber loss history, both methods are applied and results compared at the 99.9% confidence level. The SMA consistently overestimates capital for small banks (median ratio SMA/LDA = 1.43) and underestimates for large banks (median ratio = 0.86), consistent with its size-driven formula. The paper argues that a hybrid approach retaining internal frequency modelling within an SMA-compatible framework is feasible and quantifies the potential capital savings.
venue: Review of Eastern European Banking Studies

title: Frequency–Severity Decomposition of Phishing-Related Losses in Serbian Banks: A Zero-Inflated Compound Model
abstract: Many Serbian banks report zero phishing-related losses in a given quarter not because phishing attacks do not occur but because losses fall below internal reporting thresholds or are absorbed without formal recording. This paper addresses the resulting excess zeros in the frequency distribution by fitting a zero-inflated negative binomial model to quarterly event counts from 11 banks over 2015–2021 (308 bank–quarter observations). The probability of structural zero is modelled as a logistic function of the bank's cyber insurance indicator and its IT security expenditure per employee. The mixing probability is estimated at 0.34, meaning roughly one third of zero-count observations are structural. Severity is fitted with a lognormal distribution truncated below a EUR 1 000 reporting threshold; truncation correction raises the estimated mean severity by 18%. The paper is the first to apply zero-inflated frequency models specifically to phishing loss data from the Serbian banking sector.

title: Aggregate Loss Distribution Approximation Methods for Cyber Risk: Panjer Recursion, Fast Fourier Transform, and Monte Carlo Compared
abstract: Three numerical methods for computing aggregate loss distributions—Panjer recursion, Fast Fourier Transform inversion, and direct Monte Carlo simulation—are compared in terms of accuracy and computational cost for cyber risk applications characterised by heavy-tailed severities and overdispersed frequency distributions. The comparison is conducted on a standardised test battery of 24 frequency–severity combinations covering Poisson and negative binomial counts paired with lognormal, Pareto, and GPD severities, with tail parameters spanning from light to very heavy. Accuracy is measured relative to a high-precision reference obtained with 10 million Monte Carlo draws. FFT with discretisation step 100 EUR and grid size 2^20 achieves relative errors below 0.5% at the 99th percentile across all test cases in median CPU time of 0.8 seconds. Panjer recursion is accurate for Poisson–lognormal but fails to converge for heavy GPD tails. Monte Carlo with 100 000 draws achieves acceptable accuracy only above the 95th percentile. Practical guidance for practitioners choosing among methods is provided.
venue: Journal of Computational Risk and Finance

title: Operational Risk Disclosure and Cyber Incident Reporting Under the DORA Framework: Implications for Loss Data Quality in EU Banks
abstract: The EU Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) introduces mandatory ICT-related incident reporting for financial entities from January 2025. This paper analyses the expected impact of DORA reporting requirements on the quality and coverage of cyber loss datasets used to parameterise LDA models. Drawing on a survey of 31 risk and compliance officers at banks in Serbia, Hungary, Romania, and Croatia conducted in late 2023, the paper documents current internal classification and reporting practices and identifies misalignments with DORA's taxonomy of significant cyber incidents. Simulation experiments show that under DORA-compliant reporting, the number of recordable cyber loss events per bank is expected to increase by a median factor of 2.7 relative to current Basel AMA/SMA thresholds, substantially reducing the excess-zero problem documented in earlier literature. The paper discusses transition challenges for non-EU countries with close financial links to the EU, including Serbia, and recommends adoption of compatible reporting standards by the National Bank of Serbia.

title: Tail Risk Estimation for Cloud Service Outage Losses: A Spliced Distribution Approach with Application to Serbian Fintech Firms
abstract: Cloud service outages generate bimodal loss profiles: a large mass of short, low-cost interruptions and a thin tail of prolonged outages with severe financial consequences. This paper fits spliced distributions combining a gamma body with a generalised Pareto tail to hourly downtime cost data collected from 19 fintech firms operating in Serbia between 2021 and 2024, yielding 2 641 outage episodes. The splice point is selected by minimising the integrated squared error between the empirical CDF and the fitted spliced distribution, resulting in an optimal threshold at the 87th empirical percentile. The GPD shape parameter governing the tail is estimated at 0.38 (95% CI: 0.21–0.55), confirming heavy-tail behaviour. Annual aggregate loss distributions are constructed via compound Poisson simulation. The 99th-percentile annual outage loss for a median-sized firm is estimated at EUR 180 000, with high sensitivity to the GPD shape parameter. Results inform cloud resilience investment decisions and business interruption insurance structuring for the fintech sector.
venue: Preprint, SSRN Working Paper Series

title: Combining CRF Sequence Labelling with Spatial Context Features for Field Extraction in Inspection Certificates
abstract: Inspection certificates issued by accredited testing laboratories follow loose conventions but no single fixed template. This work treats field extraction as a sequence labelling problem over sorted text tokens, augmented with spatial features derived from each token's bounding box and its nearest neighbours. A conditional random field model is trained on 1,100 annotated inspection certificates and evaluated on a held-out set of 275 certificates from laboratories not represented in training. The feature set includes token geometry, font-size estimates from bounding-box height, relative page position, left-margin alignment, and the label of the spatially closest token. Adding spatial context features raised per-field extraction accuracy from 72.3 % to 83.7 % compared with a purely sequential baseline. Error analysis identified measurement units as the most frequently mislabelled token class. The trained model is integrated into a prototype pipeline, and processing throughput of 8.4 certificates per second is reported on a standard 2014-era server.
venue: Journal of Information Science and Engineering

title: Spatial distribution of plum orchards in Srem between 1890 and 1941 based on Austro-Hungarian cadastral records
abstract: This study reconstructs the extent and spatial pattern of plum orchard plots in the Srem district using 47 cadastral parcel sheets from the Austro-Hungarian land survey of 1896–1912, supplemented by corrective data from the first Yugoslav cadastral revision of 1928–1932. Sheets were digitised at 600 dpi and georeferenced to the ETRS89/UTM zone 34N coordinate system using tie points extracted from surviving trigonometric stations. A total of 6,840 parcels classified as 'voćnjak' or 'šljivik' were digitised and their areas computed. Results show a maximum orchard coverage of approximately 18,400 hectares in the study region around 1910, with pronounced clustering in a band 12–18 km east of the Fruška Gora ridge. Comparison with the 1932 revision indicates a net loss of roughly 2,100 hectares attributable to phylloxera-related land abandonment and conversion to arable. The dataset is made available as a shapefile archive. Methodological challenges related to coordinate drift in cadastral originals and the ambiguity of parcel classification terminology are discussed in detail.
venue: Glasnik Srpskog geografskog društva – Annals of the Serbian Geographical Society

title: Rootstock influence on graft-union anatomy and mineral element concentrations at the graft interface in apple
abstract: The graft union is a potential bottleneck for mineral element translocation between rootstock and scion, yet anatomical and chemical characterisation of this zone is rarely combined in apple studies. Graft-union segments from five rootstock–scion combinations ('Golden Delicious Reinders' on M.9, M.27, MM.111, Geneva 41, and NS-D2) were collected at two years after grafting and prepared for light microscopy and scanning electron microscopy with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (SEM-EDX) to map Ca, K, and Mg distribution. Cross-sections revealed incomplete vascular continuity in M.27 unions, with a discontinuous cambial zone in 14 of 30 samples. EDX mapping showed Ca accumulation at parenchymatous graft interface tissue in M.27 and Geneva 41, suggesting restricted apoplastic Ca flow. Correlative field data from the same trial confirmed lower fruit Ca in M.27 trees. The findings point to anatomical filtering as a mechanism partly responsible for rootstock-dependent mineral partitioning.

title: Aromatic Profile of Neoplanta White Wine Produced by Spontaneous Fermentation: A Comparison with Commercial Yeast Inoculation
abstract: This study compared the volatile composition of wines produced from the autochthonous Serbian white variety Neoplanta (Vitis vinifera L.) under spontaneous fermentation versus inoculation with two commercial Saccharomyces cerevisiae strains. Grapes were harvested from a single vineyard in the Fruška Gora subregion in two consecutive vintages (2013 and 2014). Volatile compounds were extracted by solid-phase microextraction and analysed by GC-MS; 54 individual compounds were identified and quantified across the three treatments. Spontaneously fermented wines showed significantly higher concentrations of ethyl esters associated with floral and fruity descriptors, including ethyl hexanoate (mean 312 µg/L) and ethyl octanoate (mean 287 µg/L), while commercial yeast wines exhibited elevated higher alcohol content. A trained panel of nine assessors evaluated aroma intensity, freshness, and overall quality using a structured 10-point scale. Spontaneous fermentation wines received higher median scores for complexity (7.4 vs. 6.1) across both vintages. Vintage had a significant effect on total ester content (p < 0.05), but treatment effects were consistent across years.

title: Class Imbalance in Serbian Administrative Court Decisions: A Baseline Study
abstract: Administrative court rulings in Serbia exhibit a pronounced class imbalance: approximately 78% of decisions in a collected corpus of 3,400 documents belong to a single outcome category. This paper documents the construction of that corpus, covering rulings from 2005 to 2012, and evaluates five standard classifiers—naive Bayes, logistic regression, decision tree, random forest, and SVM—under original class distributions. F1-scores for minority classes fall below 0.21 across all methods when no resampling is applied. The paper analyses the linguistic and structural features most predictive of outcome, including citation patterns and procedural section length. Results serve as a reproducible baseline for subsequent resampling and augmentation experiments. All preprocessing code and anonymised metadata are released alongside the paper. The study intentionally avoids resampling or cost-sensitive learning so that future work can quantify gains relative to a clean reference point.

title: Back-Translation as Data Augmentation for Low-Resource Legal Sentence Classification
abstract: Legal sentence classification in low-resource Slavic languages is constrained by the scarcity of annotated data and the domain specificity of vocabulary. This paper investigates back-translation—translating Serbian sentences to English and back—as an augmentation strategy for a sentence-level dataset of 1,120 annotated clauses from civil procedure documents. Three translation pipelines are tested using freely available neural machine translation models, and the round-trip fidelity of legal terminology is measured against a manually curated glossary of 340 terms. Back-translation preserves legal term identity in 74% of cases for the best pipeline. Augmented training sets are used with a fine-tuned multilingual BERT model, yielding a macro F1 of 0.68 compared to 0.59 on the original data. Error analysis reveals that procedural verbs suffer the highest mistranslation rate, suggesting domain-adaptive fine-tuning of the translation component as a future direction. The dataset and annotation guidelines are publicly available.

title: Transfer Learning from General Croatian–Serbian Legal Texts to a Specialised Serbian Labour-Law Corpus
abstract: Transformer-based language models pretrained on large general corpora require substantial fine-tuning data to adapt to specialised legal domains. This paper examines whether intermediate pretraining on a moderately sized Croatian–Serbian legal text collection (approximately 120,000 sentences from publicly accessible legislation and court decisions) improves downstream performance on a Serbian labour-law classification task with only 640 training examples. Four model variants are compared: multilingual BERT with no intermediate pretraining, the same model with intermediate pretraining on the combined corpus, and two models pretrained on each national subset separately. Intermediate pretraining on the combined corpus achieves the best macro F1 (0.72) on a held-out test set of 160 examples, surpassing the no-pretraining baseline by 0.11. Differences between the Croatian-only and Serbian-only intermediate pretraining conditions are modest, suggesting that vocabulary overlap rather than syntactic similarity drives the gain. Computational cost and practical guidance for reproducing the pipeline on limited hardware are discussed.

title: Predicting Sequences of Procedural Outcomes in Serbian Civil Litigation Using Recurrent Models
abstract: Civil litigation in Serbia often involves multiple procedural stages, and the outcome of each stage influences the distribution of subsequent outcomes. This paper frames judicial decision sequences as a temporal classification problem and evaluates three recurrent architectures—vanilla RNN, LSTM, and GRU—on a dataset of 2,180 complete case trajectories spanning first instance, appeal, and revision stages. Each stage is represented by a combination of extracted text features and structured metadata (case type, duration, court tier). The dataset is severely imbalanced at the revision stage, where case types eligible for revision constitute only 9% of trajectories. Weighted cross-entropy and focal loss are compared as training objectives. The GRU with focal loss achieves a macro F1 of 0.61 at the revision stage, compared to 0.43 for weighted cross-entropy. Sequence length and court tier are identified as the strongest non-textual predictors via ablation. Limitations related to data availability outside the University's legal informatics collaboration are discussed.

title: A Survey of Synthetic Data Generation Methods for Small Legal Datasets
abstract: The application of machine learning to legal tasks is frequently limited by small annotated corpora and ethical constraints on data sharing. This chapter surveys methods for generating synthetic legal data, covering rule-based paraphrasing, conditional language model generation, variational autoencoders, and generative adversarial networks adapted to text. For each method the chapter describes the underlying mechanism, summarises reported performance on legal benchmarks from the literature, and lists known failure modes, such as hallucinated case citations and vocabulary drift in conditional generation. Special attention is given to evaluation protocols, since standard NLP metrics such as BLEU and perplexity do not capture the legal validity of generated texts. The chapter concludes with a decision framework helping practitioners choose a generation strategy based on available corpus size, annotation type, and downstream task. Thirty-seven papers published between 2015 and 2022 are reviewed.

title: Cost-Sensitive Learning vs. Resampling: A Controlled Comparison on Four Serbian Legal Classification Tasks
abstract: Practitioners addressing class imbalance must choose between modifying the training objective and modifying the training set, but systematic comparisons on legal text data are rare. This paper applies seven resampling strategies (random oversampling, random undersampling, SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE, ADASYN, and two hybrid methods) and four cost-sensitive objectives (weighted cross-entropy, focal loss, asymmetric loss, and class-balanced softmax) to four Serbian legal classification tasks drawn from administrative, civil, criminal, and labour law subdomains. Corpus sizes range from 412 to 2,180 documents and imbalance ratios from 1:4 to 1:19. Results show no single strategy dominates across tasks; cost-sensitive objectives outperform resampling on the two smallest datasets, while hybrid resampling performs better on the two larger corpora. Statistical significance is assessed with paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests across cross-validation folds. The paper provides a reproducible experimental framework and releases all task-specific evaluation scripts.

title: Annotated corpus of Serbian electrical maintenance texts: construction methodology and baseline statistics
abstract: Reliable named entity recognition and relation extraction in the power-systems maintenance domain require annotated corpora that reflect the vocabulary and writing style of field personnel. This paper describes the construction of a 9,800-sentence corpus drawn from work orders, inspection reports, and incident summaries produced by two Serbian electricity distribution companies between 2008 and 2014. Annotation guidelines were defined to cover four entity types—equipment identifier, fault descriptor, location reference, and repair action—and two relation types: fault-equipment and action-equipment. A team of four annotators, including two electrical engineers and two computational linguists, performed the labelling using the BRAT annotation tool. Final inter-annotator kappa values ranged from 0.68 to 0.79 depending on entity type. The corpus contains 47,000 entity mentions and 31,000 labelled relation instances. Baseline results using a CRF tagger are reported, with an F1 of 0.73 for fault descriptors, which proved the most variable category. The corpus is released under a restricted-access licence pending operator approval.

title: Diverzitet arbuskularnih mikoriza u vinogradima Fruške gore: preliminarni pregled morfotipova
abstract: Istraživanje je sprovedeno u toku vegetacione sezone 2009. godine na četiri lokaliteta duž severnih padina Fruške gore, u vinogradima koji se gaje konvencionalnim metodama. Uzorkovano je ukupno 48 uzoraka rizosferne zemlje tokom cvetanja i šarka. Spore arbuskularnih mikoriza izolovane su mokrim prosejavanjem, a morfotipovi određeni klasičnom mikroskopijom. Identifikovano je 14 morfotipova koji odgovaraju rodovima Glomus, Rhizophagus i Funneliformis. Brojnost spora bila je statistički značajno viša u vinogradima na laganim ilovastim nanosima (prosečno 312 spora/100 g suvog zemljišta) nego na glinastim tlima (195 spora/100 g). Kolonizacija korena kretala se od 38 do 67 % u zavisnosti od lokaliteta i fenofaze. Rezultati ukazuju na to da tekstura zemljišta ima veći uticaj na strukturu zajednice mikorize od primenjene agrotehnike na ispitivanim lokalitetima.

title: Seasonal shifts in arbuscular mycorrhizal fungal communities in a conventionally managed Graševina vineyard on Fruška Gora
abstract: We monitored AMF community composition at monthly intervals across a full growing season (April–October 2011) in a single-cultivar Graševina vineyard near Sremski Karlovci. Root samples were collected from twelve marked vines and assessed for colonisation rate using the gridline-intersect method. Spore suspensions were prepared by wet sieving. Fungal communities were characterised by cloning and Sanger sequencing of the SSU rRNA gene (n = 312 clones). Colonisation peaked in July at 74 % and dropped to 31 % after harvest. Community composition shifted from Rhizophagus irregularis-dominated assemblages in spring toward more diverse communities including Claroideoglomus and Diversispora taxa in midsummer. Shannon diversity index ranged from 1.1 in April to 2.4 in August. Soil moisture and root sugar content were the best predictors of both colonisation intensity and community turnover in a partial RDA framework (R² = 0.61). These findings establish a seasonal baseline relevant for timing inoculation practices.

title: Uticaj prelaska sa konvencionalnog na organski sistem gajenja vinove loze na zajednice Glomeromycota u zemljištu
abstract: U cilju praćenja promena u zajednicama arbuskularnih mikoriza nakon konverzije u organsku proizvodnju, odabrana su tri para susednih parcela na Fruškoj gori kod kojih je jedna parcela prešla na organsku proizvodnju 2010. godine, dok je susedna zadržala konvencionalne prakse. Uzorkovanje je vršeno godišnje tokom trogodišnjeg perioda (2011–2013), sa po 24 uzorka po parceli svake jeseni. Fragmenti rDNA amplifikovani su prajmerima AM1/NS31 i klonisani. Analiza OTU-ova pokazala je statistički značajno povećanje bogatstva vrsta na organskim parcelama treće godine (p < 0,05), sa porastom indeksa raznovrsnosti sa 1,8 na 2,6. Zastupljenost Paraglomus vrsta bila je veća na organskim parcelama, što se poklapa sa smanjenjem dostupnog fosfora u zemljištu. Organska agrotehhika je pokazala merljiv uticaj na sastav AMF zajednice već nakon tri sezone, naročito u pogledu retkih taksona.

title: Root colonisation intensity and spore density as proxies for AMF community health in Fruška Gora organic vineyards
abstract: Arbuscular mycorrhizal colonisation intensity and spore density are widely used indicators of AMF activity but their relationship to community composition remains unclear. We sampled fifteen organic vineyards distributed across the Fruška Gora foothills in autumn 2014, collecting 180 root and soil samples. Colonisation was scored by the Trouvelot scale, and spore density was determined by wet sieving. Community composition was assessed using 454 pyrosequencing targeting the ITS2 region, yielding 41,200 quality-filtered reads assigned to 38 VT (virtual taxa). Colonisation intensity and spore density were only weakly correlated (r = 0.32). Spore density was a better predictor of community richness (R² = 0.48) than colonisation intensity (R² = 0.21). The two most abundant VTs, affiliated with Rhizophagus and Septoglomus, dominated across all sites regardless of proxy values. We conclude that neither metric alone adequately represents community diversity and recommend their combined use alongside molecular characterisation.

title: Ectomycorrhizal fungi associated with oak windbreaks bordering vineyards on Fruška Gora: potential reservoirs of inoculum
abstract: Oak hedgerows and windbreaks bordering vineyards on Fruška Gora support diverse ectomycorrhizal (ECM) fungal communities that may serve as inoculum sources for adjacent agricultural soils. We sampled ECM root tips from 28 Quercus cerris trees along windbreak strips flanking seven organic vineyards in autumn 2015 and spring 2016. Morphotyping was followed by ITS1-5.8S-ITS2 Sanger sequencing (n = 224 tips). Forty-one ECM taxa were recorded, dominated by Tomentella and Inocybe s.l. genera. Soil hyphal ingrowth bags placed at distances of 0.5, 1.5, and 3.0 m from windbreak edges showed declining ECM hyphal biomass with distance (16.4, 7.1, and 1.8 mg NLFA 16:1ω5 per g soil, respectively). AMF taxa were found at all distances. Although ECM fungi are not typical vineyard mutualists, the proximity gradient suggests that mixed-fungal inoculum pools exist within at least 1.5 m of windbreak edges.

title: Procena metoda inokulacije komercijalnim AMF preparatima u rasadnicima vinove loze u Vojvodini
abstract: Komercijalni preparati koji sadrže arbuskularne mikorize sve se više koriste u rasadničarskoj praksi, ali podaci o njihovoj efikasnosti u lokalnim uslovima Vojvodine su oskudni. U ovom istraživanju testirani su tri komercijalna preparata (označena kao P1, P2 i P3) i neinokulisana kontrola na sadnicama Cabernet Sauvignon tokom rasadničke sezone 2016–2017. Primenjena su dva načina inokulacije: zamakanje žila i primena na supstrat. Parametri rasta (visina, masa suvih žila, ukupna masa), stopa kolonizacije i morfotipi identifikovani su na kraju sezone. Preparati P1 i P3 statistički su značajno povećali masu suvih žila (za 28 % i 31 % redom), dok P2 nije pokazao statistički značajan efekat. Zamakanje žila bilo je efikasnije od primene na supstrat (p < 0,01). Kolonizacija endogenim gljivicama bila je prisutna u svim tretmanima uključujući kontrolu, što upućuje na aktivnu mikoriznu zajednicu u supstratu. Preporučuje se obavezno testiranje lokalnih sojeva pre uvođenja komercijalnih preparata.

title: High-throughput amplicon sequencing reveals distinct AMF communities under different cover crop regimes in Fruška Gora vineyards
abstract: Cover crops are increasingly adopted in Serbian viticulture as a soil management strategy, yet their effect on AMF communities is poorly documented in this region. We established a replicated field trial in 2017 across three organic vineyards on Fruška Gora, comparing four cover crop treatments (ryegrass monoculture, phacelia monoculture, mixed legume–grass, bare soil control). Soil samples collected in spring and autumn 2018 and 2019 (n = 288 total) were processed for Illumina MiSeq amplicon sequencing targeting the SSU rRNA gene. A total of 1,240,500 quality-filtered reads were assigned to 62 VTs. Mixed legume–grass cover significantly increased AMF richness relative to bare soil control (ANOVA, p < 0.01) in both seasons and both years. Rhizophagus irregularis VT113 was dominant across all treatments. Diversispora VTs were enriched under legume–grass cover. Bare soil plots showed the lowest diversity and highest within-plot beta diversity, suggesting community instability. Cover crop type explained 18 % of community variance in a permanova framework.

title: Phosphorus and nitrogen gradients shape AMF community turnover across a Fruška Gora toposequence
abstract: Nutrient gradients along hillslope toposequences may drive spatial turnover in AMF communities independently of management practices. We sampled soils from ridge, midslope, and footslope positions in nine organic vineyards distributed across a 14 km transect on Fruška Gora in 2020. Soil chemistry (pH, Olsen-P, total N, organic C) was determined at each of 81 plots. AMF communities were characterised by Illumina MiSeq SSU amplicon sequencing. Olsen-P was highest at footslope positions (mean 18.4 mg kg⁻¹) and lowest at ridges (7.1 mg kg⁻¹). Community dissimilarity (Bray-Curtis) between ridge and footslope within the same vineyard was comparable to dissimilarity between different vineyards at the same topographic position. Olsen-P and total N jointly explained 24 % of community variance (db-RDA). Archaeospora VTs were disproportionately enriched at low-P ridge positions. These results indicate that nutrient redistribution along slopes represents an underappreciated driver of intra-vineyard AMF heterogeneity.

title: Uticaj suše na kolonizaciju mikorize i razmenu fosfora u vinogradima sa smanjenim navodnjavanjem
abstract: Suša kao faktor stresa menja ravnotežu u mikoriznim simbiozama jer biljke redistribuiraju ugljenik od simbionata prema sopstvenoj odbrani. U ovom radu pratili smo 24 Prokupac čokota u organskom vinogradu tokom sušne sezone 2021. godine, koristeći sistem delimičnog sušenja rizosfere (PRD) naspram potpunog navodnjvanja i prirodnog padavinskog tretmana. Stopa kolonizacije merena je na svake tri nedelje; fosfor u ksilemu uzorkovan je punkcijom. Pregled AMF zajednice obavljen je amplikon sekvenciranjem na kraju sezone. Kolonizacija je bila najviša u tretmanu bez navodnjavanja (68 %) ali je prenos fosfora u ksilem bio statistički značajno niži nego u PRD tretmanu (p < 0,05). Shannon indeks AMF raznovrsnosti nije se statistički razlikovao između tretmana, ali se taksonomski sastav promenio u korist Claroideoglomus-dominantnih zajednica u sušnom tretmanu. Nalaze treba razmatrati u kontekstu predviđenog povećanja učestalosti suše u Panonskom regionu.

title: Mycorrhizal network connectivity estimates in organic vineyard blocks using quantitative PCR species-specific assays
abstract: Common mycelial networks (CMNs) potentially redistribute carbon and water between neighbouring grapevines but their extent under field conditions is poorly quantified. We developed qPCR assays targeting three dominant AMF VTs (affiliated with Rhizophagus irregularis, Funneliformis mosseae, and Claroideoglomus claroideum) in a single 0.4 ha organic Riesling block on Fruška Gora. In 2022 and 2023, root and hyphal ingrowth core samples were collected at 1 m intervals along three parallel transects. Assay efficiency ranged from 93 to 98 % (R² > 0.99). Gene copy numbers for all three VTs were spatially autocorrelated (Moran's I > 0.4) at scales up to 3 m, suggesting continuous hyphal networks across at least a single vine interrow. Network connectivity was higher in spring than autumn and declined following copper-based fungicide application in both years. The qPCR approach provides a resolution not achievable with community-level sequencing alone.

title: Pedološki i klimatski faktori koji određuju AMF sastav u Fruškogorskim vinogradima: metaanaliza setova podataka 2010–2023
abstract: Sistematska istraživanja sprovođena od 2010. do 2023. godine na vinogradima Fruške gore akumulirala su obimne skupove podataka o zajednicama AMF, hemiji zemljišta i klimatskim parametrima. U ovom radu sprovedena je metaanaliza ovih skupova podataka (n = 1.140 uzoraka, 31 lokalitet, 14 sezona uzorkovanja) korišćenjem jedinstvenog protocola ponovnog mapiranja svih sekvenci na referentnu MaarjAM bazu podataka. Identifikovano je ukupno 84 VT u analiziranom skupu podataka. Ograničena analiza permanova sa deset pedoloških i klimatskih kovariata pokazala je da pH, Olsen-P i letnja suma padavina zajedno objašnjavaju 31 % varijanse zajednice. VT bogatstvo značajno je opalo na parcelama sa pH < 5,8 i Olsen-P > 25 mg kg⁻¹. Detekcija retkih taksona (zastupljenost < 0,1 %) bila je konzistentna između godina samo na parcelama bez fumigacije. Rezultati ukazuju na potrebu harmonizovanog dugoročnog monitoringa AMF zajednica u vinogradima jugoistočne Evrope.

title: Seasonal dynamics of leaf mineral status in 'Braeburn' apple across a rootstock series: a two-year field study
abstract: Leaf mineral composition in apple is routinely interpreted using single-point sampling norms, yet the seasonal trajectory of mineral accumulation may differ by rootstock. This study tracked weekly leaf concentrations of N, P, K, Ca, Mg, Fe, Mn, Zn, and Cu in 'Braeburn' grafted on M.9 NAKB T337, M.26, Jork 9, and a dwarfing seedling selection from Novi Sad (NS-D2) from leaf emergence to post-harvest leaf fall over 2015 and 2016. ICP-OES data from 1,104 individual leaf samples revealed that the timing of the mid-season Ca plateau differed by up to 18 days among rootstocks, with M.26 reaching plateau earliest. Jork 9 produced significantly higher midsummer leaf Mn (62.4 vs. 38.1 mg kg⁻¹ dry weight on M.9). The data challenge the common practice of applying a single sampling date for diagnostic leaf analysis across rootstock types and provide corrected reference windows for each rootstock examined.
